concepts.name: Refined missing piece (Open): a ferromagnetic coupling between the primes (and the archimedean place) that produces the Riemann kernel Φ; the underlying equivalence RH ⇔ Φ is a Lee–Yang single-spin measure (Λ = 0 margin) is a known restatement
concepts.plain: Newman's results turn RH into a statement in statistical mechanics: RH holds exactly when the kernel Φ behaves like the spin distribution of a ferromagnet, so that every ferromagnetic system built from copies of it has its field zeros on the imaginary axis. That equivalence is a restatement, not progress. The conjectured missing piece is a mechanism: a ferromagnetic system whose sites are the primes (and the archimedean place) and whose block-spin law is Φ. Such a system would give the Lee–Yang property, and hence RH, as a structural consequence. Two pictures point the same way. Li's criterion moves the zeros onto a unit circle, and RH says exactly that they all lie on it; Lee and Yang proved that ferromagnetic coupling puts zeros on a unit circle. And only the genuine prime angles keep the window form positive, as if the primes were coupled ferromagnetically, while shuffled angles behave like a frustrated spin glass. In Li's variable the two circles are the same circle, so the first link is now a theorem about shapes, while RH stays a restatement there; the second link is an analogy. The Riemann Hypothesis is not proved.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Open. The equivalence RH ⇔ Φ Lee–Yang is a cited Restatement (Newman 1974/1976, Lieb–Sokal 1981); only a ferromagnetic construction from the primes would be new. RH is not proved. A Gram factor of the Weil form always exists under RH and is, up to rotation, indexed by the zeros, so reading couplings off the Weil form is circular; a construction must define J_pq from primes and ∞ and prove J_pq ≥ 0 independently. Link (29 Oct 2026): two unit circles. Li's map w = 1 − 1/ρ sends the critical line to |w| = 1, and under RH λₙ = Σ_ρ 2sin²(nθ_ρ/2) [Theorem]; Lee–Yang: ferromagnetic coupling puts the partition-function zeros on |z| = 1 [Theorem]. Correction (v1.6.1): the two circles can be matched. In Li's variable z = 1 − 1/s, F(z) = ξ(1/(1 − z)) satisfies F(1/z) = F(z), has positive Taylor coefficients and a₁/a₀ = λ₁ [Theorem], which is the shape of a Lee–Yang partition function in the fugacity z; RH is then the Lee–Yang property of F [Restatement]. What stays open is a ferromagnetic mechanism that produces F. Nonnegative couplings plus a pole are not enough: sign-shuffled ζ·L(χ₄) fails the window test in 20/20 cases [Numerical]. Li's λₙ ≥ 0 for all n is itself a restatement of RH. The genuine-versus-shuffled angle result reads as ferromagnetic versus frustrated, spin-glass-like coupling [Analogy]. RH is not proved.
concepts.formula: RH ⇔ Φ(u)du has the Lee–Yang property (Newman 1974, as stated by Lieb–Sokal 1981) ⇔ b₀ ≥ 0 (Newman 1976, Λ = −4b₀, since Newman's variable is t = 2u; ∫Φ(u)e^{hu}du = ¼ξ(½+h/2)) ⇔ Λ ≤ 0; with Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao) the margin is zero. Refined form: Φ(u)du = lim_N law of (Σ_{i∈B_N} c_{N,i}σ_i), with σ_i = ±1 Ising spins with ferromagnetic couplings J_ij ≥ 0 indexed by primes and ∞

lattice-factor no-go: if Φ = φ∗ψ with φ a measure on a lattice LZ (L > 0.111, e.g. L = log 2) and ψ̂ entire, then φ̂ has no zeros (finitely supported ⇒ a pure shift; otherwise Euler-factor-like, with poles but no zeros) [Theorem]

mean-field no-go: Φ = e^{λu²}ν with λ > 0 and ν Lee–Yang would give Λ ≤ −λ < 0, contradicting Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao); the dBN tilt is exactly a Curie–Weiss self-coupling [Theorem, given de Bruijn and Rodgers–Tao]
one prime as a spin-1 site: 2e^{t log²p}cos(z log p) − a/√p is the transform of a (signed, if a > 0) spin-1 measure; its one-site Lee–Yang threshold is t = Λ_p [Theorem]
excluded ferromagnets: free Euler-factor systems (J = 0 between primes) and finite mean-field couplings; open: pair-dependent couplings J_pq ≥ 0 defined from primes and ∞ alone

Li's criterion: w = 1 − 1/ρ maps the critical line Re s = ½ onto the unit circle |w| = 1; under RH each w_ρ = e^{iθ_ρ} and λₙ = Σ_ρ [1 − (1 − 1/ρ)ⁿ] = Σ_ρ 2sin²(nθ_ρ/2) ≥ 0 (zeros paired with their conjugates) [Theorem; Li 1997, Bombieri–Lagarias 1999]
Lee–Yang circle theorem: ferromagnetic pair couplings (J_ij ≥ 0) put every zero of the Ising partition function in the fugacity z = e^{−2h} on the unit circle |z| = 1 [Theorem; Lee–Yang 1952]

the window angle test read physically: the genuine Frobenius angles of Δ and 11a1 keep window positivity, while permuted, i.i.d. Sato–Tate and adversarial-but-allowed angles break it; read as ferromagnetic (aligned) versus frustrated, spin-glass-like coupling [Analogy; the test itself is Numerical]
pitfalls: Λ = −4b₀ (not −b₀) in Newman's 1976 normalisation; Ξ-type transform of Φ is ¼ξ(½+iz/2), not ξ(½+iz)

Corrected in v1.6.1: v1.6 said no map between Li's circle and the Lee–Yang circle is known. In Li's variable z = 1 − 1/s, ξ becomes a self-reciprocal series with positive coefficients, so the circles coincide; RH remains the (unproved) Lee–Yang property of that series.

concepts.name: Weil positivity criterion
concepts.plain: A quadratic form built from primes, the archimedean place and the pole. RH holds exactly when it is never negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Weil 1952: RH ⇔ W(f∗f̃*) ≥ 0 for all test f; equivalently the Hermitian form 𝒬 is positive, ⇔ a unitary Hilbert realization of the scaling flow (TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1 (iv)). TAA Lemma 161: positivity read as definite (apsidal/Kepler) stability vs gyroscopic (TAA Lemma 4) stability: the FE is a work-free J that DH also has; only a definite form excludes Krein collisions (Heuristic).
pitfalls: The zero-side check is tautological (TAA Lemma 142); only the prime side with no zeros is a test.
"Q = LP + positive" is false (TAA Lemma 8).
Definition, not source (TAA Lemma 152 §3): Weil's criterion ⇔ RH, so it cannot by itself supply the positivity.

rels.note: TAA Lemma 142: Weil form = relative intersection matrix on translates
Spec ℤ analogue of Hodge index on V₀ (TAA Lemma 91)

concepts.name: ψ(x) − x (explicit formula, deviation from the pole)
concepts.plain: Count prime powers with weight log p and subtract the pole’s prediction x; what remains is a sum over zeros. RH ⇔ the remainder is O(√x log²x).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Explicit formula ψ(x) = x − Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ − log 2π − ½log(1 − x⁻²); RH ⇔ ψ(x) − x = O(x^{½+ε}). In TAA the x term is the pole/𝕃 reference; ψ − x ≠ 0 measures the flow-relative H¹.
concepts.uncertain: The explicit-formula wording is standard (cited), not from a specific lemma section.
pitfalls: ψ(x) − x ≠ 0 is not a failure: it is the zero contribution relative to the pole reference.

concepts.name: Two Verschiebungs: pairing dual V^∨ vs positive adjoint V†
concepts.plain: The Verschiebung can be defined by a pairing (always available, blind to fake zeros) or by a positive inner product (the hard part). RH says the two definitions agree.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] For a flow generator Θ on a real space with a nondegenerate pairing B for which Θ is a derivation into a twist-1 top class (B(Θx,y)+B(x,Θy) = B(x,y), Deninger's cup product), the B-dual is Θ^∨ = 1 − Θ (ρ ↦ 1−ρ: the functional equation, ghost-blind; DH has it). For a positive form g(x,y) = B(x,∗y) the g-adjoint is Θ† = ∗⁻¹ Θ^∨ ∗. Hence Θ† = Θ^∨ ⇔ [∗,Θ] = 0, and then Θ = ½ + A with A skew (Deninger ICM98 §3, p.169, opened). Group form: for F with ω(Fx,Fy) = q·ω(x,y), V := F^∨ = qF⁻¹ always; F† = qF⁻¹ ⇔ F/√q ∈ Sp ∩ O = U(n). Polar F = UP: F^∨ = P⁻¹U⁻¹, F† = PU⁻¹, gap ‖F^∨ − F†‖ = ‖P − P⁻¹‖ (= 2 sinh r in 2D). Lie algebra: Θ^∨ − Θ† = −2S, S = symmetric (squeeze) part of Θ − ½. TAA Lemma 161: in 2D the gap form is the radial speed r·v; apsides are its zeros; circle ⇔ dual = adjoint; e_K = tanh d_H(i, τ).
numbers: polar identities: 60 random Sp(2n), n ≤ 3, residuals ≤ 3.2e−10
pitfalls: RH ⇒ dual = adjoint needs Θ normal for g (semisimple + orthogonal eigenlines); the converse needs nothing.
Building the positive g from the Euler product is open (= MP4).

concepts.name: Frobenius-graph lattice on E×E (relative counts = intersections with Δ)
concepts.plain: On the square of an elliptic curve, the graph of Frobenius meets the diagonal in the point count; the sign pattern of these intersections is exactly the Riemann hypothesis for the curve.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: e₁, e₂, Δ, Γ_{F^n} on E×E/F_q: Γ_n·e₁ = 1, Γ_n·e₂ = q^n, Δ·Γ_n = N_n, Γ_m·Γ_n = q^{min}N_{|m−n|}; complement Gram −[[2,a],[a,2q]] = −2 deg(m+nF); det = −(4q − a²); Hodge index ⇔ signature (1,3) ⇔ Hasse. NUM 11a1, 15 primes: (1,3,0), with Γ₂ (1,3,1); fake a > 2√p → (2,2). TAA Lemma 152 Prop 4.1 (NUM, zeta-free): 11a1, brute-force counts over F_{p^k} (p^k ≤ 729; p = 2,3,5,7,13,17,19) satisfy Γ_m·Γ_n = q^m N_{n−m} (incl. m = n, N₀ = 2 − 2g); Gram of ⟨e₁,e₂,Γ₀..Γ_K⟩ rank 4, inertia (1,3) exactly; fakes (5,5),(7,6),(13,8),(2,3) give (2,2). rels.note: Rosati form = intersection form on the Frobenius plane

concepts.name: Kähler triple (ω, J, g) = polarization; elliptic ⇔ positive form preserved
concepts.plain: A positive form on phase space needs a choice of complex structure on top of the symplectic pairing; over finite fields the polarization provides it, for ζ it is missing.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] ω antisymmetric (pairing side; Sp preserves it; ω-dual of symplectic F is F⁻¹). Positivity is extra data: compatible J, g = ω(·,J·) > 0 (Riemann form E with E(ix,x) > 0 for abelian varieties: polarization ⇒ Rosati positive). sp = u(n) ⊕ {squeezes}: rotations commute with J, squeezes anticommute. SL₂: for M ≠ ±1 the invariant symmetric forms form a line, spanned by a definite / indefinite / degenerate form as |tr M| <, >, = 2. 𝔽_q: M = Frobenius/√q on ℤ[π] preserves the norm form m² + amn + qn², positive ⇔ a² < 4q ⇔ TAA Lemma 150 lattice U ⊕ (−2N) has signature (1,3); fakes (2,2), det −(4q − a²) (q = 101: a = −3, 0, 12, 20 → (1,3); 21, 25, 40 → (2,2)). Hyperbolic Γ_q = 2 arccosh(|a|/2√q)/log q. TAA Lemma 161: S_t = |x − τp|² with τ = F/√q: the preserved complex structure; eccentricity measures d_H(i, τ) (e_K = tanh d).
pitfalls: The J preserved by an elliptic M is forced by M (unique up to scale); the arithmetic content is that the polarization supplies the same g for all Frobenius powers.

concepts.name: Lagarias/Hinkkanen criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the log-derivative of ξ has positive real part to the right of the line.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Lagarias 1999 (1.5), credited to Hinkkanen: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 on Re s > ½ (TAA Lemmas 17, 146).

concepts.name: Connes trace formula
aliases: Connes cokernel: positive space sees only critical zeros; RH ⇔ global trace formula
concepts.plain: Connes’ trace formula on the adele class space: zeros appear as an absorption spectrum, and the global trace formula holding is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Connes 1999 (read at source, TAA Lemma 30/TAA Lemma 71): global trace formula ≡ RH; Thm 1 sees only critical zeros (δ > 1); Thm 5 char p; zeros = absorption spectrum (TAA Lemma 71). TAA Lemma 82: cutoff, non-critical zeros as resonances. TAA Lemma 118: Connes reduces RH for Hecke L to the trace formula ⇒ Weil positivity; absorption spectrum ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 138 R2: Hilbert–Pólya positivity is circular if the inner product is Weil’s form. TAA Lemma 151: Connes's cokernel L²(C_k)/Im E (absorption spectrum) is the MP1 candidate; E carries |g|^{½} (canonical real half twist); C ⊕ C(1) boundary = H⁰/H². Missing on both sides: MP4. TAA Lemma 153 (E, corrected per H): Selecta Math. (N.S.) 5 (1999) 29–106, doi 10.1007/s000290050042 (Crossref; abstract re-read). Connes cokernel: the positive (Hilbert) space sees only the critical zeros — spectral realization of the critical zeros as an absorption spectrum (δ > 1 version, Thm 1 as read at source in TAA Lemma 30/TAA Lemma 71), noncritical zeros only as resonances; semi-local trace formula proved; RH ⇔ validity of the global trace formula (⇔ Weil positivity). A quotient of a Hilbert space is automatically positive, so 'positivity of the inherited form ⇔ RH' was wrong (TAA Lemma 153, correction 18): RH ⇔ nothing is missing from the positive space. The two quotients: (1) by ℚ^× acting on ideles → C_ℚ = 𝔸^×/ℚ^× (modular analogue Γ∖ℍ); (2) the cokernel of the summation map E (modular analogue: the constant term at the cusp; cusp forms = its kernel). CM points are not the quotient.

rels.note: RH ⇔ nothing missing from the positive space

concepts.name: Kähler identities → Serre/Deninger–Singhof unitarity → MP4 in degree 1 ⇔ the flow preserves a leafwise Hodge splitting
concepts.plain: Kähler identities make the Hodge star expressible through the complex structure and the Kähler class; then any flow that respects both is a rotation up to scale, which is RH. For Deninger's space positivity is free; the missing piece is a complex structure the flow respects.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C,N] Kähler identities [Λ,∂̄] = −i∂*, [Λ,∂] = i∂̄*, [L,Δ] = 0 (Wikipedia/Huybrechts §3.1; sign verified symbolically on ℂ² with ω = (i/2)Σdz∧dz̄: residual 0, opposite sign fails). sl₂ (L,Λ,Π) ⇒ hard Lefschetz, Hodge–Riemann on primitive classes. [C] Deninger–Singhof 2002 (opened): Kähler–Riemann foliations: H̄ⁿ_F = ⊕H^{pq} (depends only on J, Prop 4.2), hard Lefschetz (4.3), polarization (4.4), Prop 4.6 (Serre 1960 analogue): f leafwise holomorphic, f*[ω_F] = q[ω_F] ⇒ f* = q^{n/2}·unitary. [T] infinitesimal: Θ derivation, Θ[ω] = α[ω], [Θ,J] = 0 ⇒ Θ = nα/2 + skew on H̄ⁿ; finite model N: 60 trials, commuting part Re = ½ to 6e−16, generic sp part off-line in 88%. [T] Surface leaves (Deninger's 3-dim picture): ∗ = −J on 1-forms (∗dz = −i dz), positivity tr(h∪∗h) is automatic for every Riemannian foliation (Den05 (15)); so MP4 in degree 1 ⇔ [J,Θ] = 0 on H̄¹ (Restatement). Den05: 'one will need the Kähler identities on cohomology' (for (11)). El Kacimi 1990 (opened): basic (transverse) Hodge/Lefschetz — the other flavour, not Deninger's leafwise H̄.
numbers: Kähler identity residual 0 (16 forms, ℂ²); opposite sign 14.55
finite Serre model: Re − ½ ≤ 5.6e−16 when [J,Θ] = 0
pitfalls: El Kacimi treats basic (transverse) cohomology; Deninger needs leafwise reduced cohomology (Deninger–Singhof).
Leafwise holomorphic is a pointwise (forms) condition; Deninger doubts it for number fields. The cohomological condition [J,Θ] = 0 suffices but is equally open.

concepts.name: Primitive part V₀ = U^⊥
concepts.plain: What is left after removing the reference plane; on it the form should be negative (curves: theorem; ℚ: RH).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D° = D − d₁f₂ − d₂f₁; (D°)² = −Tr_{H¹}(α_Dα_D†) (TAA Lemma 133). Over ℚ V₀ = U^⊥ and D·D ≤ 0 on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91). TAA Lemma 167: Weil-form analogue numerically: kerP (pole/cusp functionals) removes exactly ζ's one pole direction; DH index on kerP = full index (primitive failure).

concepts.name: Definite cup square / Krein one-liner
concepts.plain: Positivity is put in by a definite Hermitian square: a flow that scales it forces every eigenvalue onto the line, and only null vectors (ghosts) can escape.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: If ⟨φᵗx, φᵗy⟩ = eᵗ⟨x,y⟩ for a Hermitian form, an eigenvector with eigenvalue e^{tρ} has Re ρ = ½ or is null; ρ pairs only with 1 − ρ̄ (Krein-neutral (1,1) block); definite ⇒ all on the line (TAA Lemma 152 Prop 2.1; NUM 2.3e−16). A bilinear cup pairing only pairs ρ with 1 − ρ (= functional equation, ghost-blind; Cor 2.2): Hermitian needs conjugation + Weil operator/polarization. Over F_q: the definite form is the Rosati trace form on End⁰(J)⊗ℝ (ππ′ = q ⇒ |σ(π)|² = q), equivalently Hodge index on NS(C×C) — not a Hermitian form on H¹_ét (TAA Lemma 152, correction 1). For ζ: MP4 (TAA Lemma 151), the only positivity input. On E×E the projection D_n = Γ_n − qⁿe₁ − e₂ gives D_m·D_n = −Σ αᵢⁿ βᵢᵐ, β = q/α: Hermitian iff |α| = √q (TAA Lemma 152 Prop 4.3).
pitfalls: Over F_q there is no positive Hermitian form on H¹_ét (TAA Lemma 152, correction 1).
A bilinear (cup) pairing gives only the FE (TAA Lemma 152, correction 2).

concepts.name: Missing: Deninger's conjectured cohomology for Spec ℤ, stated as axioms MP0–MP4 (no coined name)
concepts.plain: For ℚ both cohomologies we can compute vanish (étale H¹ = 0, Arakelov Pic⁰ = a point), yet ψ(x) − x ≠ 0. The zeros need a cohomology relative to the scaling flow.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Construct the middle term of Tate's split at |x| = 1 as an H¹ for Spec ℤ carrying (a) a Frobenius-type flow whose spectrum is the zeros (MP1–MP2; needs the Euler product, absent for DH) and (b) a cup product H¹ × H¹ → H² ≅ ℝ(−1) (MP3; absent for DH), and prove the cup square definite on the primitive part (MP4 = Hodge index/Rosati sign; the only positivity input). MP0: H⁰/H² = Tate boundary terms f(0), f̂(0) (DH: none). Deninger's axioms, TAA refinements MP0/MP4 (TAA Lemma 151 Conj 4.1). TAA Lemma 153: Connes's cokernel (TAA Lemma 153, correction 18) — its Hilbert space is automatically positive and sees only critical zeros; RH ⇔ nothing missing ⇔ global trace formula. Recorded as a precision of MP4, no new missing piece (MPU153). TAA Lemma 157 sharpening of MP4: Deninger's conjectured cohomology carries a positive g = tr(· ∪ ∗·) with ∗ commuting with Θ, i.e. the Poincaré dual of the flow equals its Hilbert adjoint (Θ^∨ = Θ†); equivalently the arithmetic J (from the Euler product) makes the flow a rotation. Den98 §3 p.169 (opened) gives ⇒ RH. TAA Lemma 158: degree-1 form of MP4 for surface leaves: positivity tr(h∪∗h) is automatic (Den05 (15)); ∗ = −J on H̄¹; MP4 ⇔ the flow preserves a leafwise Hodge splitting ([J,Θ] = 0), cf. Deninger–Singhof Prop 4.6. Missing Piece v5 (headline adopted by J. W. McGreevy): MP4 is headed by the one-line Conjecture "the Euler product induces the Hodge splitting of the square, with its sign" (entry: Euler product induces the Hodge splitting), with the v4 sharp form underneath: a complex structure J on H¹ with (1) [J,Θ] = 0, (2) g = ω(·,J·) positive definite on the primitive part (a Θ-invariant fundamental decomposition of the Krein form; σ: ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄ fixes every eigenvalue), (3) the positivity derived, not verified, from a structural input built from the whole Euler product that is prime-crossing and uses all primes in each window at once (R8′). Requirements R1–R8′ unchanged; no-go list 32 items. Headline reworded geometrically: "the Euler product, taken as geometry (the Frobenius correspondence: graph classes on the square with an ample class), not as counting data, induces the Hodge splitting of the square, with its sign".
concepts.formula: N_n − (1 + qⁿ) = −Tr(Fⁿ | H¹) ↔ ψ(x) − x = −Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ + …
concepts.proved: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1 ⇒ H¹ét = 0 (TAA Lemma 140); curve row: N_n − (qⁿ + 1) = −Tr(Fⁿ | H¹) with relative Gram NSD (TAA Lemma 141 §1); Tr ↔ −(ψ − x) up to the s = 0 term and ARCH (TAA Lemma 142 corrections).
concepts.tests: Must carry a positive structure (Ax2), not only the trace formula: the explicit formula alone is ghost-blind in data (TAA Lemma 143: ghost defect ≤ 1.9e−5, 0.08× noise).

concepts.name: Missing: arithmetic Castelnuovo object (positive involution on a space where the Weil distribution is a |·|²)
concepts.plain: A space with an infinite H¹, a positive involution † and a flow u_t with u_t u_t† = eᵗ, on which the explicit-formula (Weil) distribution becomes a squared norm, with that positivity proved without using the zeros.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Arithmetic Castelnuovo object = (C1) infinite H¹, (C2) positive involution, (C3) u_t u_t† = eᵗ, (C4) positivity proved without zeros (TAA Lemma 136); equivalently a positive involution plus a Frobenius-type flow with positivity proved without zeros (TAA Lemma 136 synthesis). Hilbert–Pólya form: a positive V ≅ H¹ (TAA Lemma 115); “all that is missing is an appropriate inner product” (Lax–Phillips, TAA Lemma 105/TAA Lemma 141).
concepts.proved: Over F_q: Ax2 ∧ Ax3 ⇔ |α| = √q (TAA Lemma 137, theorem). Over ℚ: isometry of the flow is unconditional (TAA Lemma 1); the Čech 2-class supplies C2–C3 structure but not the sign (TAA Lemma 138); Ax2 alone holds for fakes, Ax3 alone is tautological (TAA Lemma 137).
concepts.tests: Must separate ghosts: Ax2 and Ax3 jointly, never one alone (TAA Lemma 137). Must not define the inner product by Weil’s form (circular, TAA Lemma 138 R2; TAA Lemma 106).

concepts.name: Missing: H¹ on the square of the scaling site (Connes–Consani s(f,f) ≤ 0)
concepts.plain: A first cohomology on the square of Connes–Consani’s scaling site; with it, an RR theorem would give D(f)•D(f) ≤ 0, which is RH.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: CC18: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0, s(f,f) = D•D with D = ∫fΨ_λ; five steps, only step 1 (complex lift) built; H¹ on the square of the scaling site, and hence RR there, is open (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2). ½D(f)•D(f) = ½s(f,f) is the Weil form (TAA Lemma 142).
concepts.proved: No RR for C_ℚ × C_ℚ exists (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2). The square exists as a site with Ψ_λ (TAA Lemma 30) but carries no H¹, RR or Hodge index (TAA Lemma 65).
concepts.tests: All H⁰-side objects built from ℤ ⊂ 𝔸_ℚ are ghost-blind; the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45, actual DH from 4.70) (TAA Lemma 142, TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: a Néron–Severi strictly larger than U containing the Frobenius classes Ψ_λ
concepts.plain: An intersection theory on the square in which the Connes–Consani correspondences Ψ_λ are genuine classes outside the pole plane U, with enough sections that their growth sees s(f,f).
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Need NS ⊋ U with Ψ_λ, and #H⁰(±nD(f)) ≥ 2^{n² s(f,f)/2} (TAA Lemma 147). Decisive missing objects: H¹ on the square, an intersection theory putting Ψ_λ into an NS larger than U, and quadratic RR (TAA Lemma 147 (iv)).
concepts.proved: Laurent piece of HZ ∧_𝕊 HZ: box count 2n² + 4n exact, but the quadratic coefficient 2αβ is the U-form ⇒ vacuous on degree-0 D(f) (TAA Lemma 147 Thm vac).
concepts.tests: Quadratic growth must come from V₀ = U^⊥, not from U (Thm vac). Ghost-sensitive side is s(f,f), which must be negative for ζ and fail for DH (TAA Lemma 142, TAA Lemma 147).
pitfalls: TAA Lemma 150 Prop 2.3: classes at log n (n ≤ 90, disjoint hats) are ghost-blind — ζ, DH and inserted ghosts all give λ_max < 0; NS ⊋ U must use continuous translates or all ratios λ ∈ ℚ₊ (PSI-2).

concepts.name: Missing: surface + ample class + Riemann–Roch for Spec ℤ (D8)
concepts.plain: The top substantive direction: a surface S over Spec ℤ with an ample class and a Riemann–Roch whose χ(nD) is quadratic, so that Hodge index follows as it does for curves.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: D8: surface + ample + RR for Spec ℤ — find S with χ(nD) quadratic and a Hodge index; obstacle: the collapse ℤ ⊗ ℤ = ℤ; sign = Weil form (TAA Lemma 140, TAA Lemma 141). Acceptance test (TAA Lemma 141): reconstruct the relative space and its form from independent constraints — (a) the hyperbolic plane U = ⟨𝟙, 𝕃⟩, (b) the scaling flow acting on it as diag(1, eᵗ), (c) ampleness at ∞, (d) RR/GRR with quadratic growth — then prove negativity on U^⊥. Any proof that uses the zeros, or defines the form by its negativity, fails. TAA Lemma 152: phrased as a 'degree' — a count (≥ 0) on arithmetic correspondences whose polarization is Weil's form; in Cayley–Klein terms the absolute of the arithmetic pairing must be imaginary (= MP4). TAA Lemma 158: the collapse as an object: requirements R1–R5 on a defect invariant (missing_square_spec_z); collapse alone is ghost-blind.
concepts.proved: Over F_q: surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (Segre 1937, Grothendieck 1958) (TAA Lemma 140). Spec ℤ ×_ℤ Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ (TAA Lemma 65). Arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K) satisfy V1–V3, but the relative part is Néron–Tate, not ζ (TAA Lemma 145).
concepts.tests: Must pass the tautology test (no zeros, no definition by negativity, TAA Lemma 141) and the must-fail-for-DH test (TAA Lemma 147).

concepts.name: Missing: a BRST-type complex Q with H(Q) = U^⊥ positive (PM-3)
concepts.plain: A nilpotent operator on the test functions whose cohomology is exactly the relative space U^⊥, so that “remove the pole plane, then the rest is positive” becomes a cohomology statement, as in Gupta–Bleuler/BRST.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: PM-3: Gupta–Bleuler/BRST complex Q on TAA Lemma 142’s test functions with H(Q) = U^⊥ (TAA Lemma 146). Thm gb (linear algebra, proved): for V = U ⊕ U^⊥, U = ⟨F₁, F₂⟩, F_i² = 0, F₁F₂ = 1, the quotient F₁^⊥/⟨F₁⟩ is isometric to U^⊥; a nilpotent Q with cohomology U^⊥ would package it as a flow-relative cohomology (Open).
concepts.proved: TAA Lemma 115: BRST structure exact over F_q and ℚ; “no ghosts” ⇔ RH (restatement); missing positive V ≅ H¹ (Hilbert–Pólya). TAA Lemma 146: the BRST quartet decouples, but a ghost quartet survives.
concepts.tests: A ghost quartet is exactly a quartet that fails to decouple (TAA Lemma 146); the complex must not decouple it. Positivity of the quotient is an input in QED and is RH for ζ.

concepts.name: Missing: passivity of ξ′/ξ from a zero-free mechanism (Lagarias margin)
concepts.plain: RH is equivalent to ξ′/ξ being a passive (positive-real) response to the right of the line. What is missing is a proof of a passivity margin that uses only primes, the pole and the archimedean place.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Lagarias (1.5), attributed to Hinkkanen: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 on Re s > ½ (TAA Lemma 146, opened). PM-1: a Lagarias margin h(σ) for ξ vs DH/ghost — a provable, ghost-sensitive passivity margin? (TAA Lemma 146).
concepts.formula: RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 for Re s > ½
concepts.proved: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²): each zero an absorption line, an off-line zero a gain line (TAA Lemma 146). Passivity ⇒ causality, not conversely (TAA Lemma 146 corrections). Free positivity (Λ(n) ≥ 0, KMS, Bagchi recurrence) is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 136, TAA Lemma 118).
concepts.tests: Grid σ ∈ [.505, 1.1], t ∈ [80, 92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; ghost −66.97, 1.94% (TAA Lemma 146). The margin must stay positive for ξ and go negative for both.

concepts.name: Missing: quadratic Riemann–Roch + “ampleness ⇒ effectivity” on the square
concepts.plain: A Riemann–Roch on Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ whose Euler characteristic is quadratic in D, together with the step “ample ⇒ has sections ⇒ effective”. This is exactly the part of the curve proof that Spec ℤ lacks.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Classical chain: S1 quadratic RR, S2 Serre duality, S3 h¹ ≥ 0 / Minkowski, S4 sections ⇒ effective, S5 ample·effective > 0. Missing Spec ℤ step = quadratic S1 + S4 (“ampleness ⇒ effectivity” via a 2-dim h⁰) (TAA Lemma 145 V3, verdict VF-E). Parity: quadratic χ is even in D, linear χ odd ⇒ fixed rank proves only degree c(D) = 0, never sees D².
concepts.uncertain: The displayed “needed shape” is the classical surface RR, quoted as the target form.
concepts.proved: Every proved Connes–Consani RR is 1-dimensional, χ = deg + const (TAA Lemma 147); fixed-rank products are linear, h⁰/n = 2.000 at n = 400 (TAA Lemma 145 Thm linear); on ℙ¹_ℤ χ̂ is quadratic and realizes the U-form (TAA Lemma 145). Hodge index also needs S2, S3, S5 (TAA Lemma 145 corrections).
concepts.tests: Must fail for Davenport–Heilbronn, hence must use the Euler product (TAA Lemma 147, necessary condition). Must see D², i.e. be quadratic. V3 on the square ⇔ Weil ⇔ RH, so it must be proved, not assumed (TAA Lemma 145).

concepts.name: Missing: RR/GRR on an arithmetic Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ producing the sign (RG-5, “the missing row”)
concepts.plain: In the relative Gram dictionary every entry has an analogue except the one that proves the sign: a Riemann–Roch or Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch theorem on an arithmetic square.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: RG-5: RR/GRR on an arithmetic “Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ” producing the sign — the missing row of the TAA Lemma 142 dictionary (TAA Lemma 142). D9: arithmetic GRR test on the scaling-site square (TAA Lemma 140/TAA Lemma 141 candidate).
concepts.proved: TAA Lemma 142 Thm 1.1: Weil Gram on translates is Toeplitz (flow), POLE = rank-2 signature (1,1) = the curve U-part exactly; every entry zero-free (flow, U/Tate poles, Γ_ℝ, Λ(n)); G_rel ≤ 0 on all spans ⇔ RH (Weil, restatement). Unconditional sign only on windows ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) and arch-only a* (TAA Lemma 127), both ghost-blind.
concepts.tests: Ghost ⇒ n₊(G_rel) = 2 (TAA Lemma 142); DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45. The theorem must produce G_rel ≤ 0 for ζ on every span without using zeros.

concepts.name: Missing: an inequality consequence of automorphy (SC-E / HS-1)
concepts.plain: Automorphy (invariance under the full modular group) decides where the zeros are but does not derive it; what is missing is an inequality that automorphy forces on δ_ρ.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: SC-E (structural P: Hecke/Euler product) = Selberg-class RH, the open non-circular version of trapped-set rigidity (TAA Lemma 143); sharpened to “an inequality consequence of automorphy” (→ Weil positivity, TAA Lemma 142) (TAA Lemma 144). HS-1: an automorphy-defect functional 𝒟(Λ_X) ≥ 0 with 𝒟 = 0 ⇔ Λ_X = ξ; it needs an inequality that the defect forces on δ_ρ, which we do not have (TAA Lemma 144).
concepts.proved: Thm 3.3 (TAA Lemma 144): automorphy picks a = 1/ξ(2s), c = φ uniquely, exact defect formula; Hecke alone puts no constraint on φ (Prop 3.2). SC-A ⇔ RH (restatement); SC-B false (DH); SC-C false (all cofinite Γ); HS-B (Hecke + unitarity ⇒ δ = 0) false (fakes).
concepts.tests: Fakes pass Hecke/FE/Δ/unitarity to 1e−25 but fail S-invariance: DH by 1.4–3.2%, the degree-0 ghost by 4.5e−6–1.6e−4 (TAA Lemma 144). The inequality must be violated by both.

concepts.name: Passivity (positive real part)
concepts.plain: A system that never produces energy; its impedance has non-negative real part. For ξ′/ξ this is Lagarias’ criterion.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Passivity ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ > 0 on Re s > ½ ⇔ RH (Lagarias/Hinkkanen). Passivity ⇒ causality (TAA Lemma 146, correction 3). TAA Lemma 159: the working 'second law': each zero contributes a Lorentzian of sign sgn(σ−β), ghosts are gain for ½ < σ < β; [N] ζ min 0.0467 vs DH −15.08 on t ∈ [80,120]; on the line ξ′/ξ = −iΞ′/Ξ is purely reactive and Foster monotonicity = Laguerre inequality (⇐ RH, ⇏ RH).
concepts.formula: Re ξ′/ξ(s) > 0 for Re s > ½
pitfalls: Not independent of causality.

concepts.name: Relative Gram matrix G_rel
concepts.plain: Take a test function, translate it, and form the matrix of pairings after removing the pole plane. RH ⇔ this matrix is positive (semi)definite for all choices.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 149: prime side to x = e^16, exact u-space ARCH; hats h = 0.025, all 316 spans 0.25–16: ζ λ_max(G_rel) < 0 everywhere (−2.31e−6, −5.13e−9, −4.90e−11, −2.78e−11, −6.45e−12 at L = 1, 4, 8, 12, 16), n₊(C) = 1; roundoff floor 5e−15 (not a certificate).
pitfalls: Using the zero side to "check" it is tautological.
Negative sign is predicted both by RH and by any ghost with δ below the detection threshold (δ ≈ 0.01 at γ 85.7 by L = 16).

rels.note: [tested-by] DH prime side positive from L = 3.85 (TAA Lemma 149)

concepts.name: Verschiebung as the positive adjoint of Frobenius (F† = V)
concepts.plain: Frobenius has a partner map going the other way, Verschiebung, with F·V = q; the true statement behind RH is that V is the mirror image (adjoint) of F for a positive inner product, and J. W. McGreevy’s animation runs this pairing continuously.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] On an elliptic curve over F_q: FV = VF = q and F + V = a (trace); deg(m − nF) = (m − nF)(m − nV) = m² − a·mn + q·n² (the norm conic); a² < 4q ⇒ ellipse and V = F̄ (complex conjugate eigenvalues), so |α|² = αᾱ = FV = q: Hasse; a² = 4q double line; a² > 4q hyperbola, F, V two different real numbers (a fake). Dieudonné modules W(k){F,V}/(FV − p); Rosati: π∘π† = q ⇒ π† = qπ⁻¹ = V (TAA Lemma 115 §6.1, Milne AV Lemma 1.2 as cited there). [R] The ghost-sensitive statement is V = F† for a POSITIVE form (Rosati trace form): ⟨Fx,Fy⟩ = q⟨x,y⟩ (Krein one-liner, definite_cup_square); for a finite model RH ⇔ there is a positive involution with F† = V (TAA Lemma 115 §6.3, via TAA Lemma 113 Thm 2.1). Flow form: adjoint = inverse up to eᵗ ⇔ Re ρ = ½. On the Eisenstein constant term Ve = Fr̄ on y^s iff Re s = ½ (TAA Lemma 115; a Ramanujan statement for E(·,s), not RH for ζ). [Ghost-blind] FV = q alone is pure algebra: any fake with char. poly x² − ax + q has V = a − F with FV = q (TAA Lemma 113 Thm 5.1 via TAA Lemma 115). TAA Lemma 117 §4: with the pairing ρ ↔ 1 − ρ̄, Ve = Fr† always; an on-line zero is self-paired (definite square), an off-line pair spans a hyperbolic plane where p^{−½}Fr is a boost of rapidity δ log p. TAA Lemma 121: Π_p′ (transpose of Frobenius) is Verschiebung, Π_pΠ_p′ = p; mod p, Φ_p = 0 is graph of j ↦ j^p ∪ its transpose (Kronecker congruence). [A] J. W. McGreevy’s animation as the dynamic F ↔ V sweep: the half turn swaps F and V; running a through a² < 4q, = 4q, > 4q is lobe → wedge → hyperbola. TAA Lemma 157: V^∨ (pairing dual, = qF⁻¹, ghost-blind) vs V† (positive adjoint); F† = J⁻¹F^∨J; agree ⇔ F/√q ∈ U(n); per-eigenline gap |q/α − ᾱ| (exponent form Γ = |1−2β|).
concepts.formula: FV = VF = q; deg(m − nF) = (m − nF)(m − nV); F† = V ⇔ |α| = √q
numbers: TAA Lemma 115: s = ½ + 7.3i, p = 3: Fr = −0.28601 + 1.70827i, Ve = conj(Fr), Fr·Ve = 3
TAA Lemma 115: T_pE = (p^{s−½} + p^{½−s})E checked to 1e−30
concepts.uncertain: No new lemma build: assembled from TAA Lemma 115/TAA Lemma 117/TAA Lemma 121/TAA Lemma 152/TAA Lemma 153; Milne AV Lemma 1.2 as cited in TAA Lemma 115.
pitfalls: FV = q is ghost-blind (fakes have it); only “V is the adjoint for a POSITIVE form” is ghost-sensitive.
TAA Lemma 115 TAA Lemma 115, correction 12: “Verschiebung drives the birth” holds only as a parameter flow (V_N: y ↦ Ny is not Γ-invariant), not as a symmetry of the zero set.
TAA Lemma 115: on the Eisenstein side “Ve = Fr†” restates Ramanujan/temperedness for E(·,s), not RH for ζ.
The animation reading is an Analogy; its code is lost and per-frame autoscaling could fake a flip (TAA Lemma 152, correction 11).

rels.note: finite model: RH ⇔ positive involution with F† = V (TAA Lemma 115 §6.3); for ζ a Restatement of MP4
off-line pair: p^{−½}Fr is a boost (TAA Lemma 117)
fakes keep FV = q but V ≠ F†

concepts.name: Cayley–Klein absolute: definite ⇔ no real null rays (rotations vs boosts)
concepts.plain: A geometry is definite exactly when its absolute (the conic at infinity) has no real points; real points give boosts and null directions, i.e. ghosts.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Every projective metric = cross-ratio with a fixed conic, the absolute (Cayley 1859, Klein 1871). Imaginary absolute ⇔ definite form ⇔ rotations, eigenvalues e^{±iθ} on the unit circle, no real null vectors. Real absolute (null rays at ±45°) ⇔ indefinite ⇔ boosts, eigenvalues e^{±η}, rapidity η = ½ log CR(ℓ₁,ℓ₂; N₊,N₋) (TAA Lemma 152 NUM 4.4e−16), real null vectors = Krein-neutral pairs = ghosts. Gap restated: is the absolute of the arithmetic pairing imaginary? Over F_q yes (Hodge index); for ζ this is MP4 ⇔ RH. J. W. McGreevy's withdrawn 45° null rays are the picture of the failure mode.
pitfalls: Cayley 1859 and Klein 1871: bibliographic data verified via Crossref only.
Restatement: it re-expresses Weil positivity; it supplies no positivity.

rels.note: imaginary absolute of the arithmetic pairing = MP4 ⇔ RH (Weil)
RH = exclude boosts (TAA Lemma 42/TAA Lemma 58/TAA Lemma 98)

concepts.name: Riemann–Roch strategy: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0
concepts.plain: Connes–Consani’s plan: build divisors D(f) on the square from test functions; RH is equivalent to their self-intersection being ≤ 0, and an RR theorem there would prove it.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: CC18: RH ⇔ s(f,f) ≤ 0 (12), s(f,f) = D•D with D = ∫fΨ_λ (14); five steps, only step 1 (complex lift) built; H¹ on the square open. ½D(f)•D(f) = ½s(f,f) is the Weil form (TAA Lemma 147 §4, TAA Lemma 142).
pitfalls: The H⁰ side is ghost-blind; only the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (TAA Lemma 147 §4).

concepts.name: Zero-side real form = RH: under MP0–MP3 a finite Θ-stable σ-stable block with m off-line orbits has Krein isometry group U(n₀+m, m); the normalized flow is in a compact group on every block ⇔ RH; DH's Weil Gram reads O(n−q, q), q up to 24 (h =.025, L = 15.95), ζ compact on all TAA Lemma 149 windows
aliases: which real form is ζ's G×G (B1)
concepts.plain: On the side of the zeros, asking whether ζ's hidden symmetry is the compact (rotation) form is the same as asking whether all zeros are on the line. DH visibly fails it; ζ passes every tested window, but that is a readout, not a proof.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T given MP0–MP3] Krein lemma ⇒ on-line lines h-definite, σ-2-cycles hyperbolic planes (1,1); flow unbounded on off-line pairs. [N] finite explicit formulas: inertia (6+2m, 2m), m = 0..3 (60 digits). [C] Katz–Sarnak Bull. AMS 36 (1999) 1–26: over F_q normalized Frobenius in USp(2g) (Weil). [N] spacing statistics: ζ GUE-consistent (KS.024, 20000 zeros), DH on-line rejected at 5% (KS.121 >.063): readouts of the zeros (fail R5). Answer to B1: compact real form for ζ = RH restated.
pitfalls: Circular: compactness on the zero side is RH.
GUE statistics are computed from the zeros (fail R5).

concepts.name: Block-wise Weil-form diagnostic (BR-2): R-symmetric tilt blocks detect DH’s off-line pairs from the prime side
concepts.plain: Testing Weil’s form on pairs of tilted wave packets finds Davenport–Heilbronn’s two off-line zero pairs from the primes alone, while ζ stays positive on the same tests.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: 2×2 blocks of Weil's form at height γ on f± = e^{−u²/2w²}cos(γu)e^{±τu}; R: u ↦ −u swaps f±, so A = [[a,b],[b,a]], eigenvectors cosh/sinh tilts, hyperbolic iff |b| > a. Prime side (Dirichlet coefficients only) + arch (+ pole for ζ), X ≤ e^16; zero side = check. w = 1.5: prime side converged to ≤ 1e−7 (X-cut differences); ζ: no significant negative eigenvalue anywhere on γ ∈ [10,120] (all τ); DH (τ = 0.15, 0.3): hyperbolic on [85.48,85.92] and [114.04,114.29] plus a flank [84.36,84.77], nowhere else (λ₋ = −1.884 and −0.367 at τ = 0.3), first significant at X = e^12 (111,273 nonzero DH coefficients; ζ: 15,040 prime powers), matching the zero side; τ = 0 (1-dim) blind at w = 1.5. Planted ghost on ζ's zero side detected at [85.57,85.87]. The brief's cos/sin block is conformal (∝ I) and never hyperbolic (TAA Lemma 153, correction 8). Not a proof: prime side = zero side exactly (explicit formula); detection is finite-X resolution.
numbers: w=2.5: prime side not converged at X=e^16 (false negatives for ζ)
pitfalls: Circular as a proof: the prime side equals the zero side.
w = 2.5 needs X > e^16.
Zero list (TAA Lemma 141) differs from the converged prime side by up to 0.17 at γ ≈ 50, 100.

concepts.name: Euler product and functional equation work only together: the window positivity test
concepts.plain: Take Weil-type window forms with the same archimedean term (an odd character of conductor 5) and compare four functions. The genuine product ½L(χ)L(χ̄), which has both an Euler product and a functional equation, stays positive on every window up to length 12. The Davenport–Heilbronn function (functional equation, no Euler product) loses positivity at window length 4.8. Random completely multiplicative Euler products (Euler product, no functional equation) lose it at 1.7–2.5, and the same Euler product with every atom sign flipped at 1.6. So neither property alone carries the sign: a proof step has to use both at once. This is a diagnostic on finite windows, not evidence for RH.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Euler product and functional equation work only together: the window positivity test. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: Z_ℓ = arch(odd, q = 5) − Σ Λ_f(n) n^(−½) · (box kernel at log n), box grid h = 0.02; first window ℓ with n₋(Z_ℓ) ≥ 1
numbers: ½L(χ)L(χ̄), χ the odd quartic character mod 5: n₋ = 0 to ℓ = 12 (λ_min = 4.0e−5 at ℓ = 8, 1.7e−5 at ℓ = 12)
Davenport–Heilbronn: first crossing 0 → 2 at ℓ = 4.80; n₋ = 2 at ℓ = 8
random unimodular completely multiplicative coefficients (6 seeds): first crossing ℓ = 1.68–2.48; n₋ = 27–44 at ℓ = 8
same Euler product with all atom signs flipped: first crossing ℓ = 1.60
pitfalls: Window positivity of the genuine form up to ℓ = 12 is consistent with GRH for χ mod 5; it is not evidence for it.

The functional equation is shown necessary only numerically here. Davenport–Heilbronn shows that a functional equation alone is not sufficient (Theorem); it does not make the Euler product necessary, since Weng zeta functions have a functional equation, no Euler product, and satisfy RH (Lagarias–Suzuki; Suzuki; Ki–Komori–Suzuki).

concepts.name: Completeness rigidity: one missing prime creates many unstable modes
concepts.plain: The count "exactly one unstable mode" of the arithmetic side of Weil’s form is reached only when every prime power up to the window scale e^ℓ is present. Dropping a single prime from ζ’s Euler product creates many negative modes on every window tested (1 → 7 at ℓ = 2 without p = 2; 1 → 53 at ℓ = 6). Truncated products give counts that go up and down as primes are added, so there is no monotone prime-by-prime filtration. The count is a global cancellation, not a product of local counts. Mechanism [Theorem]: dropping p multiplies ζ by (1 − p^(−s)), whose zeros lie on Re s = 0, at distance ½ from the critical line.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Completeness rigidity: one missing prime creates many unstable modes. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: n₋(Z_ℓ) is subadditive: n₋(A + B) ≤ n₋(A) + n₋(B) [Theorem]; (n₋(Z), n₋(W)) on box grids h = 0.02
numbers: ℓ = 4: (1, 0) once all p ≤ 55 are present; all but 2 (27, 26); all but 7 (20, 20)
ℓ = 6: (1, 0) once all p ≤ 404 are present; all but 2 (53, 52); all but 7 (44, 44)
non-monotone count at ℓ = 4 as primes are added: 8, 11, 15, 20, 19, 23, 18, 8, 1
pitfalls: "Each local Euler factor has exactly two invariant lines and the product keeps the count" fails as stated: each local factor 1/(1 − p^(−s)) has a whole lattice of poles on Re s = 0 [Heuristic reading].
The qualitative observation that positivity breaks after the first omitted prime is earlier work in the programme; the counts and the drop-one-prime test are new.

concepts.name: DH prime-side Gram test
concepts.plain: Build the Weil-form Gram matrix of Davenport–Heilbronn from its Dirichlet coefficients alone; it turns indefinite at span 3.85.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: c_DH(n), n ≤ e^{3.85} ≈ 47, plus Γ-factor suffice; λ_max jumps −8e−9 → 3e−2 between L = 3.80 and 3.90. TAA Lemma 168: reproduced at h = 0.025 by P-smooth truncations: DH onset 3.85 reached at P = 43 and fixed for all 428 primes ≤ e⁸.

concepts.name: Primitive-part Weil spectrometer: the TAA Lemma 149 Weil Gram restricted to kerP = {∫f e^{±u/2} = 0} (pole/cusp functionals): ζ’s only negative direction without the pole row is the pole direction (index 1, removed by kerP); ζ, L(χ₅) PSD on full and kerP to W = 16; DH’s failure is primitive: same onset (3.875 at h = 0.025, 5.7 at h = 0.05) and essentially the same index (24 / 14 at W ≈ 16) on kerP
concepts.plain: Split the Weil test into the part tied to the pole of ζ and the rest. The pole part accounts for exactly one negative direction and nothing else; ζ and a genuine L-function are fine on the rest, while DH fails on the rest exactly as before. So DH's failure is in the 'primitive' part, where the missing positivity has to come from.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: [N] TAA Lemma 149 cubic-B-spline hats, h = 0.05 (N = 4..319) and h = 0.025 (N = 4..637 step 3); generalized eigenproblem vs hat Gram; thresholds −1e−9 and −1e−12 agree. ζ full λ_min ≥ 6.6e−12 (floor), ζ without pole row: 1 negative from W = 0.25/0.275, none on kerP. χ₅ (χ(2) = i): 0 on both. DH index 1 → 24 (h = 0.025) and 1 → 14 (h = 0.05) by W ≈ 16; kerP differs by ≤ 1 at a few W. [C] Bombieri 2000 (Rend. Lincei 11): if RH failed with finitely many off-line zeros, for large truncations #negative eigenvalues = ½ #off-line zeros; read here for DH by analogy only. The primitive part is where the MP4 sign lives; it is not supplied by the projection.
pitfalls: Index not converged in h (24 vs 14): finite-resolution count, not a zero count.
ζ passing to W = 16 is a check consistent with the known zeros, not evidence for RH beyond them.

concepts.name: Two standing ghosts in the truncated Weil test: the Epstein zeta Z_Q/2, Q = x² + 5y² (non-negative coefficients, FE, pole, Γ_R(s)Γ_R(s+1), conductor 20, no Euler product) fails at W = 3.0 (kerP 3.175; no pole row 1.05) and locks there for all P ≥ 7 (all P-smooth n); prime powers only lock at 3.35; ζ_K = ζL(χ₋₂₀) (same Γ factor, Euler product) passes to W = 8 and its truncations track log q; Epstein index 32 at W = 7.9 vs DH 6 at W = 8
concepts.plain: The Epstein zeta function of x² + 5y² has positive coefficients and the right symmetry but no Euler product. In the same prime-truncation test it fails early (at 3.0) and stays failed, like DH; its Euler-product partner ζ_K, with the same symmetry, passes.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: [N] h = 0.025, n ≤ e^8.1; coefficients exact (r_Q(n)/2; genus check ζ_K = Σ_{d|n} χ₋₂₀(d) max error 0; ζ_K composite c(n) ≤ 6e−14). Epstein composite c(n) ≠ 0 from n = 6 (c₆ = 2 log 6 = 3.584), then 14, 21, 36, 46, …; |c| leakage share 0.55/0.70/0.78 at n ≤ 40/400/3296 (DH 0.48/0.60/0.70; ζ_K ≤ 6e−16). ζ_K truncations: onset W > log q with larger slack than ζ for small P (degree-2 archimedean term). [C] Davenport–Heilbronn 1936 / Lamzouri 2021 (arXiv 1907.06387): Epstein with h(D) ≥ 2 has infinitely many zeros in Re s > 1 and ≫ T zeros in σ₁ < Re s < σ₂. Positive coefficients + FE + pole do not give positivity; the separating input is multiplicativity (cf. TAA Lemma 164, TAA Lemma 166).
pitfalls: Normalization F = Z_Q/2 so a₁ = 1; the Weil form of a non-Euler series is a formal analogue (its explicit formula still holds via −F′/F).
Index counts at finite h, not zero counts.

concepts.name: Weil Gram matrix of prime-localised bumps (mutual-inductance matrix), computed from primes and ∞ only
concepts.plain: Put a narrow bump at each log p and evaluate the Weil quadratic form on pairs, using only the primes and the archimedean term. The matrix agrees with the zero-side sum to 1e−12 and is positive semidefinite to rounding; its smallest eigenvalue goes to 0⁺ and its rank saturates at the number of zeros the bumps can see. Replacing the exponent ½ in the prime weights by 0.4 or 0.6 destroys positivity.

concepts.name: Growing-S rate test (h = 0.025, all 428 primes P ≤ e⁸): Euler-product truncations (ζ, L(χ₅)) fail just after log q of the first omitted prime (offsets 0.009–0.051 for ζ, all P; 0.017–0.063 for χ₅, P ≥ 7; small-P slack of χ₅ since χ₅(5) = 0) with pre-onset margin 1.8e−6 → 5e−11 (numerical floor); DH with all P-smooth composites tracks log q until P = 41 and locks at its global onset 3.85 for all P ≥ 43; DH prime powers only locks at 1.90 for all P ≥ 3
concepts.plain: Keep only the primes up to P and test positivity. For true Euler products the test fails exactly when the first missing prime comes into view, every time, for all 428 primes tried. DH behaves the same while its composite terms are kept, until it hits its own failure point at 3.85, where it stays.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: [N] onset = first span with λ_min < −1e−9 (bisection, exact to h). ζ_P = pole + arch + prime powers p ≤ P; DHs_P = arch + all P-smooth n; DHp_P = arch + prime powers only. Per-prime offset bounded by about half the hat support (2h = 0.05; χ₅ up to 0.063), no trend with log q: no finite S is positive beyond log of the next prime (per-prime data cannot certify positivity; v5 no-go 27/28). DH lock at 3.85 reproduces TAA Lemma 149 dh_prime_side_gram (n ≤ e^3.85 ≈ 47 suffices); DHp lock at 1.90 reproduces TAA Lemma 165 (c₆ at log 6). DH-sensitivity appears only through composites; the per-prime offset itself is not DH-sensitive (DHs offsets match ζ’s until P = 41).
pitfalls: Margins below ~1e−10 are at the conditioning floor of the hat basis (full ζ λ_min ≈ 7e−12 at W = 16).
Rate = offset in span; no claim about the size of positivity added per prime beyond the margin column.

concepts.name: Chebyshev bias for elliptic curves (averaged sign of a_p)
concepts.plain: Individual signs of a_p are phase data, but their running average is biased, and the bias is governed by the zeros of L(E, s) and the analytic rank, in the same way ψ(x) − x is governed by the zeros of ζ. An off-line zero would make the averaged sign blow up like a power of x.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Sarnak, letter to Mazur (2007, opened): S_{1,E}(x) = (log x/√x) Σ_{p≤x} a_E(p)/√p has mean −2r + 1 under GRH + independence. TAA Lemma 150 NUM (p ≤ 1e7): log-mean of θ_E/√x = 0.942, −1.101, −3.189, 0.949 for 11a1, 37a1, 389a1, 32a (1 − 2r = 1, −1, −3, 1); ζ: (θ(x) − x)/√x log-mean −1.123. An off-line zero gives power-law growth x^{β−½}.

pitfalls: Literature citation to verify: none is given until opened at source.
Counting version (signs of a_p) differs for CM vs non-CM curves (Sarnak); TAA Lemma 150 uses only the weighted sum.

concepts.plain: A (TAA Lemma 103) replaces one on-line zero by a pair and so adds a zero (tests multiplicity); B compares the pair with an on-line double zero (pure β, O(δ²)); C replaces two neighbours by the pair (count preserved).

concepts.name: Deninger’s foliated program
concepts.plain: Deninger’s program: a foliated dynamical space whose leafwise cohomology carries the zeros; a positive Hodge star plus the flow would force Θ = ½ + (skew part).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 4: foliation-like (Deninger) structure carries the explicit formula with its signs; contact-like (Reeb) gives only the analytic shadow; on closed M, Reeb flows and Deninger systems are mutually exclusive. TAA Lemma 28: zeros = leafwise zero modes [analogy/conjectural]. TAA Lemma 50 Prop 7.1 (Den98): positive J commuting with Θ ⇒ Θ − ½ skew [RESTATEMENT]. TAA Lemma 93: Deninger D1–D5 stated exactly. TAA Lemma 141 §2: level S3 of the "surface" target. TAA Lemma 151 Conj 4.1 (OPEN): Deninger's conjectured cohomology stated as axioms MP0–MP4 (H⁰/H² = Tate boundary terms; H¹ with flow, spectrum = zeros; trace formula; cup product to ℝ(−1); definite cup square on primitive part = the sign). Naming rule: no coined name until constructed. Deninger 2007 (opened): 'the conjectured cohomology has not been constructed'. TAA Lemma 174: Livšic route audit — conformal ⇒ α = 0 on compact manifolds (Thm V; Deninger Rem. 2); explicit formula fixes only ε = +1 and |det A_p| = p (Thm I). Reference note: ICM 1998 paper: page range 163–186 (Documenta Extra Volume; 23–46 is a database numbering).

concepts.name: Light cone U = ⟨𝟙, 𝕃⟩ (pole plane, null rays)
concepts.plain: The two special directions (the trivial class 𝟙 and the Lefschetz/pole class 𝕃) span a plane with one positive and one negative direction; positivity is always measured relative to it.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Over F_q: U = ⟨f₁, f₂⟩ ⊂ NS(C×C), signature (1,1), f₁, f₂ null; ample class lies in U; complement negative definite. Over ℚ: the pole/Tate plane spanned by 𝟙 and 𝕃 (poles at s = 0, 1), U^⊥ = V₀ (TAA Lemma 142).

concepts.name: Surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (D8)
concepts.plain: The curve proof needs a surface, an ample class and Riemann–Roch.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D8 (TAA Lemma 140): surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index. TAA Lemma 145 V3: classical S1 quadratic RR, S2 Serre, S3 h¹ ≥ 0, S4 sections ⇒ effective, S5 ample·eff > 0; the missing Spec ℤ step is quadratic S1 + S4. TAA Lemma 147: CC18 calls exactly this "the key missing step". TAA Lemma 152 Table 1: the chain exists for F_q curves and arithmetic surfaces; for Spec ℤ the space is partial, the ample class missing (Pic^ ≅ ℝ), RR 1-dimensional (CC22/23), Hodge index ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91). Deligne's route avoids Hodge index but not positivity (deligne_tensor_power).

concepts.name: Ax1–Ax3 axioms (Yoneda specification)
concepts.plain: The three ingredients that together force RH for curves: Hodge index on Frobenius graphs (Ax1), a positive involution † (Ax2), and ππ† = q for that same † (Ax3).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 137: on T_W, |α| = √q ⇔ Ax2 ∧ Ax3 ⇔ Ax1 ∀N. Each axiom alone is ghost-blind (Ax3 alone tautological; Ax2 alone holds for fakes); only the joint requirement separates. All qualifying items are over F_q; no Spec ℤ item qualifies.
numbers: 7 of 135 items in the programme’s positivity inventory pass (TAA Lemma 137)
pitfalls: Ax3 (unitarity, ππ† = q) is satisfied by ghosts too; never present it as positivity.

concepts.name: Limiting mixed Hodge structure / nilpotent and SL₂-orbit theorems (Schmid; CKS)
concepts.plain: When a family of Hodge structures degenerates, the limit remembers a filtration with a definite form on each layer; this is the formal object behind the rings.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: A polarized VHS over a punctured disc has quasi-unipotent monodromy T; with N = log of its unipotent part, Schmid's nilpotent orbit theorem (Invent. 22, 1973, Thm 4.9) and SL₂-orbit theorem (Thm 5.13) give a limiting MHS: weight filtration W(N) centred at w, N^k: Gr_{w+k} ≅ Gr_{w−k}, the form Q(·, N^k C ·) positive on primitive pieces (CKS, Ann. 123, 1986). J. W. McGreevy's picture mapped: definite family = polarized VHS; origin = degeneration; rings = W(N); duality across strata = N^k. Correction: a half-turn (T = −1, finite order) has N = 0 and gives no weight filtration; the rings need unipotent monodromy such as τ ↦ τ + 1 (TAA Lemma 153, correction 11).

rels.note: local model of a degenerate H¹

concepts.name: Tensor square HZ ∧_𝕊 HZ and its Laurent piece (quadratic only in U)
concepts.plain: The tensor square of ℤ over the sphere spectrum is bigger than ℤ and has a Laurent-polynomial piece; its sections grow quadratically, but the quadratic term is only the U-form, so it is vacuous on the degree-0 divisors that matter for RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CC16 Prop 7.4: HZ ∧ HZ ≇ HZ, assembly onto ℤ[t^±]^{⊗k}/ℤ. TAA Lemma 147 Laurent model (t-degree ≤ nβ, coefficient ≤ 2^{nα}): box count 2n² + 4n exact; ℓ² ball counts = volume to 4.8e−6 (n = 10), log₂ # = 2n² − n log₂ n + O(n); coefficient 2αβ is the U-form ⇒ vacuous on degree-0 D(f) (Thm vac). Needed: NS ⊋ U containing Ψ_λ with #H⁰(±nD(f)) ≥ 2^{n² s(f,f)/2}.
concepts.formula: log₂ # = 2n² − n log₂ n + O(n); quadratic coefficient 2αβ = U-form
pitfalls: Quadratic growth here comes only from U, so it says nothing about the primitive part V₀ (Thm vac).

concepts.name: Livšic route to conformality, split: under Deninger’s working hypothesis 7.5 ζ’s explicit formula fixes only ε_γp(k) = +1 and |det A_p| = p for the return map of the log p orbit; tr M_p (M_p = A_p/√p) is constrained only by |tr M_p| < √p + 1/√p, while Kalinin–Sadovskaya’s periodic-data conformality theorem needs |tr M_p| < 2; the scalar factor e^t is supplied by abelian Livšic, the conformal structure (≡ invariant leafwise J, i.e. H4 at the prime orbits) is not
concepts.plain: If every closed orbit of Deninger's hoped-for flow stretched its two transverse directions equally, a theorem of Kalinin and Sadovskaya type would make the whole flow conformal, and Deninger's theorem would put the zeros on the line. The explicit formula, though, only tells us each orbit's sign and its area scaling p. It cannot tell a rotation from a mild squeeze, so the key local input has to come from somewhere else. Worse, equal stretching on every orbit is more than RH needs: a slightly bent version of Deninger's own example keeps RH, yet stretches unequally at one fixed point. So the missing input has to be global, a positivity on the square, as in Connes and Consani's programme.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Thm I (invisibility) and Prop S (abelian half) of TAA Lemma 174; conditional on (A1) a solenoidal version of KS 2010 Thm 1.3 (Open). [C] Kalinin, Ann. Math. 173 (2011): Livšic for GL(m,R) cocycles over transitive homeomorphisms of compact metric spaces with the closing property; Kalinin–Sadovskaya, JMD 4 (2010) Thm 1.3: 2-dim fibres, return maps diagonalizable over C with equal-modulus eigenvalues ⇒ conformal (base: transitive C² Anosov diffeo of a compact manifold). [Open] (A1) solenoidal KS; [Open] (A2) fixed points (infinitely generated orbit lengths); [Open] (A3) the local input, invisible to the explicit formula. RH is not proved. [T] Conformal (SO(2)) periodic data on the prime orbits is invisible to the explicit formula (Thm I) and strictly stronger than RH: a nonlinear perturbation of Deninger's CM elliptic-curve solenoid over F₅ keeps H¹, hence RH, but has a node fixed point (agreed in partner review; the perturbation is not reproduced in TAA Lemma 174). So a per-orbit route needs a rigidity axiom that arithmetic does not supply, and (B) must be global: an intersection pairing Γ_F·Δ on the square with Rosati/Hodge-index positivity [R: this restates Connes–Consani]. Model: Deninger's elliptic-curve solenoid satisfies all links (return maps π^ν, C-linear; Hasse ⇔ |π| = √q).
numbers: |det A_p| = p from the k ≤ −1 coefficients Np^k
pitfalls: Kalinin–Sadovskaya 2010 is for C² Anosov diffeomorphisms of compact manifolds only.
The earlier reading “each prime orbit’s transversal is a rotation” holds only when |det| = 1 (TAA Lemma 174, correction 1).

concepts.name: Parity argument: linear χ cannot see D²
concepts.plain: A Riemann–Roch whose Euler characteristic is linear (odd) in D can prove "positive degree ⇒ sections" but never contains D²; a quadratic (even) χ is needed for Hodge index.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 145: quadratic χ is even in D, linear χ odd ⇒ fixed rank only proves degree c(D) = 0, never sees D². TAA Lemma 147: for CC23, χ(D) + χ(−D) = 2 for deg₂D ∉ ℤ (even part constant 2χ(𝒪), odd part ⌈deg₂D⌉′); χ(D) + χ(K−D) = 0 except −1 on deg₂ ∈ (−2,0) (observation).
pitfalls: χ-symmetry is an observation, not a CC claim (TAA Lemma 147 s2).

concepts.name: Adelic gluing: ℍ at ∞ and Bruhat–Tits trees at p in GL₂(ℚ)∖GL₂(𝔸)
concepts.plain: The global object glues the hyperbolic disk at infinity to a tree at each prime; local RH holds at each prime for holomorphic forms, but the global RH does not follow.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: GL₂(ℚ)∖GL₂(𝔸)/K glues the upper half-plane (∞) with the (p+1)-regular Bruhat–Tits tree at each p (BIB, Serre 'Trees', unopened). Local RH at p = temperedness: Hecke eigenvalue in the ℓ²-spectrum [−2√p, 2√p] of the tree (Ramanujan–Petersson; proved for holomorphic weight ≥ 2 by Deligne 1974; open for Maass forms). GRH for these L-functions remains open. GL₁ version: Connes's adele class space 𝔸_ℚ/ℚ^× (Connes 1999). This is the 'global picture' J. W. McGreevy asked for: the gluing exists; the missing input is global positivity (MP4).
concepts.uncertain: Serre Trees and the tree spectrum statement: BIB, not opened.

concepts.name: Tautology boundary (zero side vs prime side)
concepts.plain: Checking positivity using the zeros themselves is circular; a real test must use only primes, the pole and the archimedean place.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: all entries of the relative Gram are zero-free (flow, U/Tate poles, Γ_ℝ, Λ(n)); sign = RH (Weil); the zero-side check is the tautology. Unconditional sign only on windows ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) and arch-only a* (TAA Lemma 127), both ghost-blind.
pitfalls: "Without zero locations" is vacuous in finite models (Newton identities, TAA Lemma 109).

concepts.name: No étale H¹ for Spec ℤ
concepts.plain: Spec ℤ is simply connected; the "H¹" must be relative to the flow (ψ − x ≠ 0).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 140: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1 ⇒ H¹ét = 0. TAA Lemma 141 §4: H¹ table with a flow-H¹ column; Q(√2) circle length √2·log(1+√2) = 1.24645 (Schoof). The H¹ that carries zeros is flow-relative (ψ − x).

concepts.name: MP4 headline: the Euler product, taken as geometry (the Frobenius correspondence: graph classes on the square with an ample class), not as counting data, induces the Hodge splitting of the square, with its sign
aliases: Euler product induces the Hodge splitting (v5 wording)
concepts.plain: Unique factorization splits ζ across the primes but carries no sign; on a surface the Hodge index splits the square and supplies the sign. Over finite fields Weil needed both. The conjecture: over the integers the first produces the second.
concepts.label: Conjecture
concepts.core: Two splittings. (a) Euler product: a splitting across primes, no sign [Theorem]: −ζ′/ζ supported on prime powers ⇔ Euler product (TAA Lemma 165); for eigenforms one SU(2) class per prime, Flath restricted tensor product; every Dirichlet L has it and GRH for them is open. (b) Hodge index on the square: an ample class splits NS ⊗ ℝ = ℝH ⊕ H^⊥ with H^⊥ negative definite, which on Frobenius graphs is Weil/Castelnuovo positivity. (c) Over F_q both are needed (Riemann–Roch on C×C plus an ample class for the sign; the Frobenius correspondence for the arithmetic); fake polynomials share the counting input and fail the sign (TAA Lemma 137, TAA Lemma 141). Conjecture: in Deninger's conjectured cohomology splitting (a) produces a Θ-invariant splitting of the square whose primitive part is definite, i.e. MP4(1)–(2), with the sign derived (R7) and all primes in each window used at once (R8′). Not the claim (a) = (b): the two tensors (across primes vs L ⊗ R) are distinct and identifying them is an Analogy. Undefined for DH (composite leakage): exclusion, not a sign. Provisional reading of "couple all places" (adopted until a better definition is found): a signed product formula on the square (Open). TAA Lemma 166 (function-field test): counts + FE + positive integer closed-point counts do not induce the sign (675/2935/4961 count-positive off-circle fakes, g = 2, q = 7/11/13); the conjecture survives only in a geometric reading (the Euler product of an object whose square has Hodge index). Headline reworded (approved by J. W. McGreevy after TAA Lemma 166): "the Euler product, taken as geometry (the Frobenius correspondence: graph classes on the square with an ample class), not as counting data, induces the Hodge splitting of the square, with its sign". Reason: over F_q, counting data, the functional equation and non-negative closed-point counts do not induce the sign (TAA Lemma 166: 675/2935/4961 count-positive off-circle fakes); the sign comes from the Frobenius correspondence on C×C with an ample class (Hodge index). The v4 sharp form stays underneath. Standard controls for any proposed mechanism: DH and Epstein x² + 5y².
concepts.formula: Euler product as Frobenius correspondence on the square (+ ample class) ⟹? Hodge splitting with sign
pitfalls: Do not identify the Euler-product tensor (across primes) with the L ⊗ R tensor of the surface: Analogy only.

concepts.core: The shape of the missing piece: ten necessary properties (P1–P10). From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
numbers: P1 sees all primes jointly (fails when one prime is dropped) — proved necessary for this criterion [Theorem mechanism + Numerical]

P2 uses the Euler product and the functional equation together — a functional equation alone is not sufficient [Theorem, Davenport–Heilbronn]; the Euler product is not necessary in general (Weng zetas satisfy RH without one) [Theorem]; functional equation necessary [Numerical only]
P3 invariant under the reflection s ↦ 1 − s (centrosymmetry of the window) [Restatement]
P4 gives a sign on the primitive part, not on the pole plane, which is indefinite (1,1) — proved necessary [Theorem, Haynsworth inertia]
P5 reduces to Castelnuovo–Severi / Hodge index over F_q [Heuristic: desirable, not forced]
P6 works with zero margin, as an identity rather than a bound — proved necessary [Theorem: no uniform margin; sup r = 1]
P7 controls the infimum of λ₂ over windows (monotone, continuous at log p), not jump events [Theorem + Numerical]
P8 is not ghost-blind: it must change when an off-line zero is planted — proved necessary [Theorem, logic]
P9 carries a metric, not only a measure: a positive pairing of half-densities [Heuristic/Restatement]
P10 is additive under gluing of windows: gluing defect 0 for ζ, at least 2 for Davenport–Heilbronn [Numerical; testable]
pitfalls: Every criterion on this list that is equivalent to RH is circular as an input.
The missing structure is referred to as Deninger’s conjectured cohomology; no new name is coined.

concepts.name: Rosati positivity
concepts.plain: An involution † on endomorphisms with Tr(φφ†) > 0 — like a squared length that is never negative. With ππ† = q it forces |α| = √q.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Tr(φφ†) > 0 on End⁰(J); ππ† = q ⇒ |α| = √q (Milne AV 14.3). On R[F]: Rosati PD ⇔ RH-model ⇔ ∃ compatible J with [J,F] = 0; n₋ = #real pairs + 2#quartets (TAA Lemma 106). Over ℚ: Rosati = Weil form is a restatement.
numbers: TAA Lemma 157: Rosati positivity = the g of the Kähler triple attached to the polarization (Riemann form E(ix,x) > 0); dual = adjoint ⇔ |α| = √q
pitfalls: |φ| = 1 on Re s = ½ is only the adjoint half ππ† = q (Ax3), ghost-blind.
Positivity over F_q is geometric, from intersection numbers, not arithmetic (TAA Lemma 106, correction 1).

rels.note: Rosati = Cartan θ_J on commutant (TAA Lemma 99)

concepts.name: Krein collisions (how ghosts are born)
concepts.plain: Zeros on the line carry a sign; two can only leave the line together if they meet with opposite signs.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 111: semisimple unit-spectrum F strongly stable ⇔ Krein form definite on each eigenspace; ghosts born only at opposite-sign collisions (710/710 births). For ζ the graphical Krein sign alternates ⇒ no protection; Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable. TAA Lemma 160: KGL rule re-sourced (Gelfand–Lidskii MR0091390 record); 4×4 toy (ε = 0.2): opposite signs exit for |ω₁ − ω₂| < 0.2, same sign never; H_t collision (4,5) re-checked t* = −3.954792524 (diff 2.2e−9 from TAA Lemma 111); box count conserved, real count 2 → 0. TAA Lemma 161: Gascheau–Routh TAA Lemma 4 as the classical model: slow mode Krein −, fast +; collision at μ_R = 0.0385209; μ = 0.04 quadruple ±0.0675 ± 0.7103i; damping makes the pre-collision regime unstable too (BKMR 1994). TAA Lemma 163: sp(4,ℝ) normal form: equal-frequency oscillators coupled by ε leave the axis iff Krein signatures are opposite (band ≈ 2ε). TAA Lemma 165: realized arithmetically: every DH ghost with t ≤ 600 is born from a collision of two opposite-sign on-line crossings of the σ-pencil (signs 200/294 → 185/279).
pitfalls: Krein = stability, not positivity; presupposes unit spectrum (TAA Lemma 111 circularity).

concepts.name: Castelnuovo–Severi inequality
concepts.plain: On the surface C×C a class cannot be "too timelike" relative to the two fibre directions; applied to Frobenius graphs it gives RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: D² ≤ 2(D·f₁)(D·f₂); def(D) = 2d₁d₂ − D² = −(D°)² = Tr_{H¹}(α_D α_D†) (C–S = Rosati, TAA Lemma 133). Weil mF + n: −(2gqm² + 2amn + 2gn²) ≤ 0 ⇔ a² ≤ 4g²q (TAA Lemma 125). TAA Lemma 152 §3: the proved source of positivity over F_q (Weil 1948, BIB): surface → ample → RR → Hodge index; Weil's criterion is the definition, not the source.
numbers: primitive Gram det 4p − a² > 0 (29 primes, TAA Lemma 133)
pitfalls: A “−2Tr” formula holds only on the primitive part with the g-dimensional trace.

concepts.name: de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ
concepts.plain: Heat flow on ξ; Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao), RH ⇔ Λ = 0.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Λ ≥ 0 ⇒ ζ not heat-flow stable (TAA Lemma 111). Healing times TAA Lemma 124/TAA Lemma 136 conflict. TAA Lemma 150 (opened): Rodgers–Tao Λ ≥ 0 (Forum Math Pi 2020), Polymath 15 Λ ≤ 0.22; H_0(z) = Ξ(z/2)/8, so t_RT = 4·t_Ξ (TAA Lemma 150, correction 8). DH heuristic (truncated list): pair at 85.70 closes at t_RT ≈ 0.177 (isolated 2δ² = 0.190); does not separate DH from ζ's known range. TAA Lemma 158: H_t = ∫e^{tu²}Φ(u)cos(zu)du solves the BACKWARD heat equation ∂_tH = −∂_zzH (Rodgers–Tao, Polymath, opened); increasing t (= exp(−tD²), anti-dissipative) makes zeros real (Pólya); the dissipative (forward-heat) direction t ↓ creates collisions and complex pairs. RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0; Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao, Forum Math Pi 2020); Λ ≤ ½ (de Bruijn 1950); −∞ < Λ (Newman 1976); Λ ≤ 0.22 (Polymath). Toy exp(−tD²)(z²−1)(z²−1.6²): Λ_toy = −0.0463. F/V merge = 𝔽_q picture of the collision (Analogy, fv_merge_trichotomy). TAA Lemma 159: Newman–Wu 2019 (opened): the 1976 theorem's motivation came 'more by statistical physics and Euclidean field theory … than by analytic number theory'; Lee–Yang property of Φ is the precise Lee–Yang form of RH (lee_yang_fisher_rh). TAA Lemma 160: direction stated explicitly (RT convention ∂_t H = −∂_zz H; increasing t makes zeros real; collisions come from lowering t); RH ⇔ Λ = 0; under RH with simple zeros the forced collisions escape every compact set as t → 0⁻ (dbn_parabolic_threshold). Newman 1976 is Proc. AMS 61, 245–251 (AMS DOI record; TAA Lemma 158 had 246). L180: local flow = F/V sweep; Λ_p = ACM Lemma 3.18 (t_ACM = t log²p, t_RT = 4t); product cross-term explicit; Λ_global = 0 for incommensurable Hasse products (Heuristic/Numerical).
pitfalls: t* = 2δ² vs δ²/2.

concepts.name: Frobenius as a boost (rapidity ½ log q)
concepts.plain: On the light-cone plane Frobenius acts like a Lorentz boost of rapidity ½ log q; a true curve needs one boost, a fake needs two.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hodge index + one boost of rapidity ½ log q on the H–V plane ⇒ Hasse; fakes need two (TAA Lemma 98 thm:fqboost). Over ℚ: translation is an isometry, pole boost rapidity ½ log λ; Lorentzian = Weil positivity (restatement). TAA Lemma 150 §4.5: Doppler red/blue shift = boost; on-line motion = rotation (a_p = 2√p cos θ_p), off-line displacement σ − ½ = rapidity; a shift √p e^{±η} is forbidden for curves by Castelnuovo/Hodge index; TAA Lemma 58 'RH = exclude boosts'. Ghost-sensitive (it is δ itself).
concepts.formula: B_{½ log q}(H + V) = Γ/√q (hyperbolic part)
pitfalls: Dividing by √q does not undo the boost (TAA Lemma 114, correction 14).
Two boosts are never a pure rotation unless inverse (TAA Lemma 107).

rels.note: Levinson/Szegő step = boost of rapidity artanh|α| (TAA Lemma 98, TAA Lemma 117)
Doppler reading is ghost-sensitive, Higgs reading is not

concepts.name: Epstein zeta no-go
concepts.plain: Epstein zeta functions of binary quadratic forms have a functional equation but no Euler product, and they have zeros off the line — the classic counterexample class next to DH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 83: Epstein x² + 5y² = ζL(χ₋₂₀) + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅); N(200) = 253 zeros, 183 on the line (70 off-line); first off-line 0.93297 + 15.66825i. TAA Lemma 135: 46 zeros with ½ < σ < 1 for t ≤ 250; control x² + y² (= 4ζL(χ₋₄), has Euler product): 0. TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion and FE hold, unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 153 (G, CM points): Σ′(m²+n²)^{−s} = 4ζ(s)L(s,χ₋₄) (NUM s = 3: 4.6589136156); Σ′(m²+mn+n²)^{−s} = 6ζ(s)L(s,χ₋₃) (6.3758815528); x²+5y²: ζ_K + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), 2x²+2xy+3y²: ζ_K − L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅), sum over the class group = 2ζ_K (Euler product restored, Hecke; NUM to 1e−12). Off-line zero refined: 0.9329696975 + 15.6682495313i (|Z| = 3e−21; ζ_K there 0.933). CM points are where one restricts (toric periods), not a quotient (TAA Lemma 153, correction 22). TAA Lemma 164 (merged here; the delta proposed a separate positive-ghost entry): Z_Q = ζL(χ₋₂₀) + L(χ₋₄)L(χ₅) (genus theory, checked n ≤ 300) has non-negative integer multiplicities (a Gibbs/KMS system with H = log Q(m,n)), the functional equation and Bochner positivity, yet zeros with ½ < Re ρ < 1, so KMS/thermal/partition-function positivity does not force RH; r_Q(2)r_Q(3) = 0 ≠ r_Q(6) = 4 (a sum of two Euler products, like DH). Davenport–Heilbronn 1936: infinitely many zeros in σ > 1 (cited). TAA Lemma 164 Krawczyk-certified 52 zeros with Re ρ ≥ 0.52, t < 400 (max Re 0.9549; mpmath |Z_Q(ρ₁)| = 2.8e−15). Correction (Missing Piece v5, I16): the 52 is a lower bound, not a census, because TAA Lemma 164's scan grid starts at σ = 0.52 (TAA Lemma 135 already found 46 zeros with ½ < σ < 1 for t ≤ 250, against 38 in TAA Lemma 164's list there); and the ghost is not new: it is this entry (TAA Lemma 83, TAA Lemma 135, TAA Lemma 138, TAA Lemma 153, TAA Lemma 159). TAA Lemma 164 adds the KMS/Bochner reading and the certification.
numbers: TAA Lemma 164: ≥ 52 certified zeros with Re ρ ≥ 0.52, t < 400 (lower bound: grid starts at σ = 0.52)
TAA Lemma 169: truncated Weil test h = 0.025: onset 3.0 (kerP 3.175, no pole 1.05); index 32 at W = 7.9; ζ_K control passes to W = 8
TAA Lemma 174: counting θ̂ ≈ 0.32; composite share of |c(n)| 0.921; ψ slope 0.92 (max Re 0.955)
pitfalls: TAA Lemma 159: Epstein x² + 5y² is a genuine positive-weight gas (Bochner, convexity) with FE and an off-line zero: gas positivity is not RH-forcing; its log is not infinitely divisible (40 negative Lévy coefficients, n ≤ 2000).
TAA Lemma 164 presented this ghost as new; it was already this entry (correction I16 of Missing Piece v5). Its count 52 is a lower bound, not a census.

class number 2 ⇒ no Euler product ⇒ off-line zeros (DH 1936)
