concepts.name: Zeros as Breit–Wigner resonances (line shapes, cusp doublets)
aliases: Zeros as Breit–Wigner resonances; ghosts as gain lines
concepts.plain: In scattering language every zero is a resonance peak; at the cusp it is a pair of peaks whose widths are equal exactly when the zero is on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Breit–Wigner line (Γ/2)/((E−E₀)² + (Γ/2)²): FWHM Γ, area π, lifetime 1/Γ (Fourier image of e^{iE₀u−Γu/2}); BW 1936 Phys. Rev. 49, 519–531 (Crossref record only). Zero lines of ξ′/ξ on Re s = σ are signed BW lines (gamma_fwhm_of_a_zero). Cusp (TAA Lemma 153 Thm 7.7): −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1/(¼+t²) + Σ_ρ two positive BW lines at γ/2, HWHM β/2 (from ξ(2s−1)) and (1−β)/2 (from ξ(2s)); sum ½; no inverted lines on the cusp. [N] DH ghost 1 cusp widths 0.09574 / 0.40415 vs 0.09574 / 0.40426, amplitudes 2.000/2.000; ghost 2 0.1737/0.3219 vs 0.1746/0.3254 (far-tail limited). [R] parity-doublet splitting = unequal widths; [A] Higgs complex doublet (loose: no continuous group, vev, eaten modes); [A] ±Γ pair ↔ PT-symmetric gain/loss.
numbers: TAA Lemma 117: min τ_d on [10,30], true ξ 0.00105 (d = 0.01); ghost (γ₁, 0.3) −0.22, −2.49 at d = 0.01, 0.1; excess delay 4π per quartet
[N] TAA Lemma 156, correction 1: cusp ghost 2 widths 0.17458489/0.32541474 vs 0.17458496/0.32541504 after subtracting certified zeros < 200 (quadratic bg); TAA Lemma 154 0.1737/0.3219 superseded
pitfalls: Higgs doublet comparison is a loose Analogy (TAA Lemma 154, correction 13).
BW 1936 not opened; facts proved directly.
A ghost’s width on σ = ½ + d tends to Γ = 2(β−½) from below as d → 0; it never stays “at least Γ” (TAA Lemma 154, correction 2).
Optics’ “negative group delay is harmless” does not transfer: for ξ, RH ⇔ positive group delay on every line σ > ½ (TAA Lemma 154, correction 12; TAA Lemma 117).
Lagarias 1999 (Hinkkanen) criterion: opened in TAA Lemma 146 and re-opened in TAA Lemma 154; TAA Lemma 117 proves τ_d > 0 ∀d ⇔ RH inline and cites only Lagarias–Suzuki.

The TAA Lemma 154 cusp widths for DH ghost 2 (0.1737/0.3219) are superseded by 0.17458489/0.32541474 (predicted 0.17458496/0.32541504) once certified zeros below t = 200 are subtracted (TAA Lemma 156, correction 1).

rels.note: Wigner delay = sum of BW lines
J. W. McGreevy: direct touch point
no gain lines right of ½

concepts.name: Conic type decided at infinity: degree positivity ⇒ ellipse ⇒ Hasse
concepts.plain: Whether the quadratic form deg is an ellipse or a hyperbola is decided at infinity; deg ≥ 0 because it counts points, so it is an ellipse, which is the Hasse bound.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: A conic is an ellipse/parabola/hyperbola as it has 0/1/2 real points at infinity (discriminant of Q = 0); a plane through the cone's vertex gives a line pair (J. W. McGreevy's wedge). For E/F_q: deg(m − nF) = m² − a·mn + q·n² ≥ 0 (it counts a kernel) ⇒ a² − 4q ≤ 0 ⇔ Hasse (Silverman AEC Thm V.1.1): the norm conic is an ellipse; a² = 4q gives a double line (TAA Lemma 152, correction 10). Same as TAA Lemma 150's det −(4q − a²), signature (1,3); fakes (a² > 4q) give a hyperbola and (2,2). For ζ: Weil's form in blocks, on-line zero elliptic, off-line pair hyperbolic (1,1). Missing ingredient as a 'degree': a count (≥ 0) whose polarization is Weil's form (Open).
concepts.formula: deg(m − nF) = m² − a mn + q n² ≥ 0 ⇒ a² ≤ 4q
numbers: 11a1 at p = 2,3,5,7: ellipses; fake p = 5, a = 5: hyperbola

concepts.name: Ghost quartet ½ ± δ ± iγ
concepts.plain: A fake set of four zeros off the line, replacing a pair ½ ± iγ, used to test whether a criterion can detect RH failure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 103 convention: replace ½ ± iγ by ½ ± δ ± iγ; each quartet gives 2 negative Weil eigenvalues; onsets L* listed.
pitfalls: δ convention conflict: δ = β − ½ (TAA Lemma 25/TAA Lemma 103/TAA Lemma 143) vs δ_ρ = 2β − 1 (TAA Lemma 144).

concepts.name: Poincaré disk: period domain, cusp degeneration and the trace classification
concepts.plain: In the hyperbolic disk every motion is a rotation, a slide toward the boundary, or a boost between two boundary points; Frobenius of an elliptic curve is always a rotation, a ghost would be a boost.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ℍ ≅ D = SL₂(ℝ)/SO(2) is the period domain of weight-1 rank-2 polarized Hodge structures; degeneration at a cusp with unipotent T: τ ↦ τ+1, N = log T, W(N) weights 0, 2. The Klein (projective) model is the Cayley–Klein geometry with a real absolute conic; the boundary = null rays of ℝ^{2,1}; SO⁺(2,1) ≅ PSL₂(ℝ). Trace classification: |tr| < 2 elliptic (rotation), |tr| = 2 parabolic (unipotent; horocycles to a cusp), |tr| > 2 hyperbolic (boost along a geodesic, two real fixed boundary points). Frob/√q has trace a/√q: elliptic ⇔ |a| < 2√q (Hasse; for a² = 4q Frobenius is ±√q·I, not unipotent). TAA Lemma 153 NUM: 11a1, 302 primes < 2000, max |a_p|/√p = 1.947 (all elliptic); fake trace 2cosh 0.3 = 2.091 hyperbolic. Ghost = boost (TAA Lemma 42 Def 6.12 'every arithmetic Frobenius Euclidean'; TAA Lemma 58 'RH = exclude boosts'). Not global: the cusp ≠ archimedean place (TAA Lemma 146); Maass–Selberg/Petersson positivity reaches only Re s = 1 and is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 69, TAA Lemma 146).

rels.note: disk boundary is not the archimedean place

concepts.name: F/V merge: circle → ellipse → parabolic → hyperbola (t = a/√q; τ(t); sign pattern)
concepts.plain: As Frobenius and Verschiebung slide together on the unit circle, the invariant conic goes from a circle to ever thinner ellipses; when they meet it degenerates, and past that it becomes a hyperbola with positive and negative wedges, which only fake zeta functions reach.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] M_t = [[0,−1],[1,t]] (Frobenius/√q on ℤ[π], t = a/√q) preserves Q_t = m² + tmn + n² (residual 0); disc t² − 4: |t| < 2 definite (closed ellipses; circle iff t = 0), |t| = 2 degenerate, |t| > 2 indefinite (1,1): + in two opposite wedges, − in the other two. Eigenvalues α, ᾱ = (t ± i√(4−t²))/2 start at ±i (t = 0), meet at 1 (t = 2), split on ℝ. Fixed point τ(t) = (−t + i√(4−t²))/2 of z ↦ −1/(z+t): τ = i at t = 0 (the round START), → ∂ℍ as |t| → 2. [N] t = 0 occurs for every supersingular E/𝔽_p, p ≥ 5 (y² = x³ − x, p ≡ 3 mod 4: 8/8; y² = x³ + 1, p ≡ 2 mod 3: 9/9): not specific to CM by ℤ[i]. |t| = 2 on actual curves: y² = x³ − x over 𝔽_{p²} (p = 3, 7, 11): a = −2p, π = −p scalar (every form invariant, TAA Lemma 157, correction 4), not a Jordan block. [T] Mirror α ↔ ᾱ and half turn Q(−x) = Q(x) persist in every stage: ghost-blind; the signal is sign(t² − 4) (signature), coordinate-free. [A] The merge is the 𝔽_q picture of the de Bruijn–Newman collision. TAA Lemma 160: the merge never happens in a single Euler factor at a good prime (|a_p| < 2√p); at the level of zeros it is the dBN double zero (zeros_as_frames_trichotomy); one-frame Wick rotation in euler_factor_wick_rotation. TAA Lemma 161: F = V is the parabolic escape of the invariant conic (Kepler e_K = t/2 = 1 after Bohlin); hyperbolic F, V span the asymptotes, mirror images in the 45° apsidal axis.
numbers: scalar Frobenius over F_{p²}: a = −2p for p = 3, 7, 11
pitfalls: τ = i is the start (t = 0), not the meeting point (TAA Lemma 158, correction 13).
At |t| = 2 actual curves have scalar Frobenius; the parallel-line picture is the non-semisimple model (TAA Lemma 158, correction 14).
The 'tilt' of an axis is coordinate-dependent; use the discriminant/signature (TAA Lemma 158, correction 17).

concepts.name: Compatible complex structure J commuting with Frobenius
concepts.plain: A quarter-turn that commutes with Frobenius and makes the form positive; it exists exactly when the curve satisfies RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: J = (2F − a)/√(4q − a²) (TAA Lemma 101) exists only if a² < 4q; 2^g sign choices, exactly one positive. Finite: compatible J with [J,F] = 0 ⇔ F unitary semisimple (TAA Lemma 104). For ζ: J exists ⇔ RH (restatement, TAA Lemma 104 dichotomy).
numbers: g = 1, q = 101: J = J_F exact; ghosts give Cl(1,1)
pitfalls: A quartet J is symplectic but never compatible (sig (2,2)) (TAA Lemma 110).
With a W-independent form J is unconditional but ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 104).

concepts.name: Ghost map Δ_w: zeros right of σ from damped Dirichlet sums
concepts.plain: Subtract the smoothed comb from a damped prime sum: whatever is left is a bump at each zero that lies right of the observation line, and its phase tells how far right.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] D_w(s) = Σ c(n) n^{−s} e^{−w² log² n/2} (entire), A_w = Gaussian-smoothed archimedean part, k_w*F_σ = smoothed comb on Re s = σ. Then A_w − D_w = Σ_ρ J_w(s−ρ) and Δ_w := A_w − D_w − k_w*F_σ = Σ_{β>σ} (√2π/w) exp((s−ρ)²/2w²): one Gaussian bump (width w) per zero right of σ, peak (√2π/w)e^{(β−σ)²/2w²}, phase slope (σ−β)/w² ⇒ γ̂, β̂, Γ̂ = 2(β̂−½). Identity holds whatever the zeros do (no RH content). Inputs: coefficients + Γ-factor + FE (F_σ by theta-function AFE); no zero list (TAA Lemma 155, correction 1). [N] DH: SNR (vs ζ control) ≥ 10 at X ≈ e^4 ≈ 55 (w = 0.4–0.5), β to 0.01 at X ≈ e^5 (w = 0.5, σ = 0.55), β̂ = 0.80852 / 0.65083 to ≤ 4e−9 at X = e^16 (SNR 6e6); ζ: no bump, floor ≤ 1e−6.
numbers: [N] AFE comb = TAA Lemma 154 direct to 6.5e−13 (DH, σ = 0.55), N = 13 terms suffice
[N] ghost map SNR ≥ 10 at log X = 4 (w ≥ 0.4)
pitfalls: Not coefficients alone: needs Γ-factor and FE inside the strip (TAA Lemma 155, correction 1).
Threshold measured only at t ≈ 86–114 (TAA Lemma 155, correction 7).
ζ null result proves nothing about RH.

rels.note: AFE uses θ(1/x) = x^{3/2}θ(x) for DH
ghosts the map detects are certified by Krawczyk boxes (TAA Lemma 156)

concepts.name: Arithmetic unitarity ("RH = unitarity")
concepts.plain: TAA’s founding claim made precise: the scaling flow is always an isometry of the Weil form; RH is the statement that this form is positive, so the flow is genuinely unitary.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 1 Thm 2.1: (ii) T_t is a 𝒬-isometry unconditionally; (iii) growth exponent = Θ − ½; (iv) RH ⇔ 𝒬 ≥ 0 ⇔ unitary Hilbert realization ⇔ bounded matrix coefficients.
pitfalls: Isometry is free (Ax3-like); positivity of the form is the content (Ax2).

concepts.name: Genealogy of DH ghosts: the σ-pencil f_λ = (1−λ)Λ(χ) + λWΛ(χ̄) (χ mod 5) keeps a functional equation for all real λ, runs from the Euler product L(χ) to DH (λ = 1/2); on-line zeros = crossings of one phase θ(t) with the level tan θ = −(1−λ)/λ; off-line pairs are born at folds (Krein collisions of opposite-sign crossings) with the square-root law; t ≤ 600: 17 escapes, 2 captures, net 15 = DH census
concepts.plain: Slide continuously from a genuine L-function to DH and watch: zeros move along the line, and every time two of them with opposite orientation collide, a pair jumps off. Doing this up to height 600 recreates exactly DH's 15 known bad zeros and records when and where each was born.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N] 154875-point Arb grid t ≤ 620; 242 certified folds; escapes (t_c, λ*) from (85.90,.3054) … (531.73,.0330); every endpoint Krawczyk-certified as a DH zero, equal to TAA Lemma 156/cycle-3 census to double precision (2 in uncensused 135–200); Krawczyk both sides of each fold; exponents.496–.500; on-line 494 → 464, signs 200/294 → 185/279 (one of each per collision). Captures at λ =.4445 (t 286.2),.4148 (t 475.8). LRL/precession comparison: Analogy only.

concepts.name: Fake Weil polynomials (finite ghosts)
concepts.plain: Polynomials that look like curve zeta numerators (functional equation, integer counts) but have roots off the circle. They are the F_q test ghosts.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Fakes pass FE, count positivity, mod-2 data and the Hecke lattice (1,2); they fail Hodge index on ⟨H,V,Δ,Γ_{Fⁿ}⟩ (n₊ ≥ 2) and Rosati. Mixed fake (T² − 6T + 7)(T² + 7) passes N ≤ 2, fails from N = 4 (TAA Lemma 137, TAA Lemma 141). TAA Lemma 166: on the primitive Gram, #positive eigenvalues = #σ-2-cycles of off-circle roots (real pair 1, quartet 2), checked on all stored fakes.
pitfalls: Degenerate fakes (|α| ∈ {1, q}) cause pole-degenerate exceptions (TAA Lemma 92 C9).

concepts.name: RH for curves over F_q (Weil)
concepts.plain: For a curve over a finite field the Frobenius eigenvalues all have size √q. This is the one setting where TAA’s positivity is a theorem.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Weil 1948: Castelnuovo–Severi / Hodge index on C×C ⇒ |α_i| = √q. Proved without the zeros: surface + ample class + Riemann–Roch ⇒ Hodge index ⇒ sign.
pitfalls: Weil already did column 2 (1940 note, 1948 books); the open step is column 3.

concepts.name: Γ is the dual−adjoint gap: ⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v,v⟩ = 1 − 2β
concepts.plain: The width Γ of a zero equals how far the pairing-dual and the positive adjoint disagree on that zero.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] For any eigenvector v (|v| = 1) of Θ with eigenvalue ρ = β+iγ: Θ^∨v = (1−ρ)v and ⟨Θ†v,v⟩ = ρ̄, so ⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v,v⟩ = 1 − 2β and Γ_ρ = |1−2β| = |(1−ρ) − ρ̄| ≤ ‖Θ^∨ − Θ†‖ = 2‖S‖ (no normality needed). 𝔽_q: |q/α − ᾱ| = |q − |α|²|/|α|; in exponents (α = q^s) |(1−s) − s̄| = |1−2β|. [N, certified inputs TAA Lemma 156] DH: ρ₁ gap 0.617034364913274771106, ρ₂ 0.301660161219474164808, ρ₃ 0.14871210090161198144, ρ₄ 0.448515389253619560422 (mirrors equal); ζ (52 zeros, t < 150) and DH on-line (122, t < 200): gap 0.
pitfalls: Γ ≤ ‖Θ^∨ − Θ†‖ is an inequality per eigenline; equality of operators needs normality.

concepts.name: KMS/modular positivity is coefficient positivity: a KMS system with partition function F = Σ a_n n^{−β} exists ⇔ a_n ∈ ℤ≥0; then t ↦ F(β+it) is positive definite (|F(β+it)| ≤ F(β)). Compact pieces of the modular route: Tomita J (ℤ/2) and the imaginary-time circle; the BC modular group n^{it} is unitary but not periodic and acts on the prime side (log n)
concepts.plain: The thermal (KMS) route makes imaginary time a circle and gives a positivity, but that positivity is only about the coefficients being counts. It rules out DH for the wrong reason and lets other bad functions through.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Bochner; Tomita–Takesaki S = JΔ^{1/2} (checked 2e−16); thermal time = Hamiltonian time (Connes–Rovelli); BW: wedge boost, e^{2πiK} = 1. [N] BC: Tr e^{−βH} = ζ(β); Galois-averaged KMS value (p^{1−β}−1)/(p−1) (2e−31); symmetry breaking φ(e(1/5)) =.04+.606i. Toeplitz test β = 1.6: ζ, Z_Q PSD, DH min −3.96 (relative). DH excluded by coefficients (not a sign on zeros); Z_Q passes ⇒ B2 negative (TAA Lemma 164 Cor. 4.3).

concepts.name: Lee–Yang vs Fisher zeros; Newman's Lee–Yang property of Φ ⇔ RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0
concepts.plain: Lee and Yang proved that ferromagnets have their partition-function zeros on a circle. ζ's zeros are zeros in temperature (Fisher zeros), not in field; the exact Lee–Yang-type statement for ζ is the de Bruijn–Newman one, which is RH itself.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: [C] Lee–Yang (1952): ferromagnetic Ising, zeros in the fugacity z = e^{−2βh} on |z| = 1; Newman 1974 extension (Newman–Wu 2019 Thm 11, opened); Lee–Yang zeros (field) vs Fisher zeros (temperature) (Wikipedia 'Lee–Yang theory', opened). [N] 3-spin toy: ferromagnet J = 0.4 zeros |z| = 1, 1, 1; antiferromagnet J = −0.4: 13.79, 1.00, 0.0725. [T] Truncated Euler products have no zeros in any prime fugacity: ζ zeros are Fisher zeros of the Bost–Connes continuation, not Lee–Yang zeros (TAA Lemma 124). [C/R] Precise Lee–Yang form: Newman–Wu Thm 9 (de Bruijn 1950, Newman 1976): H_λ has only real zeros iff λ ≥ Λ; RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0; Rodgers–Tao Λ ≥ 0; Polymath Λ ≤ 0.22. NW19: the 1976 result's 'original motivation was provided more by statistical physics and Euclidean field theory … than by analytic number theory'. e^{λt²} weighting = Gaussian (ferromagnetic-type) tilt; increasing λ = backward heat (TAA Lemma 158, correction 16). L180: Newman 1976 (opened) proves the classification of the class 𝒫 and Φ ∉ 𝒫 unconditionally (so b₀ < ∞), and states RH as b₀ ≥ 0. It does not state 'RH ⇔ Φ Lee–Yang'; that follows from Newman 1974 via Lieb–Sokal 1981 (first pages opened). ζ zeros are Fisher-type (temperature) zeros of the Bost–Connes continuation at Re β = ½, beyond the transition at β = 1; finite truncations have zeros off the line.
pitfalls: ζ zeros are Fisher, not Lee–Yang, zeros (TAA Lemma 159, correction 5).
Lee–Yang 1952 originals not opened (via Newman–Wu, Wikipedia).

concepts.name: Certified zero lists (Arb): DH complete for t < 200, ζ for t < 150
concepts.plain: Rigorous computer arithmetic proves that the zero lists used for the width measurements are complete and accurate, so the widths and flips are theorems, not fits.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N, rigorous] Arb ball arithmetic: argument principle on [−1,2]×[t_a,t_b] (segment enclosures excluding 0 in a sector < π), sign changes of the real completed function at γ ± 1e−12, Krawczyk boxes for off-line zeros; count = sign intervals + boxes ⇒ list complete, simple, on-line ones on the line. DH 2 < t < 135: 79 = 75 + 4 (standard list correct to 1e−12); ρ₁ = 0.808517182456637385553 + 85.699348485377592171929i, ρ₂ = 0.650830080609737082404 + 114.163342730756980904164i (± 6e−22). DH 135 < t < 200: 51 = 47 + 4; new pairs ρ₃ = 0.57435605045080599072 + 166.47930591316815587648i, ρ₄ = 0.724257694626809780211 + 176.702461242855825054474i. ζ 2 < t < 150: 52, all simple on the line. [T] ⇒ TAA Lemma 154 widths 2d, flips at d* = β−½ ∈ (0.30,0.35), (0.15,0.20), Γ₁ = 0.617034364913274771106, Γ₂ = 0.30166016121947416481 (± 3e−21), ghost FWHM → Γ from below.
numbers: [N, rigorous] DH t < 135: 79 zeros = 75 on-line + 4 off-line (certified complete)
[N] first-order fit bounds ≤ 1.6e−5 rel (ghost 2: 6.3e−5 with tail subtracted)
pitfalls: Fit outputs certified to first order only; nonlinear remainder measured (≤ 2.9e−10).
Nothing certified above t = 200.

rels.note: TAA Lemma 156, correction 1: corrected cusp ghost-2 widths

concepts.name: Λ = 0 (⇔ RH, given Rodgers–Tao) puts ζ at the parabolic threshold of the de Bruijn–Newman family — at infinity: with simple zeros, forced collisions for t < 0 escape every compact set
concepts.plain: Under RH the heat-flow family sits exactly at the point where lowering the time would push zeros off the line. Since ζ's known zeros are all simple, the first collisions would happen farther and farther up, so ζ is at the edge only at infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C] Newman 1976: −∞ < Λ ≤ ½, zeros of H_t all real ⇔ t ≥ Λ; de Bruijn 1950: real for t ≥ ½; Rodgers–Tao (Forum Math. Pi 8 (2020) e6) Thm 1: Λ ≥ 0; Polymath 15 Thm 1.1: Λ ≤ 0.22; CSV 1994 Cor. 1: for t > Λ zeros real and simple. [R] RH ⇔ Λ = 0. Direction: ∂_t H_t = −∂_zz H_t (RT: backwards heat); increasing t makes zeros real; collisions come from LOWERING t (TAA Lemma 158, correction 16, TAA Lemma 160, correction 6). [T] Prop: under RH, if H_0 has simple zeros near a compact K, then for −δ < t ≤ 0 all zeros of H_t in K are real; since H_t has non-real zeros for every t < 0, these leave every compact set as t → 0⁻: the threshold is at infinity. Simplicity verified for the first 1,500,000,001 zeros (γ < 545,439,823.215; van de Lune–te Riele–Winter 1986). Newman's 'barely true' (RT §1; CSV 'quantitative version of the dictum'); Lehmer pairs are finite-height witnesses (CSV Thm 1). [N] first low collision at t ≈ −3.95 (zeros 4, 5), far from 0.
pitfalls: ζ does not have a double zero at any computed height; the family, not ζ, is at threshold (TAA Lemma 160, correction 5).
H_t has no Euler product for t ≠ 0 (TAA Lemma 160, correction 9).

concepts.name: Decay rate ¼
concepts.plain: Every scattering resonance of the modular surface decays at rate ¼ exactly when its ζ-zero is on the line; an off-line zero decays at (1−β)/2 instead.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally, poles at ρ/2 symmetric about ¼, rate (1−β)/2; RH ⇔ all rates ¼ [R]. TAA Lemma 120: spectral rate ¼, not uniform. TAA Lemma 143 SC-A (L + unitarity ⇒ κ ≡ ¼) ⇔ RH; ringing rate 0.24996 vs predicted ¼. TAA Lemma 144: μ = ¼ for every ρ (FE), ghost and DH ring at 0.0957414 = (1−β)/2.
concepts.formula: rate = (1 − β)/2; RH ⇔ all rates = ¼
pitfalls: The circular line for the modular surface is Re s = ¼, not ½ (TAA Lemma 143 corrections); rate = (1−β)/2, not Re ρ/2 (TAA Lemma 143 corrections).
No essential spectral gap for the modular surface (Bourgain–Dyatlov 1612.09040).

concepts.name: Eisenstein scattering resonances at s = ρ/2: purity at Re s = ¼
concepts.plain: At the cusp the Eisenstein series scatters with a phase of modulus one; its poles sit at half the zeta zeros, all on one line exactly when RH holds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s) for SL₂(ℤ): |φ(½+it)| = 1 (NUM 2e−31), φ(s)φ(1−s) = 1 (FE, ghost-blind; NUM 8e−32). Zeros ρ of ζ give poles of φ at s = ρ/2 (simple: |φ|·ε → 0.5146 at ρ₁/2): under RH all on Re s = ¼ (one stratum); an off-line zero β + iγ would sit at Re s = β/2 (DH-type fake: 0.404, 0.0957, 0.325, 0.175 vs 0.25). Constant term a₀(y) = y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s} on s = ½+it: half-density lobes y^{½}e^{±it log y}. Where Selberg's zeta picks these up (Hejhal, Venkov): BIB, unopened.

concepts.name: Goldfeld’s theorem (Euler product at s = 1 ⇒ RH, analytic order)
concepts.plain: If the partial Euler product of L(E,s) at the centre behaves like C/(log x)^r, then L(E,s) satisfies RH and r is the analytic order of vanishing — with a surprising √2 in the constant.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: If ∏_{p≤x} L_p(E,1) ∼ C/(log x)^r then L(E,s) satisfies RH, r = ord_{s=1}L(E,s), C = L^{(r)}(E,1)/(r! √2 e^{rγ}) (Goldfeld 1982, cited via Conrad 2005; TAA Lemma 140).
pitfalls: It gives the analytic order, not the rank (rank = order is BSD).
a_p are not BSD generators.
Note the √2 factor (Conrad).
Finite products (±10% oscillation to 1e7) are not evidence for RH (TAA Lemma 150, correction 10).

rels.note: prime data vs the reference at s = 1

concepts.name: ℤ̂ in the dictionary: Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂; ℚ⧵𝔸 ≅ (ℝ × ℤ̂)/ℤ; C_ℚ ≅ ℝ₊* × ℤ̂*
concepts.plain: The profinite integers are where all the finite primes live in the adelic picture. They are not the analogue of Frobenius over ℚ (that is the real scaling flow); they give the totally disconnected direction and the Dirichlet-character sectors, and DH sits in no single sector.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C] Gal(𝔽̄_q/𝔽_q) ≅ ℤ̂ (Frobenius generates the dense ℤ); ℤ̂ = ∏ℤ_p, dual ℚ/ℤ; 𝔸_ℚ ≅ ℝ × (ℤ̂⊗ℚ) (Wikipedia, opened). [T] ℚ + (ℝ × ℤ̂) = 𝔸_ℚ and ℚ ∩ (ℝ × ℤ̂) = ℤ ⇒ ℚ⧵𝔸_ℚ ≅ (ℝ × ℤ̂)/ℤ, the adelic solenoid (leaves ℝ, transversal ℤ̂; Den05's S¹_p = ℝ ×_ℤ ℤ_p is the one-prime case, opened). [T] class number 1 + ℤ^× = {±1}: C_ℚ = ℚ^×⧵𝔸^× ≅ ℝ₊* × ℤ̂*. [C] Connes 1999 (20)–(21): C_k ≅ K × N, N = ℝ₊* (number fields) vs q^ℤ (function fields); H = ⊕_χ H_χ over characters of K. Dictionary: over ℚ the Frobenius role goes to ℝ₊* (the flow), not to ℤ̂; ℤ̂ carries the finite primes (transversal), ℤ̂* the Dirichlet-character sectors. [T,N] DH = ½(1−iκ)L(s,χ) + ½(1+iκ)L(s,χ̄), χ mod 5 (residual 0): a sum of two sectors, in no single one; a(2)a(3) = −0.0807 ≠ a(6) = 1. Wikipedia's line 𝔸^×/ℚ^× ≅ (ℝ×ℤ̂)/ℤ conflates the additive quotient: not used.
pitfalls: ℤ̂ ≠ the Frobenius group over ℚ: Connes N = ℝ₊*.
Sector exclusion of DH is structural, not a sign: GRH per sector remains open.

concepts.name: Trace part = polarization (projection onto span{h,v}, ample ω = h + v, ω² = 2), positivity = definiteness of the primitive part relative to it; together = Hodge index on E×E (primitive Gram [[−2,−a],[−a,−2q]] definite ⇔ a² < 4q)
concepts.plain: Split each class into the part along the two fibre directions and the rest. The first part is the polarization. Positivity means the rest is definite, and that only makes sense relative to the polarization. The two together are the Hodge index theorem, which is Weil's proof of RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Trace part = polarization (projection onto span{h,v}, ample ω = h + v, ω² = 2), positivity = definiteness of the primitive part relative to it; together = Hodge index on E×E (primitive Gram [[−2,−a],[−a,−2q]] definite ⇔ a² < 4q)
numbers: h − v complement indefinite even for real curves
pitfalls: The trace-free part alone is not positivity. The flowed primitive form is definite iff t > Λ_p (formal).

concepts.name: Gas positivities: positive weights ⇒ positive-definite KMS characteristic function and convex log Z; Euler product ⇒ infinitely divisible (free gas). DH fails all; Epstein and ζ(s)ζ(s+a) show none forces RH
aliases: Bochner positivity of the KMS state
infinite divisibility of the zeta distribution
concepts.plain: A genuine gas needs positive weights, and a free gas needs an Euler product. Davenport–Heilbronn fails both tests and even has negative heat capacity, but Epstein zeta functions and ζ(s)ζ(s+a) pass them and still have zeros off their lines, so gas positivity alone cannot give RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] For a Dirichlet series with a(n) ≥ 0 and β in the half-plane of absolute convergence: φ_β(t) = f(β+it)/f(β) is a characteristic function (positive definite, Bochner) and log f is convex in β (Cauchy–Schwarz), i.e. heat capacity ≥ 0. With an Euler product, log f = Σ b(n)n^{−s}, b(n) = Λ(n)/log n ≥ 0 for ζ: compound Poisson, infinitely divisible (a free gas of independent modes). [N] β = 2, Toeplitz [φ(t_i − t_j)], h = 0.25, N = 120: ζ min eigenvalue 1.3e−10 (PSD), DH −7.78 (10 negative). Lévy coefficients b(n), n ≤ 2000: ζ 0 negative; DH 466 negative, 615 nonzero off prime powers ('interacting'); ζ(s)ζ(s+½) 0 negative; Epstein x²+5y² (a(n) = r(n)/2 ≥ 0) 40 negative. Real-axis stability: (log DH)″ < 0 for 1 < β < 4.23183 (negative heat capacity), > 0 beyond. [T] DH coefficients periodic mod 5: (1, κ, −κ, −1, 0), κ = 0.284079 (two-sector mix, TAA Lemma 158). Ghost test: every rung separates DH (DH-sensitive) but none forces RH: Epstein x²+5y² has positive weights and FE s ↔ 1−s and an off-line zero 0.93297 + 15.66825i (TAA Lemma 83/TAA Lemma 153); ζ(s)ζ(s+a) has an Euler product and is infinitely divisible, with zeros on Re s = ½ and ½ − a, off its own FE line Re s = (1−a)/2 [T]. Hurwitz ζ(s,a) (a ≠ ½, 1; positive weights) has zeros in 1 < σ < 1+ε (Davenport–Heilbronn 1936 / Cassels, via Wikipedia).
numbers: Lévy negatives: ζ 0, DH 466, ζ(s)ζ(s+½) 0, Epstein 40 (n ≤ 2000)
pitfalls: DH-sensitive is not ghost-sensitive in general: Epstein (positive weights) and ζ(s)ζ(s+a) (Euler product) carry ghosts relative to their FE lines.
All of this lives at Re s > 1; the zeros are at Re s ≤ 1.

rels.note: signed weights, not ID, negative C for β < 4.23

concepts.name: Invariant (χ-type) vs refined (h-type) counts: Lefschetz/GRR totals, N(T), box counts are FE-determined and ghost-blind; the on-line count changes only at collisions; RH ⇔ refined = invariant
concepts.plain: Some counts can't change under deformation, like the total number of zeros or a Lefschetz number. Others can, like the number of zeros on the line. RH says the second count equals the first. Davenport–Heilbronn has the same total count as a true L-function but fewer zeros on the line, so the protected counts can't tell ghosts apart.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T/B] Lefschetz number homotopy-invariant (fixed points collide/annihilate in pairs); in flat proper families χ = Σ(−1)^i h^i is constant while h^i are upper semicontinuous (Hartshorne III.12.8, not opened); TAA Lemma 140: #C(F_{qⁿ}) − (1 + qⁿ) = −Tr(Fⁿ|H¹): H⁰/H² terms rigid, H¹ frames movable. [N] all 10,100 smooth y² = x³ + Ax + B over F_101: invariant part 102, a_p in [−20, 20] (41 values), all elliptic. [T] H_t: box count (argument principle) conserved across a collision (2.000000), real count 2 → 0. [R] N₀(T) = N(T) ∀T ⇔ RH. [H/N] DH: Riemann–von Mangoldt main term (T/2π)log(5T/2πe) by the FE argument (no source opened for DH): N(135) = 79 vs 79.0002, N(200) = 130 vs 129.548 (TAA Lemma 156 certified); on-line 75 and 122 (ghost deficits 4, 8 at 85.70, 114.16, 166.48, 176.70). ζ: N(150) = 52 vs 52.75. No-go: invariance of counts cannot exclude ghosts.
numbers: F_101 family: 1 + p = 102 fixed, 41 values of a_p
pitfalls: For ζ there is no family and no h¹ (Deninger’s conjectured cohomology, MP0–MP4): Analogy.
DH main term is Heuristic (no source opened) + Numerical (TAA Lemma 160, correction 14).

concepts.name: Li criterion
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ the Li coefficients are non-negative.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Li 1997 / Bombieri–Lagarias 1999: RH ⇔ λ_n ≥ 0 for all n — the Weil positivity in another basis. TAA Lemma 112 reads the Weil form as a Toeplitz–Carathéodory problem; TAA Lemma 131: no route supplies the positivity.

concepts.name: Cole–Hopf: Ψ = H′/H obeys backward Burgers ∂_tΨ = −Ψ″ − 2ΨΨ′; at one prime the Toeplitz sequence 2T_k(x_t) is positive-definite iff t ≥ Λ_p; product cross-term −2tΨ_pΨ_q
concepts.plain: The log-derivative side of the flow is a Burgers equation. At one prime its time-t positivity switches on exactly at the local Newman time. For products the primes couple at first order through a product of their log-derivatives.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Cole–Hopf: Ψ = H′/H obeys backward Burgers ∂_tΨ = −Ψ″ − 2ΨΨ′; at one prime the Toeplitz sequence 2T_k(x_t) is positive-definite iff t ≥ Λ_p; product cross-term −2tΨ_pΨ_q

concepts.name: de Branges spaces
concepts.plain: Hilbert spaces of entire functions built from a Hermite–Biehler function E; RH becomes "E_h is Hermite–Biehler", but de Branges’ stronger positivity conditions are known to fail for ζ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36 Thm 3.1: for h ∈ (0,½], all β ≤ ½ + h ⇔ PR on σ > ½ + h ⇔ E_{h′} HB ∀h′ > h; h = ½ free, h → 0 = RH. Conrey–Li 2000 (opened, TAA Lemma 78): de Branges positivity fails for ζ and χ₄. TAA Lemma 118: Ψ_c passive ⇔ E_c = ξ(·+c) Hermite–Biehler. TAA Lemma 34: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side.
pitfalls: Conrey–Li: de Branges’ stronger conditions fail — beware "positivity ⇒ RH" shortcuts.

concepts.name: Hasse bound as a positive degree form
aliases: Q_p = x² + a_p xy + p y²
concepts.plain: For an elliptic curve the degree of an endomorphism is a positive quadratic form; Hasse’s bound is that this form is positive (Cauchy–Schwarz / Pythagoras).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: deg(m + nπ) = m² + amn + qn² is PD ⇔ a² < 4q; Hasse = Cauchy–Schwarz. Ghost a = 25, q = 101: deg(10 − π) = −49 (TAA Lemma 106).
concepts.formula: m² + a mn + q n² > 0 ⇔ a² < 4q

concepts.name: Suzuki’s de Branges line from the prime side
concepts.plain: A de Branges / transmission-line object built from prime data whose passivity along the whole line is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Su21 (Suzuki JFA 281 (2021) 109116): E^{ω,ν} = ξ(½ + ω − iz)^ν, νω > 1, Hankel kernel from prime-side data (TAA Lemma 34). TAA Lemma 37: headline exponential line Θ_c = exp(−2c ξ′/ξ); ‖𝒦[t]‖ < 1 ∀t ⇔ sup ≤ 1; weak form sup_t ≤ 1 ⇔ RH; "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; strict pointwise bound open (M11).
pitfalls: "sup < 1" is false in the passive case; the correct form is sup ≤ 1 (TAA Lemma 37).

concepts.name: Bagchi recurrence
concepts.plain: RH ⇔ ζ approximates itself in the strip (strong recurrence).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Bagchi (via Nakamura Thm B): RH ⇔ strong recurrence of ζ for all K, ε ("infinite prime bath still recurs", TAA Lemma 118). TAA Lemma 123 local form [T given Voronin + Carlson]: ζ strongly recurrent on a disc K ⇔ no zero on K; ghosts show up as a local Rouché defect. Finite prime baths recur but are ghost-blind.

concepts.name: Inertia of a compressed Weil form gives 2/3 on the line
concepts.plain: A rank–trace inequality on a finite compression of the Weil hermitian form, with Sylvester inertia counting off-line pairs as negative squares, makes Montgomery's simple-zero argument unconditional: at least 2/3 of zeros are simple and on the line (preprint, Lean-formalized by its authors).
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Inertia of a compressed Weil form gives 2/3 on the line. Sources: arXiv:2608.13637.
concepts.uncertain: preprint, unrefereed

concepts.name: Coupled coils: the Frobenius norm form is a two-coil energy with coupling k = |a_p|/2√p; Hasse ⇔ k ≤ 1; one-factor Laguerre margin 4 log²p (1 − k)
concepts.plain: The quadratic form m² − a mn + p n² is the energy of two coupled inductors. It is never negative exactly when the coupling coefficient is at most one, which is the Hasse bound. A perfect transformer (k = 1) is the cusp; k > 1 would need an active element.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Coupled coils: the Frobenius norm form is a two-coil energy with coupling k = |a_p|/2√p; Hasse ⇔ k ≤ 1; one-factor Laguerre margin 4 log²p (1 − k)
concepts.formula: k_p = |a_p|/(2√p) = |cos θ_p|; Λ_p = log k_p / log²p; min_u (f′² − f f″) = 4 log²p (1 − k_p) for f = 2cos(u log p) − a/√p

concepts.name: Gain lines (active media)
concepts.plain: A ghost acts like a gain line: negative absorption.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §2: Re ξ′/ξ = Σ(σ−β)/((σ−β)² + (t−γ)²) — each zero is an absorption line to its right; an off-line zero gives a gain line. Grid σ ∈ [.505,1.1], t ∈ [80,92]: ξ min +0.00467; DH −66.84 at (0.794, 85.70), 1.89% negative; TAA Lemma 144 ghost −66.97 (1.94%). Lorentz model: dRe χ/dω −6 (absorber) / +6 (gain). TAA Lemma 154: measured widths — the near line of a DH ghost on σ = ½+d has FWHM 2|d − (β−½)| (match ≤ 3e−6, 13 d), inverted for d < β−½; as d → 0 its FWHM → Γ = 2(β−½) from below; the visible feature (near − mirror) keeps width ≈ ½(β−½) while its depth fades as 2d/(β−½)². KK sign invariant κ = Re F·∂_tIm F = −1/a³ flips at a gain line. [N] TAA Lemma 155: DH's gain lines reconstructed from ≈ 10 nonzero coefficients via the theta AFE (N = 13), and detected as ghost-map bumps from damped Dirichlet sums with X ≈ 55.

concepts.name: Near-null direction of ζ's relative Gram matrix
concepts.plain: The direction where ζ's relative Gram matrix is closest to zero is a function whose Fourier transform lives almost entirely below the first zero γ₁.
concepts.label: Numerical

rels.note: [explains] small-δ onsets jump where ζ's λ plateaus (L ∈ [8,14])

concepts.name: The one-box axis: F(ℓ) = W(1_[0,ℓ]) has a uniform rescaled margin on [1, 10], but only by a 1-in-9400 cancellation
concepts.plain: Instead of growing the number of test functions at a fixed window, take one box of length ℓ. The resulting function F(ℓ) is an explicit prime sum minus the pole plus the archimedean term. On the zero side it is a sum of squares under RH, and an off-line zero would add a term growing like e^(βℓ) with oscillating sign, so "F(ℓ) ≥ 0 for all ℓ" is (heuristically, Landau-type) equivalent to RH. Numerically F stays between 0.060 and 0.134 on [1, 10], but the pole and the primes cancel to one part in about 9400 at ℓ = 10. The obstruction is moved, not removed.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The one-box axis: F(ℓ) = W(1_[0,ℓ]) has a uniform rescaled margin on [1, 10], but only by a 1-in-9400 cancellation. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: F(ℓ) = ℓ·W(1_[0,ℓ]/√ℓ) = W(1_[0,ℓ]) = Σ_{γ>0} 8 sin²(γℓ/2)/γ² (under RH)
numbers: prime side = zero side (5000 zeros plus tail) to 2.1e−4 relative on ℓ ∈ [0.1, 10]
concepts.uncertain: The equivalence with RH is a Heuristic, Landau-type sketch; criteria of this shape are probably classical (not checked against the literature); no novelty is claimed.
pitfalls: As a route this is RH again (circular).
If the ordinates γ are linearly independent over ℚ, Kronecker’s theorem makes inf F = 0 over all ℓ, so the margin is uniform only on finite ranges [Heuristic].

concepts.name: Integer dimension over 𝕊 (minimal generators)
concepts.plain: On Spec ℤ̄ Connes–Consani’s dimension is an integer: the least number of generators over the sphere spectrum. The log-theta dimension of van der Geer–Schoof is a different, "virtual" count that agrees up to a bounded error.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147 [N]: brute force dim_𝕊(HZ)_[−m,m] = n + 1 for all m ≤ 16; dim_𝕊[±1] = ⌈log₃(2n+1)⌉ for all n ≤ 40; dim_𝕊 − vdGS h⁰/log 2 ∈ [1.016, 1.983]. TAA Lemma 147, correction 1: Dim_ℝ on C_p is a covering dimension, not a theta count.
pitfalls: Do not identify CC dimension with theta/lattice counts (TAA Lemma 147, correction 1).

concepts.name: Hodge index theorem
concepts.plain: On a surface the intersection form has exactly one positive direction (the ample class); everything orthogonal to it is negative. This sign is what proves RH for curves.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: NS(C×C) ⊗ ℝ has signature (1, ρ−1); U = ⟨f₁,f₂⟩ is the (1,1) part and its complement is negative definite. Over ℚ, Hodge-index form on V₀ ⇔ RH (TAA Lemma 91, restatement). Surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index (D8). TAA Lemma 162: E×E Gram of {pt×E, E×pt, Δ, Γ_F}: det = a² − 4p; one positive eigenvalue ⇔ |a| ≤ 2√p; compact-group analogue: Haar positivity (Peter–Weyl).
concepts.formula: sig NS = (1, ρ − 1); D·D ≤ 0 on h^⊥
pitfalls: Effectivity and Hodge index are independent on both sides (TAA Lemma 94).
Hodge index needs S2, S3, S5 too (TAA Lemma 145).

rels.note: D·D ≤ 0 on V₀ over ℚ (TAA Lemma 91)
U^⊥ = physical quotient (TAA Lemma 115, TAA Lemma 146)

concepts.name: Osterwalder–Schrader reflection positivity
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25 Prop 6.3: OS-RP for Weil with θu = −u FAILS (atom δ_{log2}: RP ≍ −1/ε, −2.50, −11.08, −35.58, −121.35 at ε = 0.1…0.003); OS gives H ≥ 0 semigroup, Weil a unitary group. TAA Lemma 32: RH ⇔ |OS_a| ≤ Q on E₊(a) (domination form); OS-RP false unconditionally. TAA Lemma 42 Thm 2.1/2.2/4.4 (Hankel ≠ Toeplitz; orthogonality pincer). TAA Lemma 47: reflection ⇒ FE, positivity needs polarization. Closest literature: Neeb–Ólafsson RP ↔ Lax–Phillips. TAA Lemma 151: failure at log 2 = smallest prime, not wildness; half density = the reflection (unitary) half of OS. TAA Lemma 153 (claim 6): for Gaussian data RP ⇔ the reflected form B(f,g) = ⟨θf,g⟩ is PSD on the positive-time space ⇔ every 2-plane restriction is an ellipse or degenerate (trivially, since 1-dim restrictions suffice); NOT ⇔ 'the blocks of one chosen decomposition are ellipses' unless they are B-orthogonal (TAA Lemma 153, correction 6). TAA Lemma 153's R-symmetric tilt blocks are reflection pairs (f₊, f₋ = Rf₊).
pitfalls: As stated (OS_a ≥ 0) it is false for ζ; only the domination |OS_a| ≤ Q is RH-equivalent.

rels.note: RP kernel with H² spectrum z would force z ≥ 0

concepts.name: Legendre strata: support function / Fenchel–Moreau as a definiteness detector
concepts.plain: All the information about a convex curve sits in the intercepts of its tangent lines; the Legendre transform returns the curve exactly when it is convex, so it is a definiteness test.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Tangent lines carry a convex curve: the support function h(θ) = sup_{x∈K}⟨x,u_θ⟩ determines a closed convex K (Minkowski; BIB). For f = ½xᵀAx the Legendre transform is ½pᵀA⁻¹p, finite everywhere iff A ≻ 0; if A has a negative eigenvalue f* ≡ +∞ (on a box |x| ≤ R it grows with R: TAA Lemma 153 NUM). Fenchel–Moreau: f** = f iff f is convex lsc (BIB). Support-function window of a conic region: 2π for an ellipse; for one convex hyperbola branch exactly 2·atan√(|λ₋|/λ₊) < π (NUM 64.8° vs 64.62° predicted for λ = 1, −0.4); for both branches (or the region xᵀAx ≤ 1 with A indefinite) empty; jump 2π → 0 at det = 0. J. W. McGreevy's 'Legendre type concept' is this. TAA Lemma 159: thermodynamic potentials U, F, H, G are Legendre transforms of one generating function on one Legendrian surface; stability (convexity) is what makes the dictionary invertible.

concepts.name: Weil operator C = i^{p−q} = Wick rotation
concepts.plain: Turning an indefinite pairing into a positive one by inserting a quarter turn — the same move as Wick rotation in physics.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 139: Q indefinite → Q(C·, ·̄) PD (Rosati); Abel–Jacobi = principalization. A complex structure is a μ₄ action (J² = −1). Obstruction: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has no complex structure.
numbers: y² = x³ − x: π/√p primitive 4th root of unity for p ≡ 3 mod 4 (TAA Lemma 140)
pitfalls: The Fourier transform is the swap, not the Weil operator (TAA Lemma 140).
Over F_q the sign is algebraic (Castelnuovo); the Hodge model is only an analogy there (TAA Lemma 139 caveat).

rels.note: no complex structure on Pic^ ≅ ℝ

concepts.name: Lax–Phillips scattering
concepts.plain: Scattering theory for waves on the modular surface; resonances relate to zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: LP80 (read at source, TAA Lemma 118/TAA Lemma 141): s(z) = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s), Res_{s=1} = 3/π, poles at zeros of ζ(1+2iz), RH ⇒ Im z = ¼; Pavlov–Faddeev "RH iff Z″ decays exponentially"; spectrum of B″ = {(κ−1)/2}; "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product". TAA Lemma 118 Thm 3.1: ‖Z″‖ ≤ 1 unconditionally. TAA Lemma 153: bib verified by Crossref: Lax–Phillips, Scattering Theory for Automorphic Functions, Ann. Math. Stud. 87 (Princeton 1976; De Gruyter record dated 1977), doi 10.1515/9781400881567; Bull. AMS 2 (1980) 261–295 (Crossref pages; TAA Lemma 141 cited 261–296, TAA Lemma 153, correction 31); Pavlov–Faddeev, J. Soviet Math. 3 (1975) 522–548, doi 10.1007/BF01084688 (Zap. LOMI 27 (1972)). Poles of φ at ρ/2 = eigenvalues of the generator of the contraction semigroup Z(t) (LP80, read in TAA Lemma 141); contraction ⇒ Re s ≤ ½ (Re ρ ≤ 1) only; purity Re s = ¼ ⇔ RH: Restatement of MP4 ('all that is missing is an appropriate inner product').
pitfalls: LP (6.19) rate sign ambiguous in OCR (TAA Lemma 118, correction 7).

concepts.name: Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations
concepts.plain: Pairing a holomorphic form with its own complex conjugate gives a positive number: a genuine |amplitude|².
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: HR holds on every compact Riemann surface; HR form = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Positivity = complex structure inserted (Weil operator C = i^{p−q}). Hecke self-adjointness gives a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
pitfalls: Column 2 (F_q) never fully inherited the HR sign; Castelnuovo replaces it algebraically (TAA Lemma 140).

rels.note: cup with the conjugate through the Hodge structure

concepts.name: Function-field test of the MP4 headline: over F_q, point counts + functional equation + non-negative integer closed-point counts (an Euler product with positive multiplicities, which implies Ihara’s constraints) do NOT induce the Hodge sign; the sign on the Frobenius-graph Gram comes from the surface C×C (Hodge index), not from the counts
aliases: F_q test of the lead conjecture
concepts.plain: Over a finite field, you can write down fake zeta functions whose point counts look perfectly healthy (all positive, with the right symmetry) but whose zeros are off the circle. So the counts alone do not force the sign; what does is the geometry of the surface C×C.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Gram of ⟨H, V, Γ₀..Γ_M⟩ from counts only (Γ_m·Γ_n = q^min N_|m−n|, N₀ = 2−2g; Hallouin–Perret arXiv 1409.2357 Lemma 3); primitive Gram −q^min Σα^|m−n| is −Toeplitz(Σ u^k), so #positive eigenvalues = #σ-2-cycles (real pair 1, quartet 2). [N] 15 point-counted curves (q, g) = (7,2), (11,2), (13,2), (7,3), (11,3): full inertia (1, 2g+1), primitive part NSD rank 2g (max eig ≤ 1e−13). Exact census g = 2, |a| ≤ 6q, |b| ≤ 20q (no hits on the border), a_d exact for d ≤ 40: off-circle FE integer polynomials with all a_d ≥ 0: 675 (q = 7), 2935 (q = 11; = TAA Lemma 109), 4961 (q = 13); on-circle 205/401/513. DH-like pencil (1−λ)P₁ + λP₂ of two genus-3 curves over F₁₁: off-circle for λ ∈ [0.233, 0.9725] (4 roots, 2 positive primitive eigenvalues); genus-2 pencils and (7,3) stay on the circle (sign kept although a_d non-integral). Consequence for MP4: 'Euler product' read as counting data is insufficient; the conjecture can only hold in a geometric reading (an object whose square carries Hodge index).
pitfalls: a_d ≥ 0 checked for d ≤ 40 only (exact integers).
Not a refutation of the conjecture in Deninger’s conjectured cohomology: it rules out the reading “numerical Euler-product data ⇒ sign”.
Framework (Gram of Frobenius graphs, geometric vs arithmetic facet) is Hallouin–Perret’s; TAA Lemma 109/TAA Lemma 137/TAA Lemma 141/TAA Lemma 152 had the count-positive ghosts.

concepts.name: Connes–Consani sites
concepts.plain: Topos-theoretic candidate for Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Arithmetic site and scaling site (CC14, CC16): a square exists, with Ψ_λ and s(f,f) = D•D (TAA Lemma 30), but no H¹, RR or Hodge index on it (TAA Lemma 65). TAA Lemma 147: their proved RRs are 1-dimensional; RR on the square is open (CC18).
numbers: TAA Lemma 158: CC16 §6 (opened): ℤ_min ⊗_B ℤ_min, reduced square with Newton polygons, points over ℝ_max⁺ = product of points (Prop 6.11), Ψ(λ) congruences

concepts.name: Laguerre's formula: angle = (1/2i) log cross-ratio with the circular points
concepts.plain: The angle between two lines is read off at infinity, from how the lines sit relative to two imaginary points; the metric lives at infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(ℓ₁,ℓ₂) = (1/2i) log CR(ℓ₁,ℓ₂; I, J), I, J = (1 : ±i : 0), isotropic lines y = ±ix; CR = (m₁−i)(m₂+i)/((m₁+i)(m₂−i)) = e^{2i(θ₁−θ₂)} (TAA Lemma 152 NUM 7.1e−16, 2000 pairs). The ½: θ is defined mod π (ℝP¹). The Euclidean metric is the pair {I, J} at infinity (the absolute). Resolves J. W. McGreevy's paradox: lines through 0 are not parallel at infinity (Riemann sphere: they meet again at ∞ with the same angle, opposite orientation; ℝP²: distinct points at infinity); the angle at 0 becomes a separation at infinity.
pitfalls: Sign/orientation conventions: with CR as written Laguerre gives θ₁ − θ₂ mod π; only |θ| mod π is canonical (TAA Lemma 152, correction 9).
Laguerre 1853 (Nouv. Ann. 12, 57–66): Numdam record and first page opened; the formula’s place in the paper not seen.

rels.note: rapidity ½ log CR vs ½ log q

concepts.name: Pole plane / Tate poles at s = 0, 1
concepts.plain: The two poles of ξ(s) at s = 0 and 1 give the reference plane; subtracting them is what makes a form "relative".
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 142: the relative Gram on translates uses the pole terms f̂(0), f̂(1) (zero-free entries). Pole of ζ at s = 1 is the 𝕃-ray; the functional equation pairs it with s = 0.

concepts.name: Measure versus metric: the product formula gives an invariant measure, not an invariant metric
concepts.plain: By the product formula, multiplication by nonzero rationals preserves Haar measure on the idele classes, and the closed orbits have lengths log p. What it does not give is an invariant metric, i.e. a Hermitian structure: Spec ℤ comes with a density, and that is exactly why it is not yet Kähler. The lift the shape list asks for would turn that Haar measure into a Hermitian metric for which the pole line is self-dual and the graphs of multiplication by n are anti-self-dual. A positive Hodge star commuting with the flow would give RH (Deninger, ICM 1998, p. 169), so such a lift stated as positivity is equivalent to RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Measure versus metric: the product formula gives an invariant measure, not an invariant metric. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma). Cited: Connes, Selecta Math. 5 (1999) 29–106; Deninger, Doc. Math. Extra Vol. ICM 1998 I, 163–186.
concepts.formula: |x|_∞ ∏_p |x|_p = 1 ⇒ ℚ^× preserves Haar measure on 𝔸^×; C_ℚ ≅ ℝ_{>0} × Ẑ^×; no ℚ^×-invariant metric is supplied
concepts.uncertain: The lift itself is Open (Conjecture-level); it would need Deninger’s conjectured cohomology, which has not been constructed.
pitfalls: Random Euler products have no pole, so they are not Haar at s = 1; Davenport–Heilbronn has no Euler product, hence no adelic density [Heuristic / Theorem].

concepts.name: Cartan involution / compact unitary group
concepts.plain: A positive involution is the same thing as a compact (rotation-type) symmetry group; Albert lists the possible kinds.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Positive involution ⇔ compact unitary group (TAA Lemma 99, Milne Prop 1.20); Rosati = Cartan θ_J on commutant of J; Weil numbers generate CM or totally real fields (TAA Lemma 136); Albert types I–IV.
pitfalls: Abelian scaling has only an outer Cartan U(1); zeros-as-angles = RH (circular, TAA Lemma 99).

rels.note: no compact Hodge circle for ℚ (TAA Lemma 100)

concepts.name: On a compact manifold a flow conformal on TF with factor e^{αt} has α = 0 (Jacobian e^{αt}, volume conserved); ζ needs α = 1, so the phase space must be solenoidal, with leaf expansion balanced by contraction of a totally disconnected transversal (product formula as volume balance, in Deninger’s elliptic-curve example)
concepts.plain: A flow on a closed, finite manifold cannot stretch everything sideways forever, because the total volume has to stay the same. The Riemann zeta function needs exactly such stretching. So Deninger's space has to be a solenoid, in which the stretching along the leaves is paid for by shrinking in a dust-like p-adic direction.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] one-line proof (TAA Lemma 174 Thm V). [C] Deninger 2005 Cor. 5.5 Rem. 2 and arXiv 0709.2801 state that the conditions force α = 0; Rem. 3: finitely generated orbit-length group, infinitely generated needs fixed points; §7: solenoid (C ×_Γ T_πΓ) ×_{p^Z} R*_+ with metric e^t Re ξη̄ has α = 1. [H] multiplication by π scales leaf area by q and has index q on T_πΓ.
pitfalls: Volume balance on solenoids is shown only for Deninger’s elliptic-curve example (Heuristic in general).

concepts.name: Deligne's route: Lefschetz pencils, monodromy and Rankin's tensor-power trick
concepts.plain: Deligne proved the Weil conjectures without the Hodge index theorem, but still with a positivity: Rankin’s positivity of coefficients of tensor powers.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Deligne, Weil I (Publ. IHÉS 43, 1974, 273–307): RH over F_q without a Hodge index theorem — Lefschetz pencils and monodromy (SGA 7) reduce to a local system on a curve; Rankin's trick (Rankin 1939) bounds weights through L-functions of tensor powers. It still uses positivity: of the coefficients of those L-functions (TAA Lemma 152, correction 4). For ζ no tensor-power analogue is known to give more than zero-free regions (Heuristic, BR-4).
concepts.uncertain: Numdam record and reference list opened; the argument itself is standard knowledge (BIB), not re-read.
pitfalls: 'No positivity' is wrong: Rankin's coefficient positivity is used; what is avoided is a Hodge index theorem (TAA Lemma 152, correction 4).

rels.note: a second proof of RH over F_q
replaces Hodge index by coefficient positivity

concepts.name: Selberg eigenvalue conjecture ↔ mass shell λ = ¼ + r²
concepts.plain: The Laplacian on the modular surface is positive, which forces its eigenvalues onto a line; whether the first eigenvalue is at least ¼ for all congruence groups is still open.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Δ ≥ 0 on L²(Γ∖ℍ), λ = s(1−s) real ⇒ s ∈ [0,1] or Re s = ½; for SL₂(ℤ) λ₁ = ¼ + 9.53369…² ≈ 91.14 > ¼, so the spectral zeros of Selberg's zeta (cusp forms) lie on Re s = ½. Selberg's conjecture λ₁ ≥ ¼ for congruence subgroups: open; Selberg 3/16 (1965), Kim–Sarnak 975/4096 = ¼ − (7/64)² ≈ 0.2380 (appendix to Kim, JAMS 16 (2003) 139–183; bib data Crossref, bound via secondary sources). Shape analogy: ρ(1−ρ) = ¼ + γ² ≥ ¼ real ⇔ ρ on the line (or real) (Analogy).

concepts.name: Maxwell construction / convex effective potential
aliases: convex hull of a double well
concepts.plain: Doing the Legendre transform twice fills in a double well with a flat floor; this convexity comes for free only from a positive measure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The effective potential Γ = (log Z)* is convex automatically (a Legendre transform); for a double well the biconjugate V** is the convex envelope, flat between the two minima (Maxwell's common tangent; TAA Lemma 153 figure). log ∫e^{Jφ}dμ is convex in J by Hölder when μ ≥ 0; for a signed μ it can fail (TAA Lemma 153 example μ = ½δ₋₁ − 0.6δ₀ + ½δ₁). Physics citation left uncited (none opened).
pitfalls: No physics source opened; Hölder argument proved inline (TAA Lemma 153 §2).

rels.note: convexity needs a positive measure: Weil’s form has signed prime terms

concepts.name: Products grow linearly (2n), not quadratically
concepts.plain: Sections on naive products of Spec ℤ̄ grow only linearly in n (slope 2); a genuine surface needs quadratic growth, which forces the rank to grow with n.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147 [T/N]: product sandwich ⌈log₂ #⌉ ≤ dim_𝕊(box) ≤ Σ dims, exact = additive bound in 6/6 boxes; fixed rank ⇒ linear: Spec ℤ̄² fits 1.99993n + 2.0009 (vs 2n + 4); quadratic growth ⇒ rank ≳ n. Same as TAA Lemma 145 Thm linear (fixed-rank lattice ⇒ h⁰ linear, h⁰/n = 2.000 at n = 400).

concepts.name: Weight–monodromy conjecture (Deligne): status
concepts.plain: Deligne conjectured that the monodromy filtration and Frobenius weights match; it is proved in characteristic p and in many but not all mixed-characteristic cases.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: For X proper smooth over a local field, Frobenius weights on gr_j^N H^i are i + j. Proved: equal characteristic (Deligne, Weil II 1980, over a curve; general char p via Terasoma, Ito); dim ≤ 2 in mixed characteristic (Rapoport–Zink + de Jong); p-adically uniformized varieties (Ito; Dat); cases of Shimura varieties; set-theoretic complete intersections in projective smooth toric varieties (Scholze, Publ. IHÉS 116, 2012, Thm 1.14). Open in general in mixed characteristic. (Curves and abelian varieties: curves are in dim ≤ 2; abelian varieties BIB, not opened.)

concepts.name: Yoneda specification
concepts.plain: Specify the object by its properties (Ax1–Ax3).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 90: bare Hom sets do not determine an object (ℚ vs ℚ^(N)); naturality needed; representability ⇒ uniqueness/functoriality, presupposes positivity if it is an axiom. TAA Lemma 98 Prop 6.1: representable ⇒ unique; 𝔉(pt) ≠ ∅ ⇒ RH; "representability is the whole battle" (TAA Lemma 98, correction 19). TAA Lemma 137: T_W with Ax1–Ax3; existence open.

concepts.name: Boosts close into rotations only in imaginary time: Thomas–Wigner (boost commutators are rotations), Cartan duality H³ = SO(3,1)/SO(3) ↔ S³ = SO(4)/SO(3) (p ↦ ip), and Bisognano–Wichmann/Unruh: the Rindler boost is the modular flow of the wedge algebra; its Wick rotation is a Euclidean rotation whose 2π period is the KMS condition (T = a/2π) — arithmetic counterpart: ζ(β) as the primon-gas / Bost–Connes partition function, p^{−it} the time evolution
concepts.plain: A boost never becomes a rotation by moving it around space. It becomes one when time is made imaginary, and then the required 2π period is exactly thermal equilibrium at temperature a/2π. ζ is the partition function of a gas of primes, so the closest precise version of the idea is thermal.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: [T] Thomas–Wigner: boosts 0.9 (x) and 0.7 (y) compose to boost × rotation by 16.1546° = 2 arctan(tanh(η₁/2) tanh(η₂/2)). Rindler (t,x) = ρ(sinh η, cosh η) → ρ(sin τ, cos τ), period 2π. [C] Bisognano–Wichmann J. Math. Phys. 16 (1975) 985–1007, 17 (1976) 303–321; Unruh Phys. Rev. D 14 (1976) 870–892; Bost–Connes Selecta 1 (1995) 411–457 (abstract: partition function ζ, phase transition at β = 1); Julia 1990; Spector CMP 127 (1990) 239–252. Corrections: a boost subgroup is non-compact on any manifold (dS₃ isometry group SO(3,1) non-compact); K → iK is a change of real form, not a transport; holonomy on Riemannian S³ lies in SO(3) because the metric is definite. [H] 'boosts made global rotations' = thermal (KMS) periodicity, not topology. [O] does a KMS/modular structure give Krein definiteness for ζ? DH: no Euler product ⇒ no primon gas (ghost-sensitive point). TAA Lemma 164: the compact pieces are J (ℤ/2) and the KMS imaginary-time circle; the real-time modular group is ℝ (BC: n^{it}, not periodic).
pitfalls: Compactness of a one-parameter subgroup is intrinsic.
KMS periodicity is a property of the state, not of the group.

rels.note: no Euler product ⇒ no primon gas

concepts.name: Organizing split: ghost-blind = phase, ghost-sensitive = sign
concepts.plain: Every test that ghosts pass is about phase/unitarity; every test that catches a ghost is about the sign of a spectral weight, and for ζ that sign is RH.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 synthesis: functional equation, |φ| = 1, cocycles, Hecke, cusp positivity are ghost-blind (Ax3); Lagarias sign, Weil sign, Rosati sign are ghost-sensitive (Ax2) and ⇔ RH for ζ. Every ghost-sensitive global quadratic statement for Spec ℤ found so far is a restatement.
numbers: DH: FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8
pitfalls: An organizing observation, not a theorem: "sign" items for curves are theorems, for ζ restatements.

concepts.name: Definite (Kepler/apsidal) vs gyroscopic (TAA Lemma 4) stability: TAA Lemma 4 has indefinite energy held by the work-free Coriolis J; opposite Krein signs collide at Gascheau–Routh μ = 0.0385209 (Hamiltonian–Hopf quadruple); any dissipation destroys it (Kelvin–Tait–Chetaev); Weil positivity says ζ-type stability must be definite — DH ≈ TAA Lemma 4 past Routh
concepts.plain: A planet near periapsis is stable because its energy is a positive bowl. A Trojan at TAA Lemma 4 sits on a hilltop and is kept there only by the sideways Coriolis force, which does no work. That kind of stability breaks when two modes of opposite sign collide or when any friction is added. Weil's criterion says ζ's zeros would need the first, positive kind.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: [T] TAA Lemma 4 linearization λ⁴ + λ² + (27/4)μ(1−μ) = 0 (residual 9e−8); μ_R = (1 − √(23/27))/2 = 0.0385208965; μ = 0.04: ±0.0675 ± 0.7103i. Ω-Hessian positive definite (TAA Lemma 4 = max of −Ω); quadratic energy signature (2,2); Krein signs of the slow/fast modes −/+ (μ =,.038). Coriolis −2ω × v ⊥ v (zero power; skew block, no contribution to the gap form or energy). Linear damping −γv: max Re λ =.0018 (γ =.001),.018 (.01),.086 (.05) at μ =. Linearized motion epicyclic: long period √(27μ/4) libration + short ≈ 1 epicycle; tadpole/horseshoe are large-amplitude nonlinear (horseshoe encloses TAA Lemma 3, TAA Lemma 4, TAA Lemma 5; Dermott–Murray 1981). Kepler: a periapsis perturbation gives a nearby conic (orbital, not Lyapunov, stability: separation 0.012 → 0.150 over t ≤ 200; linear oscillator bounded). [C] Gascheau 1843 (via Sicardy 2010), Routh 1875 PLMS 6, 86–97; BKMR 1994 AIHP 11, 37–90. [R] Weil: RH ⇔ positivity → definite type; [A/H] FE/quartet symmetry = work-free J (ghost-blind, DH has it); DH ghosts ↔ quadruples past Routh; cycle 3: Weil Gram index 2 per resolved quartet.
pitfalls: Kepler apsides are not equilibria (TAA Lemma 161, correction 13).
Tadpole/horseshoe are nonlinear; linear motion is epicyclic (TAA Lemma 161, correction 14).
DH ↔ TAA Lemma 4 is Analogy; 27/4 has no arithmetic meaning claimed.

concepts.name: Must-fail-for-DH acceptance test
concepts.plain: Any future Riemann–Roch on the square must be false for Davenport–Heilbronn; otherwise it cannot prove RH. So it has to use the Euler product.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: All H⁰-side objects are built from ℤ ⊂ 𝔸_ℚ and are ghost-blind; the topological side s(f,f) is ghost-sensitive (TAA Lemma 142: DH-location ghost positive from L* = 3.45, actual DH from 4.70). Hence an RR theorem on the square must FAIL for DH ⇒ must use the Euler product / ring structure (necessary condition, proposed acceptance test, TAA Lemma 147).
concepts.uncertain: Proposed acceptance test.
pitfalls: A necessary condition only.

An argument must use more than the functional equation (Davenport–Heilbronn). The Euler product is one such input but not the only one: Weng zeta functions satisfy RH with a functional equation and no Euler product.

concepts.name: BRST / Gupta–Bleuler physical quotient
concepts.plain: Remove null and negative-norm states to get a positive physical space — as U^⊥ in Hodge index.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 115: BRST structure exact over F_q and ℚ [T]; "no ghosts" ⇔ RH [R]; missing positive V ≅ H¹ (Hilbert–Pólya) ⇒ restatement. TAA Lemma 146 §3: Gupta–Bleuler F₁^⊥/F₁ ≅ U^⊥; the BRST quartet decouples but the ghost quartet survives. PM-3 (BRST complex with H(Q) = U^⊥) open. Kugo–Ojima (TAA Lemma 146 §1, Analogy): BRST quartets are the closest physics analogue of ζ’s zero quartets, but a BRST quartet DECOUPLES (its ker Q part is null and is quotiented out), while a ghost quartet SURVIVES in the relative quotient with two positive directions (TAA Lemma 142). Higgs/ghost cancellation: which modes are physical vs null = the ghost question; Analogy only.
concepts.uncertain: PM-3 open.
pitfalls: PM-3 is open.

concepts.name: Weil template, standing assignment (Missing Piece v5): Deninger's foliation = one factor (½), the Connes–Consani square = the product (½ ⊗ ½), 1 ⊕ 0 = the splitting of the product by the ample class, cusp part split off
aliases: seeing the square from the cusp
concepts.plain: In Weil's proof a curve is one factor, the surface C×C is the product, and the ample class splits the product. Over the integers Deninger's foliation plays the factor, the Connes–Consani square the product, and the splitting is what is missing.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Over F_q [Theorem]: factor C (H¹), product C×C, ample-class splitting ℝH ⊕ H^⊥; on S² × S², L_{X×Y} = L_X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ L_Y gives ½ ⊗ ½ = 1 ⊕ 0, triplet = H⁰, ample class, H⁴, singlet = primitive H² class, negative (signature (1,1)). Over ℤ [Analogy, adopted as standing]: Deninger's foliation / H¹ of Deninger's conjectured cohomology = the factor; the Connes–Consani square of the arithmetic site = the product; 1 ⊕ 0 = a splitting of the product (not a separate space), which is the missing piece. Cusp reading (exact in parts): the split-off part pt × C, C × pt = MP0 boundary terms = poles of ζ at 0, 1 = the Eisenstein/cusp constant term (the ζ factor of L(Δ×Δ,s) = ζ(s−11)L(Sym²Δ,s), whose pole comes from the cusp constant term); MP4(2) is definiteness on the primitive part orthogonal to exactly these. Kepler/KS: r = u†u is the singlet; the collision r = 0 is Moser's point at infinity (Analogy).
pitfalls: Roles were first stated reversed (CC square as ½ ⊗ ½ and the foliation as 1 ⊕ 0); the foliation is the factor, 1 ⊕ 0 a splitting.

concepts.name: Γ, the width of a zero: FWHM of its Breit–Wigner line
concepts.plain: Each zero shows up as a bell-shaped line; its width at the critical line is twice its distance from the line. RH says every width is zero: every line becomes a spike.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] On Re s = σ each zero ρ = β+iγ contributes to Re ξ′/ξ the signed line (σ−β)/((σ−β)²+(t−γ)²): FWHM 2|σ−β|, height 1/(σ−β), area π·sgn(σ−β) (Hadamard; TAA Lemma 146). [R] Γ_ρ := 2|β−½| = lim_{σ→½} FWHM (signed Γ± = 2(β−½); FE mirror has −Γ±); s = ½+iE puts ρ at E = γ − iΓ±/2. RH ⇔ all Γ_ρ = 0 ⇔ every line sharpens to πδ_γ as σ↓½. Γ is a limit, not observable on σ = ½ itself (Re ξ′/ξ ≡ 0 there by the FE; TAA Lemma 154, correction 6). 'Stable vs decaying' is convention-dependent; invariant: unitary state vs non-unitary ±Γ pair (in u = log x the ghost grows like e^{Γu/2}; TAA Lemma 154, correction 3). [N] TAA Lemma 154: ζ (5 zeros) and DH on-line: measured FWHM = 2d to 3.3e−7 rel over 13 lines d ∈ [0.01, 0.5], area π to 6e−7; DH ghosts: near line FWHM 2|d − (β−½)| (≤ 3e−6), flips to a gain line for d < β−½, → Γ = 0.617 / 0.302 from below (0.5970 / 0.2816 at d = 0.01; TAA Lemma 154, correction 2: not 'at least Γ'); visible feature width ≈ ½(β−½) constant, depth ≈ 2d/(β−½)² → 0; planted ghost (0.8, 40) identical. [N] TAA Lemma 155: Γ recovered without a zero list — Γ̂ = 2(β̂−½) = 0.61703, 0.30166 from the ghost map's phase slope (coefficients + Γ-factor + FE); exact comb from the theta AFE agrees with TAA Lemma 154 to 1e−12. Recorded in TAA Lemma 155 §0; certification in TAA Lemma 156. TAA Lemma 156 [N, rigorous]: certified (Arb) Γ₁ = 0.617034364913274771106 ± 9e−22, Γ₂ = 0.30166016121947416481 ± 3e−21; [T given certificates] flips at d* = β−½ in (0.30,0.35), (0.15,0.20); ζ targets simple on the line ⇒ FWHM 2d exact; ghost FWHM → Γ from below; [N] TAA Lemma 154 fits certified to first order (rel ≤ 1.6e−5; ghost 2 ≤ 6.3e−5 after tail subtraction). TAA Lemma 157: Γ_ρ = |⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v,v⟩| = |(1−ρ) − ρ̄|, the dual−adjoint gap (Thm); DH ρ₃ 0.148712100902, ρ₄ 0.448515389254 (from TAA Lemma 156 enclosures).

Decaying vs growing depends on the sign convention; the FE pairs ±Γ (TAA Lemma 154, correction 3).
Hilbert–Pólya in widths is content-free without a natural operator (TAA Lemma 154, correction 5).
TAA Lemma 159: reading Γ as entropy production gives an empty second law (Γ ≥ 0 by definition); RH = Γ ≡ 0 is a reversibility (equality) statement.

concepts.name: Mass shell / even Ξ: s(1−s) = ¼ + t²
concepts.plain: Rewrite the zeros as 'masses squared': RH says every one of them is a real number at least ¼, like a stable particle.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Ξ(t) = ξ(½+it) even and real ⇒ Ξ(t) = F(t²); RH ⇔ every root z = t² of F is real and positive ⇔ every nontrivial ρ(1−ρ) = σ(1−σ) + t² + it(1−2σ) is real and ≥ ¼ (then ρ(1−ρ) = ¼ + z). Dictionary: mass² = ¼ = ρ² (half density), momentum t; off-line pair = complex mass² (DH: z₀ = 7344.283 − 52.879i); real zero in (0,1) = tachyon. Connes 1999: 'positivity properties of Δ = D(1−D)', Selberg Laplacian λ = s(1−s) ≥ ¼.

concepts.name: Two conditions: primitive positivity and pole channel
concepts.plain: On each finite section, Weil positivity splits into (a) positivity on the primitive part (functions whose Mellin transform vanishes at the two pole points), which is Castelnuovo-Severi / Hodge index on the primitive part and is where off-line zeros and finite-field fakes show up, and (b) positivity of the even and odd pole margins, which are exactly zero in the finite-field template, tend to zero generically, and are blind to off-line zeros. (a) and (b) on all sections is equivalent to RH. What is missing is a source for (a). In the finite-field model the pole channel is zero only once the graphs span the fibre classes; with an incomplete span a fake fails first in the pole channel, so the pole condition is not pure normalisation on finite sections.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Two conditions: primitive positivity and pole channel

concepts.name: The arithmetic equation of state: primon gas / Bost–Connes dictionary (T, U, S, C, Ω; KMS time; volume options; P_X(β))
concepts.plain: ζ is the partition function of a free gas of primes. Temperature, energy, entropy and heat capacity are exact; volume and pressure are not built in. With a cutoff at X the 'pressure' is a prime count whose smooth part comes from the pole and whose wiggles are the zeros.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] Primon gas (Julia 1990, Spector 1990; Wikipedia 'Primon gas', opened): Fock basis |n⟩, H|n⟩ = log n|n⟩, Z(β) = Tr e^{−βH} = ζ(β), β > 1; Hagedorn divergence at β = 1 (density of states e^E). Bost–Connes (BC95 Thm 5, opened): unique KMS_β for 0 < β < 1 (type III₁), for β > 1 extreme KMS_β indexed by embeddings of ℚ^cycl (type I∞), normalization 1/ζ(β), T_c = 1, Gal(ℚ^cycl/ℚ) broken for β > 1. Sums over all occupation numbers at fugacity 1 = grand canonical, μ = 0: Ω = −T log ζ(β) = Σ_p T log(1 − p^{−β}) (independent modes). U = −ζ′/ζ(β), S = ∂(T log Z)/∂T = log ζ + βU, C = β²(log ζ)″ = β² Var(log n). [N] β = 2: log Z 0.497700, U 0.569961, S 1.637622, C 3.537927 (residual of S ≤ 2e−30); C(1.01) = 10200.8. [T/N] No volume: with mode cutoff p ≤ X, log Z_X(2) → log ζ(2) = 0.49770 (per mode 7.5e−7 at X = 10⁷: not extensive); log Z_X(1) = γ + log log X + o(1) (Mertens; 3.35717 vs 3.35716 at 10⁷). So 'Ω = −PV' is a name, not an identity. Time (KMS strip, BC95 §1): σ_t(μ_n) = n^{it}μ_n, Tr(e^{−βH}e^{itH}) = ζ(β − it); critical line = β = ½, inside the Hagedorn-divergent region where ζ is a continuation, not a trace. [Def + T] Energy-cutoff 'pressure' P_X(β) := Σ_{n≤X} Λ(n)n^{−β}/log n; smooth part Li_β(X) = ∫₂^X u^{−β}du/log u comes from the pole (displaced reference, TAA Lemma 146 buoyancy); fluctuation P_X − Li_β is the explicit-formula sum over zeros; RH ⇔ fluctuation O(X^{½−β+ε}) (von Koch type, Restatement). [N] β = ½: fluctuation 0.268, 0.292, 0.290, 0.246, 0.247 at X = 10³…10⁷. Earlier material: density = Hagedorn density of states; half density = β = ½ weights n^{−½} (TAA Lemma 145); mass shell β(1−β) = ¼ at β = ½ (TAA Lemma 150); buoyancy = pole subtraction (TAA Lemma 146) [Analogy for the names].
numbers: log Z_X(1) − log log X → γ (3.35717 at 10⁷)
pitfalls: 'Pressure × volume' is only the name of −Ω: the primon gas has no volume and is not extensive (TAA Lemma 159, correction 2).
The critical line β = ½ is in the Hagedorn-divergent region; there Z is a continuation (TAA Lemma 159, correction 4).
Every T,P,V,S object is a Legendre transform of one generating function: a dictionary is a change of variables unless a positivity law does work (TAA Lemma 159, correction 8).

concepts.name: Composite leakage: −F′/F supported on prime powers ⇔ Euler product (unique factorization); DH leaks first at n = 6 (c₆ = 1.9364; also 12, 14, 18, 21, …); along the pencil leakage is 0 exactly at λ = 0, 1 and |c₆| ≈ 7.1λ; Saias–Weingartner ⇒ every 0 < λ < 1 has infinitely many off-line zeros, so ghost births start at λ = 0⁺ as T → ∞; truncated Weil forms (primes ≤ P = 5…13): ζ, χ₅ fail just after log of the next prime, DH at 1.90 for all P (c₆ at log 6)
concepts.plain: A true L-function's log-derivative only has terms at prime powers; that is unique factorization in coefficient form. DH has extra terms at composites, starting at 6 = 2·3, and these extra terms are exactly what turn on as you slide away from the true L-function, at the same time as zeros start leaving the line.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] elementary: log F = Σ c_n/log n · n^{−s}. [C] Saias–Weingartner Acta Arith. 140 (2009): periodic-coefficient series not P·L_χ have ≫T zeros in 1/2 < σ1 < σ < σ2 ≤ 1+η; pencil not P·L_ψ by a_p² ≠ a_{p²} at p ≡ 2 mod 5 (4λ(1−λ)W ≠ 0). [N] n ≤ 3000, 201 λ: leakage.049 (λ=.005),.233 (.033),.696 (1/2); symmetric λ ↔ 1−λ. Weil truncation table. As an RH test: 'has an Euler product' restated (L(χ) pass; GRH open).

concepts.name: Passive arithmetic response of 32a1 (Λ′/Λ as a Foster function)
concepts.plain: For the CM curve y² = x³ − x (conductor 32, root number +1) take Z = Λ′/Λ of the completed L-function, critical line Re s = 1. On the line Z is purely imaginary (lossless, phase ±90° everywhere), by the functional equation and real coefficients. Lagarias's theorem on admissible zero sets gives: GRH for this L-function holds iff Re Z > 0 on Re s > 1, i.e. the response is passive. Under GRH, Z(1+w) = Σ 2w/(w²+γ²) over zeros γ > 0, one lossless resonator per zero; off the line each has damping 2(σ−1), and an off-line zero would be a gain resonator. The absorption peaks near the line sit at the zeros, not at primes. Inert primes enter only at second order, with their own poles on Re s = 1/2. No finite Euler product is passive near the line. Kramers–Kronig and the 90° crossing hold for gain media too, so they do not supply the sign. This restates GRH; it does not prove it.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Passive arithmetic response of 32a1 (Λ′/Λ as a Foster function)

concepts.name: Compressed slogan: RH is the Hodge index theorem for Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ, holding with zero margin (Λ = 0); restates Bombieri's 'general index theorem' question; zero margin = dBN time, not a null vector
concepts.plain: Weil turned RH into a positivity statement, and Bombieri asked whether some index theorem proves it. The de Bruijn–Newman constant says that positivity holds with no room to spare.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Compressed slogan: RH is the Hodge index theorem for Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ, holding with zero margin (Λ = 0); restates Bombieri's 'general index theorem' question; zero margin = dBN time, not a null vector
concepts.formula: RH ⇔ Weil form ≥ 0 (pole terms = polarization); Λ ≥ 0 (Rodgers–Tao) ⇒ RH ⇔ Λ = 0
pitfalls: Building the pole term as a genuine ⋆-polarization is Open (Deninger).

concepts.name: Density × density: Weil’s form read off the diagonal and its log n translates
concepts.plain: The prime side of ζ is a density on the log-scale line, dΛ = Σ Λ(n) δ(x − log n). Weil’s form pairs two half-densities g(x), g(y) against a distribution that depends only on x − y. That distribution is not supported on the diagonal alone: it lives on the diagonal (the archimedean term and the pole, which is a smooth Haar part) and on its translates x − y = ±log n, with weights Λ(n)/√n. Those translates are the graphs of multiplication by n, the analogue of the graphs of Frobenius powers on C × C, whose Gram matrix over F_q is Toeplitz (Hallouin–Perret). The two pole functionals are pairings with the Haar half-densities x^(±½), so quotienting by the pole line (Gupta–Bleuler) is quotienting by "pure Haar". Positivity of the pairing is Weil’s criterion, i.e. RH.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: Density × density: Weil’s form read off the diagonal and its log n translates. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma). Cited: Hallouin–Perret, Trans. AMS 372 (2019) 5409–5451.
concepts.formula: ⟨g|g⟩_W = ∫∫ g(x) ḡ(y) dΔ(x − y), dΔ supported on {x = y} ∪ {x − y = ±log n}, weight Λ(n)/√n on the translates
numbers: ζ, Perron mode of Z_ℓ, box grid h = 0.02: net/pole E/P = 7.9e−3, 1.7e−3, 1.1e−3 at ℓ = 2, 4, 6, with n₋(W) = 0
one prime dropped (2, 3, 5 or 7): E/P = 1.3e−2 to 2.0e−1 (1.7–80 times worse) and n₋(W) = 1–52; the failure shows up in the primitive part, not as a sign flip of the pole channel
dropping p multiplies ζ by (1 − p^(−s)), which has zeros on Re s = 0 [Theorem]
pitfalls: "Read off the diagonal" should be "read off the diagonal and its log n translates".
That the four lifts (F_q → ℚ, local → global, Spec ℤ → Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ, quotient → whole space) are one move is an Analogy; only the finite-field statement (graphs against the diagonal) is a Theorem.

concepts.name: Why the area is π: the circle in every zero count (Basel as common origin)
concepts.plain: The π in each zero’s area is the circle’s π, coming from the geometry of complex numbers; the same circle gives Euler’s π²/6, but the zeros do not explain π.
concepts.label: Restatement
concepts.core: [T] ∫ a/(a²+x²)dx = π sgn a = angle subtended by ℝ at ia = half of ∮dz/z = 2πi; P_a = (1/π)a/(a²+x²) is harmonic measure, Cayley-equivalent to the disk Poisson kernel (mass 1, NUM 40 digits); 2π = circumference/radius. [R] Area is a dimensionless invariant of the complex structure (scale- and coordinate-free yes), as C/d is of a round metric. Direction: the circle puts π into every zero count; the zeros do not derive π (TAA Lemma 154, correction 9). [T] Euler: ζ(2) = π²/6, ζ(2k) = rational·π^{2k} (sin product / π cot πz; NUM sanity ζ(2) − π²/6 = 2e−41). [R] Basel and the ±π area share an origin (the circle); NOT (±π)²/6 from residue areas: ζ(2k) is archimedean (Γ-factor, trivial zeros; ζ(1−2k) = −B_{2k}/2k) (TAA Lemma 154, correction 10). [C/O] ζ(3) irrational (Apéry, BIB); rationality of ζ(3)/π³ OPEN (TAA Lemma 154, correction 11); even/odd ↔ ghost-blind/sensitive is Heuristic at most. The locked ratio is the complex structure J, which also defines the Weil operator C = i^{p−q} (OS/Wick reading Analogy, TAA Lemma 153, correction 10).
pitfalls: Not a derivation of π from zeros or RH (TAA Lemma 154, correction 9).
ζ(2) is not a product of resonance areas (TAA Lemma 154, correction 10).
ζ(3)/π³ irrational is unproved (TAA Lemma 154, correction 11).

concepts.label: Open
