concepts.name: Hilbert–Pólya
concepts.plain: Find a self-adjoint operator with spectrum the γ’s.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: Standard program: a self-adjoint/unitary realization with spectrum the γ’s would give RH. TAA verdicts: spinor route = Hilbert–Pólya in Clifford dress (TAA Lemma 104); 2B″ + ½ needs an inner product (TAA Lemma 105, LP80 "all that is missing is an appropriate inner product"); missing positive V ≅ H¹ (TAA Lemma 115); circular if the inner product is Weil’s form (TAA Lemma 138 R2); lossless Heaviside realization = Hilbert–Pólya [O] (TAA Lemma 144 HS-F). TAA Lemma 154: 'all widths Γ_ρ vanish' ⇔ RH ⇔ the γ's are the spectrum of some self-adjoint operator — content-free without a natural operator (TAA Lemma 154, correction 5).

concepts.name: Arithmetic Castelnuovo object (C1–C4)
concepts.plain: Requirements an arithmetic surface would need to reproduce the curve proof.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 136: an arithmetic Castelnuovo object needs (C1) infinite H¹, (C2) positive involution, (C3) u_t u_t† = e^t, (C4) positivity proved without zeros; circularity flagged (TAA Lemma 106). TAA Lemma 138: the Čech 2-class supplies C2–C3 structure but not the sign. TAA Lemma 147: the decisive missing objects are H¹ on the square, an NS ⊋ U containing Ψ_λ, and quadratic RR.

concepts.name: No Riemann–Roch for C_ℚ × C_ℚ (the square is open)
concepts.plain: There is no Riemann–Roch theorem for the square of the scaling site; Connes–Consani themselves list H¹ on the square, and hence RR there, as open.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 147, correction 2: "their RR for the square / C_ℚ × C_ℚ, if it exists" — it does not exist; CC18 states H¹ on the square of the scaling site, and hence RR there, is open. TAA Lemma 147 (iv): decisive missing objects = H¹ on the square, an intersection theory putting Ψ_λ into an NS larger than U, and quadratic RR.
pitfalls: Do not cite a CC Riemann–Roch on the square: none exists (TAA Lemma 147, correction 2).

concepts.name: Conjecture: a no-ghost-type polarisation forced by an algebra with central term 24
concepts.plain: What survives of the 1/24 idea is a conjecture: an operator algebra acting on the window space, with a central term fixed by 24 (an analogue of the Virasoro central charge), whose constraints force the window form to have exactly one negative square for ζ (the pole as the single "tachyon") and none for Δ. Nothing known constructs such an algebra. A cheap test of the "tachyon = pole" reading: E₁₂ against Δ in the window model.
concepts.label: Conjecture
concepts.core: Conjecture: a no-ghost-type polarisation forced by an algebra with central term 24. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: Prediction to test: n₋ = 1 for ζ, n₋ = 0 for Δ, and two pole-type modes for E₁₂ (poles at s = ½ ± 11/2)
pitfalls: The 1/24 in the window model acts only through the weight, and its edge is generic, so the conjecture has no numerical support yet.
If stated as "the quotient is positive" it is equivalent to RH; the content would be the algebra, not the sign.

concepts.name: One Perron mode against the pole
concepts.plain: Split Weil's form on a grid of narrow boxes as W = Z + P, where Z (archimedean plus primes) has non-positive off-diagonal entries and P is the rank-2 pole term. On every grid tested, Z has exactly one negative eigenvalue, with an entrywise-positive (Perron) eigenvector. The pole's positive eigenvalue cancels it with a margin of 1e-3 to 1e-6. Without the primes, Z has about ell*6.29/pi - 1 negative modes; the primes collapse them into one. Positivity of W implies at most one negative mode of Z (theorem); an unconditional proof that there is exactly one, together with a positive 2x2 margin on all grids, is open and would imply RH. In the finite-field template the single negative mode is the ample (timelike) class of Hodge index and the pole is 2 d1 d2; fakes have two negative modes. The entrywise-positive Perron vector is automatic from the sign pattern and also occurs for fakes.

concepts.name: Allowed locally ≠ aligned globally: every Frobenius angle is allowed, but only the genuine assignment keeps the window form positive (Δ and 11a1)
concepts.plain: For a degree-2 L-function each prime has an angle θ_p (α_p/√p = e^(±iθ_p)). Hasse (11a1) and Deligne (Ramanujan’s Δ) make every angle real, and Sato–Tate says how they are distributed. Both are proved; GRH is open. In the window model the genuine angles keep the form positive for every window up to ℓ = 7, while the same angles permuted among the primes, i.i.d. Sato–Tate angles, aligned rearrangements, or one wrong local factor all fail quickly. Global positivity pins each angle to a fraction of a degree although 180° is allowed. So the missing piece is the joint law of the angles across all primes, together with the archimedean place and the conductor — not any single angle.

The Hecke relations (a_mn = a_m a_n, a_p² relation) hold for any assignment of angles, including the shuffled ones; what is joint is the existence of the modular form, i.e. the functional equation.

concepts.name: The induction matrix on the Q-quotient (Weil form on S-unit lattices)
concepts.plain: Place one Gaussian test function at log m for each S-smooth m ≤ N and take M_mn = W(η_m, η_n), Weil's quadratic form built from primes and the archimedean place. Translation invariance makes M_mn a function of the rational m/n alone. The couplings take both signs about equally (their pattern follows cos(γ₁ log(m/n))), so the matrix is pair-dependent but not ferromagnetic. Its smallest eigenvalue is positive and collapses super-exponentially as the lattice fills (σ = 0.1: 2.4e−5 → 8.7e−26 for N = 30). Restricting the prime sum to S makes it strongly negative, because the indefinite rank-2 pole term is no longer cancelled by the prime density. Including all primes up to the window scale restores positivity. The matrix is the Weil form rewritten: positivity for all such lattices is a restatement of RH.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: The induction matrix on the Q-quotient (Weil form on S-unit lattices)

concepts.name: Davenport-Heilbronn window jumps
concepts.plain: The Davenport-Heilbronn function has the functional equation and archimedean factor of an odd character mod 5 but no Euler product, and has off-line zeros near 0.8085+85.699i and 0.6508+114.163i. Its window form has no negative squares for short windows and gains them in pairs, one quadruple at a time, at window length about 3.9 and 5.67. So the archimedean place and the functional equation cannot force the second mode to stay non-degenerate: any proof must use the Euler product. This matches the constant-signature mechanism of Adiprasito-Huh-Katz Prop. 7.16, where non-degeneracy is proved independently.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Davenport-Heilbronn window jumps

concepts.name: Dilution law on the path from Davenport–Heilbronn to an Euler product: ℓ*(t) ≈ 5.1 + 2.5 log(1/(1−t))
concepts.plain: Mix the two forms: (1−t)·(Davenport–Heilbronn) + t·(½L(χ)L(χ̄)). On the zero side this carries the Davenport–Heilbronn zeros with weight 1−t, so for every t < 1 the off-line zeros are still there and some window eventually sees them. The window at which they are first seen recedes only logarithmically as t → 1. In plain words: any fixed amount of non-multiplicativity is caught by a long enough window. This calibrates "a proof must use the Euler product"; it says nothing about whether RH is true.
concepts.label: Numerical

concepts.name: Certified window for one off-line pair
concepts.plain: For a synthetic off-line quadruple at the height of the first zero, Paley-Wiener interpolants at the pole pair and the four off-line points, a written-out mollification step, and a tail bound (Poisson-kernel envelope of the kernels plus the Hadamard identity sum of Poisson kernels = (1/pi) Re xi'/xi) certify three negative squares for every window length at least 5.55, 3.60, 2.90, 2.20 at displacement 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.45. The certificate is floating point, not interval arithmetic. A closed form scales like displacement^(-2/3) at low height and like (1/displacement) log(8 displacement log(height/2pi)) at large height. The explicit length needs every off-line zero to be known.

concepts.name: Which channel detects a fake depends on the span
concepts.plain: For fake Frobenius data (functional equation kept, one root pair off the circle), when the chosen graphs span the fibre classes the pole channel is exactly zero and the failure is on the primitive part. With fewer graphs, the failure appears first in the odd pole channel while the primitive part is still positive. Over the rationals no finite section spans the fibre classes, so the model does not rule out an off-line zero showing first in the pole channel.

concepts.name: Which channel an off-line zero breaks first over the rationals
concepts.plain: Diagnostic, not evidence: off-line zero quartets were planted by hand on finite sections of Weil's form (box, sine, Legendre and bump bases; supports 1 to 5). In 225 of 226 failing runs the form first goes negative through the pole channel (even or odd, about equally). The primitive part fails just after, exactly when the planted zero gives the arch-plus-primes part a second unstable mode, and the gap between the two onsets shrinks as the section is refined. The finite-field rule 'incomplete span means the pole channel fails first' carries over; its 'odd channel' refinement does not, and the L2 distance of the fibre functionals from the section does not predict the channel.

concepts.name: Gluing curvature on prime pairs
concepts.plain: The mixed second difference of the lowest eigenvalue of the window form when two primes are switched off, K_g(p,q), is invariant under adding a multiple of the identity. For ζ, L(Δ) and 11a1 it is nonnegative on almost all prime pairs, while sign-flipped and permuted variants have about half the pairs negative. It is a tendency, not a sign law: the genuine twist of Δ by the character mod 5 has a fifth of its pairs negative, the 11a1 fraction grows with the window, and first differences already separate genuine from shuffled.

concepts.name: No single prime frame is positive in the window model
concepts.plain: The archimedean part of the window form is indefinite for ζ, L(Δ) and 11a1, and adding any single prime (or any pair of primes up to 47) does not make it positive; positivity appears only after all primes are glued. Local legality lives in the Euler factors, not in partial window forms. The conductor-5 twist of Δ is the exception: its archimedean part is already positive.

concepts.name: The zeta pole mode is the single unpaired negative square
concepts.plain: Without its pole term the zeta window form has exactly one negative square at every window length, always in the exchange-even sector; it is the only obstruction to a compatible quaternionic star. Analogy: degree-0 (real) part versus degree-1 (quaternionic) part in Deninger's graded category.

concepts.name: Nonnegative couplings plus a pole are not enough
concepts.plain: The Dedekind zeta of ℚ(i), ζ·L(χ₄), has nonnegative prime coefficients 1 + χ₄(p)ᵏ and a pole, and its window form stays positive. Replacing χ₄(p) by random signs keeps every coefficient nonnegative and keeps the pole and the Gamma factors, yet the window form fails for every random sign pattern tried. So a ferromagnetic sign of the couplings and a pole do not by themselves produce positivity: the genuine character (the arithmetic alignment) is needed.

concepts.name: Curvature as cup square: convexity ↔ Rosati positivity
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: K θ₁∧θ₂ = ω₁₃∧ω₂₃ (convention-independent; dω₁₂ = ±ω₁₃∧ω₂₃): Gauss curvature is a wedge square of second-fundamental-form 1-forms; Theorema Egregium; Gauss–Bonnet. Convex (II definite) ⇒ K > 0 ⇒ Cohn-Vossen rigidity (Herglotz). Dictionary: II ↔ H¹/cup product; convexity ↔ Rosati Tr(φφ′) > 0 ↔ |α| = √q; 'what is the arithmetic C²?' (FR-1).

concepts.name: Clausius as candidate positivity: Γ ≥ 0 is automatic, RH = Γ ≡ 0 (reversible / lossless); the working positivity is passivity (ghosts = gain), with Foster ⇔ Laguerre on the line
concepts.plain: Reading the width Γ as entropy production gives nothing, because widths are never negative anyway; RH says every width is zero, i.e. the system is reversible. The positivity that does work is passivity: ζ absorbs everywhere to the right of the line, while a ghost shows up as gain.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: [C] Clausius ∮δQ/T_res ≤ 0, equality iff reversible; entropy production ≥ 0 (Wikipedia 'Clausius theorem', opened). [N] Carnot T_h = 2, T_c = 1: Σ Q/T = 0, efficiency 0.5; conduction Q = 1 from 2 to 1: entropy production 0.5. [A] Γ_ρ = 2|β − ½| ↔ entropy production: Γ ≥ 0 holds by definition, so this 'second law' is empty; RH is the EQUALITY Γ ≡ 0 ('every mode reversible'), matching TAA Lemma 118 (RH = undoubled system lossless). [N] TAA Lemma 156 certified: ζ 52 zeros t < 150 all Γ = 0; DH Γ = 0.617034, 0.301660, 0.148712, 0.448515 (t < 200), sum 1.516. [R] The precise positivity law is passivity (Lagarias/Hinkkanen): RH ⇔ Re ξ′/ξ > 0 on Re s > ½; each zero gives a Lorentzian of sign sgn(σ − β), so a ghost is GAIN (negative absorption) for ½ < σ < β — the opposite sign to 'ghost = dissipation'. [N] t ∈ [80,120], σ ∈ {.55}: ζ min 0.0467 > 0; DH min −15.08 at (0.75, 85.7), negative on [85.5,85.9] and [114.1,114.3] at σ =. [T] On the line ξ′/ξ(½+it) = −iΞ′/Ξ is purely reactive (lossless); Foster's monotone reactance dX/dt > 0 is the Laguerre inequality Ξ′² − ΞΞ″ > 0 (⇐ RH; ⇏ RH, TAA Lemma 116 locally invisible ghosts). [C] de Bruijn–Newman: the forward (dissipative) heat flow creates off-line pairs (TAA Lemma 158, correction 16) — here 'ghost = dissipation' is right. [O] An entropy-production functional built without zeros (R5) whose zero set is Γ ≡ 0: none known.
pitfalls: Γ ≥ 0 is automatic: no content (TAA Lemma 159, correction 12).
In the passivity picture a ghost is gain, not dissipation; in the de Bruijn–Newman picture dissipation creates ghosts: say which (TAA Lemma 159, correction 12).

concepts.name: Time delay (Wigner)
concepts.plain: How long a wave packet lingers in the cusp; unlike the winding of the phase, the time-delay peak does see ghosts.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 143: winding ½ per zero for all β (ghost-blind), but time-delay peak at r = 42.85 is 3.09 (ζ), 27.22 (ζ + TAA Lemma 103 ghost), 27.42 (DH): ghost-sensitive. ζ time delay is negative for r ≲ 2.9 (min −3.87), so "positive delay" fails for ζ. TAA Lemma 120: dwell time ∂_x log|Φ| = −θ′(ω). TAA Lemma 118: Connes harmonic measure of an off-line zero = (1/2π) × TAA Lemma 117 excess group delay. TAA Lemma 153: Wigner time delay = −φ′/φ(½+it) = 2π dξ/dt (Birman–Krein); Wigner 1955 (Phys. Rev. 98, 145–147, doi 10.1103/PhysRev.98.145; Crossref) gives a causality lower bound, not positivity; ζ's delay negative only through −1/(¼+t²) (t ≤ 2.8); DH's positive everywhere, ghost = peak 27.27 at 42.84. TAA Lemma 154: the Wigner delay −φ′/φ is a sum of positive Breit–Wigner lines (two per zero, HWHM β/2, (1−β)/2); the group delay of ξ along σ (Re ξ′/ξ) is a sum of signed ones; negative group delay in Re s > ½ is a ghost (TAA Lemma 154, correction 12: optics 'superluminal is harmless' does not transfer).
pitfalls: Positive time delay fails for ζ (TAA Lemma 143 corrections).

concepts.name: Källén–Lehmann spectral positivity
concepts.plain: Physical theories have non-negative spectral weight; ζ analogue is the sign of zero weights.

concepts.name: Global complex structure J on arithmetic H¹ (sharpened missing piece)
concepts.plain: RH would follow from a real structure J (J² = −1, antisymmetric) on the conjectural arithmetic H¹, commuting with the flow and making tr(f ∪ Jf) positive, restricting to the Frobenius rotation α_p/√p at each prime and to multiplication by i on the critical line at infinity. A Z/4 action with J² = −1 is the same assumption as i. i ∈ Q_p iff p ≡ 1 mod 4. Local pieces are theorems (Hasse, Deligne); the CM case shows local coherence is insufficient.

concepts.name: Hodge energy on arithmetic cohomology, and a torsion term with forced sign
concepts.plain: Deninger's heuristic: if H¹ of compactified Spec Z had a Hodge star making tr(f ∪ ⋆f′) positive definite and commuting with the flow, the generator would be ½ plus a skew operator, giving RH. This is a Maxwell-energy shape (∫F∧⋆F). Open: no arithmetic field strength exists, and it is unknown whether the conjectural cohomology or its foliated models carry a torsion term with a forced sign.

concepts.plain: Arithmetic quantities are measured relative to a reference fixed by the pole; the "error" is the displacement from that reference.

concepts.name: Formal intersection lattice vs geometric surface (ghost-blind vs proof-bearing)
concepts.plain: Numbers arranged as an intersection lattice prove nothing by themselves; on a real surface the Hodge index theorem makes them proof-bearing.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: A formal lattice of intersection numbers (TAA Lemma 150 Ψ_n lattice = Weil's form as a lattice) satisfies whatever identities are built in and was ghost-blind (λ_max −0.416 ζ vs −2.226 DH at K = 90; TAA Lemma 150 Prop 2.3). On C×C the same numbers are proof-bearing because the Hodge index is a theorem about the surface (ample class + RR), proved before the αᵢ are known. The composition law can be imposed consistently on any FE data (fakes, DH): only definiteness separates (TAA Lemma 149 DH prime-side onset 3.85; fakes (2,2)) (TAA Lemma 152, correction 5). What carries the numbers: classes Γ_t with a composition law from a flow, an ample class, RR strong enough for Hodge index.

concepts.name: Band criterion γ < 2T_M
concepts.plain: A ζ zero (or ghost) at height γ is visible in the class-number data only if every Maass form with t_j < γ/2 is known and subtracted; the zero’s frequency γ/2 must lie below the unknown-Maass band.
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 148 Prop. band [H, N support]: with T_M = 100 the DH-location ghost (85.699, δ =.3085) has count-matched SNR 238 (x = 1e8) / 270 (x = 1e10); with T_M = 35.4 it is 0.15. γ = 143.1, δ =.1: SNR 4.6 (T_M = 100) vs 0.010 (T_M = 35.4). Reaching height γ needs ≈ γ²/48 Maass forms and the zero list below γ ⇒ the readout only re-derives listed zeros.

pitfalls: Not a theorem; the noise model treats unknown t_j as random.

concepts.plain: In foliated Lefschetz formulas, a leaf preserved by the flow contributes a term that looks like the archimedean factor. Matching it with the pole push is an open test.

concepts.name: Log-det Hessian curvature on prime directions is negative for genuine forms
concepts.plain: Defining a metric on prime weights by the Hessian of -log|det| of the window form (window length 3, primes up to 19), every genuine L-function tested has negative sectional curvature on all coordinate planes and negative Ricci and scalar curvature; the hypothesis of nonnegative curvature fails. Sign-flipped forms differ mainly by an indefinite metric, which restates the ghost count.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Log-det Hessian curvature on prime directions is negative for genuine forms.

concepts.name: Dedekind zeta of ℚ(i): one pole, exactly one unstable mode, aligned with the pole vector
concepts.plain: For ζ_ℚ(i) = ζ·L(χ₄) the arithmetic side of the window form is ζ’s plus a pole-free part. As predicted, it has exactly one unstable mode on every window tested, aligned with the pole vector and entrywise positive, and the full form W has no negative squares. Its margins are about three times ζ’s, which is automatic because W_K = W_ζ + W_χ.

concepts.name: The admissible prime weights form a thin slab: narrow along total mass, about 30 times wider along mass-neutral directions

The allowed region is narrowest near 30–37° (close to the total-mass, i.e. pole, direction) and widest near 127° (roughly mass-neutral). The aspect ratio is about 30, and both widths shrink at about e^(−0.8ℓ). Rotating by 45° separates a pole direction from a primitive direction but does not escape the shrinking.

The prime pattern does fit somewhat better than additive or random patterns, and better on the true form than on a control built from jittered zeros: a weak arithmetic signal. Any exact factor is, up to rotation, indexed by the zeros (circular).

concepts.name: Birman–Krein bridge: scattering phase = spectral shift; −φ′/φ = spectral density = Wigner delay = Maass–Selberg intercept
concepts.plain: The scattering phase at the cusp counts states; its derivative is a sum of positive bumps, one pair per zeta zero, whose widths tell where the zero sits.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Birman–Krein (Dokl. 144 (1962) 475–478): det S(λ) = e^{−2πiξ(λ)} [Cs]. Cusp of SL₂(ℤ): S = φ (one cusp), φ(½+it) = Λ(2it)/Λ(1+2it), |φ| = 1 (NUM 3.9e−31, t ≤ 60), so dξ/dt = (1/2π)(−φ′/φ)(½+it) (sign convention). THEOREM (Hadamard; NUM ≤ 3.9e−6 with 1517 zeros + tail): −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1/(¼+t²) + Σ_ρ [a/(a²+(t−γ/2)²) + b/(b²+(t−γ/2)²)], a = (1−β)/2, b = β/2: each zero gives two Lorentzians of mass π (winding ghost-blind), widths ghost-sensitive. The only negative term is the ζ pole term −1/(¼+t²) (negativity t ≤ 2.8; TAA Lemma 153, correction 23 refined). DH (Λ entire): −φ′/φ > 0 everywhere (min 0.41 on [0.5,60]) even with its ghost, so density positivity is ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 153, correction 29); ghost = narrow Lorentzians (peak 27.27 at t = 42.84; predicted ghost part 25.84). The ratio across the y-axis = φ; for ζ the analogous ratio is χ(s) = ζ(s)/ζ(1−s), χ(½+it) = e^{−2iθ(t)} gives the smooth part θ/π of N(T).

concepts.name: Ghost count of the arithmetic side
concepts.plain: Write Weil's form as W = Z + P, with P the rank-2 pole term of signature (1,1) and Z the archimedean-plus-primes side, and restrict to test functions supported in a window of length l. The number of negative squares of Z on the window is at most 1 + N+, where N+ is the number of distinct zeros off the critical line to the right, and for every finite N <= N+ it is at least 1 + N once the window is long enough. So the count increases to 1 + N+. In the combined ledger the pole pair at +-i/2 enters exactly like an off-line zero pair with multiplicity -1; its negative direction is the even (cosh) pole vector, i.e. the Perron mode.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Frobenius-graph Toeplitz form and its pole/count split
concepts.plain: For the graphs of Frobenius powers, the defect between the m-th and n-th graph is q^min(m,n) times the trace t_|m-n|. After rescaling by q^(-n/2) the defect Gram matrix is Toeplitz (Hallouin-Perret 2019). It splits as a rank-2 pole term of signature (1,1) (the fibre classes) plus minus the Toeplitz matrix of normalised point counts, which is the finite-field shadow of Weil's form split as pole plus archimedean-and-primes. Checked by brute-force counts for an elliptic curve at three primes and for three genus-2 curves.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Castelnuovo-Severi and Weil's bound
concepts.plain: On a product of two curves, the defect 2 d1 d2 - D^2 is non-negative for every divisor D (Castelnuovo-Severi). It follows from the Hodge index theorem applied to the primitive part of D, and Hodge index itself follows from Riemann-Roch on the surface plus the existence of an effective multiple. Applied to the diagonal and the graph of Frobenius it gives Weil's bound. Weil's own 1948 proof used Riemann-Roch on the curve only; Mattuck-Tate (1958) used Riemann-Roch on the product; Grothendieck (1958) reduced it to Hodge index.

So the counts being non-negative is exactly the off-diagonal sign pattern, and Hodge index is exactly one negative mode.

concepts.name: In Li's variable ξ is a self-reciprocal series with positive coefficients
concepts.plain: Put z = 1 − 1/s and F(z) = ξ(1/(1 − z)). The functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s) becomes F(1/z) = F(z), the critical line becomes the unit circle |z| = 1, every Taylor coefficient of F at z = 0 is positive, and a₁/a₀ = λ₁, Li's first coefficient. This is the shape of a Lee–Yang partition function in the fugacity z, so Li's circle and the Lee–Yang circle are the same circle in this variable. RH is then the Lee–Yang property of F (a Restatement); nothing is proved about the zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: In Li's variable ξ is a self-reciprocal series with positive coefficients.
concepts.formula: F(z) = ξ(1/(1−z)) = Σ aₙzⁿ, aₙ > 0, F(1/z) = F(z), a₁/a₀ = λ₁ = 1 + γ/2 − ½log 4π
pitfalls: Positivity of coefficients is proved: ξ(½ + w) = Σ b_k w^{2k} with b_k > 0 and w = (1 + z)/(2(1 − z)) has positive coefficients. It does not imply that the zeros lie on |z| = 1; that is RH.

concepts.name: RH for zeta-built functions without Euler product
concepts.plain: Weng zeta functions of reductive groups over Q are finite combinations of completed zeta ratios with a functional equation and no Euler product; RH is proved for rank 2 and Sp(4), and for all but finitely many zeros in the Chevalley case under a geometric hypothesis.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: RH for zeta-built functions without Euler product. Sources: arXiv:math/0412039; arXiv:0802.0102; arXiv:1011.4583.

concepts.plain: Connes and Consani proved Riemann–Roch for the compactified Spec ℤ, counting sections by integer numbers of generators; it is a one-dimensional "χ = degree + constant" law and cannot see D².
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: CC23 Thm 1.1/5.1 over 𝕊: dim H⁰ − dim H¹ = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (genus 0, base 2, no exceptional set); CC22 over 𝕊[±1]: ⌈(deg D + log 2)/log 3⌉′ − 1_L, duality H⁰(K−D) ≅ Hom(H¹(D), U(1)_{1/4}), K = −2{2}; scaling site Thm 5.17 Dim_ℝ H⁰(D) − Dim_ℝ H⁰(−D) = deg D. Verdict (TAA Lemma 147): all proved RRs are 1-dimensional, χ = deg + const ⇒ blind to D² by TAA Lemma 145 parity.
pitfalls: RR is for the Arakelov compactification Spec ℤ̄, not Spec ℤ; two versions, the 𝕊 one supersedes 𝕊[±1] (TAA Lemma 147, correction 3).
Dim_ℝ is a Lebesgue covering dimension on C_p, not a theta count (TAA Lemma 147, correction 1).

concepts.name: Oscillator semigroup: positive ⇔ real A with symplectic eigenvalues ≤ 1 (archimedean, ghost-blind)
concepts.plain: Positive Gaussian operators exist exactly on the stable (rotation) side; this is real but archimedean, so it cannot tell ζ from a fake.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: [C] Dereziński–Karczmarczyk arXiv:1701.07297 Prop. 10: a·Op(e^{−A}) (A ∈ Sym++(ℂ^{2d})) is Hermitian iff a ∈ ℝ, A real; positive iff a > 0 and A ∈ Sym_p(ℝ^{2d}) (σ(Aθ) ⊂ [−1,1]); following Howe. [T,N] d = 1: Op(e^{−λ(x²+p²)}) = r^N/(1+λ), r = (1−λ)/(1+λ): positive iff λ ≤ 1; normalized elements are contractions with generator −N (harmonic oscillator, the rotation side). The IHO quadratic x² − p² is indefinite, so its Gaussians are not in the positive cone. [T] dissipative A ⇒ Re⟨(λ−A)⁻¹x,x⟩ > 0 for Re λ > 0 (Carathéodory). [R] A contraction semigroup whose generator realizes {ρ − ½} would give Lagarias's Re ξ′/ξ > 0 and, with the functional equation, RH. [A] the oscillator semigroup itself has spectrum {−n}, unrelated to zeros: 'contraction ⇒ no gain lines' is an analogy for it.
numbers: Carathéodory: min Re m = 0.0308 > 0 over 200 random dissipative 6×6
pitfalls: Re A > 0 gives bounded operators, not positive ones (positive needs A real, Prop. 10).
Contraction alone + FE would already force β = ½ if the zeros were its spectrum: the content is the realization, not the sign.

concepts.name: Width → area → 2-form: (1/2π)Δ log|ξ| dσ∧dt = Σ δ_ρ
concepts.plain: A zero’s line always has area π however wide it is; stacking these areas over the strip gives the 2-form that counts zeros, and RH would need that count to come from a positive pairing.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Re ξ′/ξ(σ+it) = ∂_σ log|ξ|; each line has area π·sgn(σ−β) independent of its width (width × height = 1); crossing σ = β the area jumps by 2π = flux of ∇log|ξ| around ρ; Poincaré–Lelong/Jensen: (1/2π)Δ log|ξ| dσ∧dt = Σ_ρ δ_ρ (BIB). [N] TAA Lemma 154 fitted amplitudes = 1 to ≤ 3.4e−5 (area π); DH ghost-1 near amplitude −1 at d = 0.30, +1 at d = 0.35. [R] Pairing the 2-form with test functions = zero side of Weil's explicit formula; making it positive = MP4. Local areas are ghost-blind in total; their sign seen from σ > ½ is ghost-sensitive.

concepts.name: Automorphy defect (TAA Lemma 144)
concepts.plain: How far a function fails to be modular, packaged as a cocycle; it is phase data.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 144: defect is a cocycle; ghost-blind. "Cocycles give structure, not sign."

concepts.name: Certified positivity windows
concepts.plain: Computer-certified intervals on which the Weil form is positive.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Certified windows: progress log reaches e² and hybrid e^2.4; one text says "stop at 1.6". All below ghost onsets, ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 142).
concepts.uncertain: Which extent is current needs a check of the progress log.
pitfalls: Source conflict: "stop at 1.6" vs progress log to e², e^2.4.

concepts.name: Base-regularity test (B) and the B* no-go: B* (Euler product + counting error O(x^θ), θ < ½ ⇒ RH) appears false — a deterministic discretization of a continuous Beurling system keeps an exact zero at 0.75 ± 10i while the measured counting exponent is θ̂ ≈ 0.29 up to x = 5·10⁷ (Numerical refutation; asymptotic θ < ½ not proved); integer-counting error over 9 systems: ℤ bounded (≤ 1), Davenport–Heilbronn bounded, Epstein and ζ_Q(i) θ̂ ≈ 0.32, random discretizations at order √x
concepts.plain: To separate the genuine integers from imitations, count how many 'integers' lie below x and compare with the expected straight line. For ℤ the error never exceeds 1. Imitation number systems built with random or slightly shifted primes wobble by about √x, which first suggested a conjecture (B*): a system with unique factorization whose wobble stays well below √x must satisfy RH. That now looks false. Choosing the imitation primes deterministically, so that they track a smooth system with a planted zero off the line, keeps unique factorization and keeps the planted zero exactly, yet the wobble grows only like x^0.29 as far as it was computed (x = 5·10⁷). So counting regularity alone does not force RH. This is numerical evidence, not a proof: nobody has shown the exponent stays below ½ forever.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: [N] B* (Euler product + N(x) = ρx + O(x^θ), θ < ½ ⇒ RH) appears false: a deterministic discretization of the continuous Beurling system below (g-primes chosen greedily so that the prime-counting discrepancy, prime powers included, stays ≤ 1) keeps an exact zero at 0.75 ± 10i, because ζ_P = ζ_T·e^H with H holomorphic on Re s > 0 [T, given the continuous system], while the measured counting exponent is θ̂ ≈ 0.29 up to x = 5·10⁷ (max|N − ρx| ≈ 4.3·x^0.3; ratio to √x falls from 0.61 to 0.116). Asymptotic θ < ½ is not proved, so this is a numerical refutation, not a theorem. Compare Diamond–Montgomery–Vorhauer (2006) and Broucke–Vindas (arXiv 2102.08478); prior examples were not exhaustively searched. Consequence: integer-counting regularity is a no-go as a route to RH on its own. [N] Earlier controls to X = 10⁷: random (Poisson) discretizations and integer-supported random multiplicities fluctuate at order √x; that √x noise came from the prime-counting discrepancy, not from discreteness [H]. [T] continuous system ζ_C = (s − ρ₀)(s − ρ̄₀)(s + 10)/(s²(s − 1)), N_C = ρx + O(log² x), positivity min f/t = 0.193 (computer-assisted). [C] DMV 2006 (θ > ½, RH fails), Zhang (RH with regular N), BDV 2020 (RH with large N oscillation), Hilberdink 2005 (the integer and prime exponents cannot both be < ½; not contradicted here, since the prime count is far from li x).
numbers: deterministic discretization: θ̂ ≈ 0.28–0.29 up to x = 5·10⁷ (2,994,465 g-primes); max|N − ρx| ≈ 4.3·x^0.3; ratio to √x 0.61 → 0.116
ψ regression coefficient on the planted term 0.9999993
random controls, ratio to √x: PERT 0.19–0.28; CRAMER 0.6–1.4; ZERO 1.6–2.0; RANDMULT 3.1–4.4
concepts.uncertain: Numerical refutation: θ < ½ for the discretized system is not proved asymptotically; prior examples in the literature were not exhaustively searched.
pitfalls: θ̂ are finite-range slopes (x ≤ 5·10⁷); θ < ½ asymptotically is not proved.
B* was earlier listed as a live conjecture; it is withdrawn on this numerical evidence.
Euler product + counting data still excludes Davenport–Heilbronn and Epstein, but only through the Euler product.

rels.note: (B) as the additive shadow of stable directions [H]

concepts.name: Wick rotation of one Euler frame: t = 2cos θ → 2cos(iφ) = 2cosh φ; elliptic (bounded U_k, poles on |u| = 1 = local unitarity) → parabolic (k + 1, double pole) → hyperbolic (sinh growth); endpoint φ = ½ log p is ζ(s)ζ(s−1) (Eisenstein)
concepts.plain: Each prime's Euler factor is one frame. Changing cos θ to cos(iφ) = cosh φ slides it from bounded oscillation, through the meeting point, to exponential growth. The far end of the slide is exactly the Euler factor of ζ(s)ζ(s−1). An Euler factor never vanishes, so this moves poles, not zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] 1/(1 − tu + u²) = Σ U_k(t/2)u^k, u = p^{½−s} (arithmetic s, weight 2) = p^{−s'} (analytic). Elliptic t = 2cos θ: c_k = sin((k+1)θ)/sin θ, poles e^{±iθ}; parabolic t = 2: c_k = k + 1, double pole u = 1; hyperbolic θ = iφ: c_k = sinh((k+1)φ)/sinh φ, poles e^{±φ}, Re s = ½ ∓ φ/log p. φ = ½ log p: t = √p + 1/√p, factor = 1/((1 − p^{−s})(1 − p^{1−s})), Hecke eigenvalue 1 + p (weight-2 Eisenstein). sl₂: tr exp X = 2cos √det X (det X = θ², 0, −k²). [T] No Euler factor vanishes; a convergent product of non-zero factors is non-zero (zeros only after continuation). [N] errors ≤ 5e−30; ζ(s)ζ(s−1) identity 3.4e−31; sl₂ 6.3e−14 (300 X). |u| = 1 is local unitarity (tempered), NOT the critical line (Re s = 1 arithmetic) (TAA Lemma 160, correction 3). Cusp forms elliptic (Eichler–Shimura + Weil; Deligne); Maass: Ramanujan open, Kim–Sarnak 7/64 bounds the hyperbolic excursion. [A] physics Wick rotation rotates time, here the angle/frequency is rotated (TAA Lemma 160, correction 7). TAA Lemma 162: ζ frames are exactly the four-squares/Eisenstein frames r₄(p)/8 = p + 1; KS coupling-constant metamorphosis ω² = −E/2 is the oscillator version of cos θ → cosh φ.
concepts.formula: cosh φ = cos(iφ); 1/(1 − 2cosh φ·u + u²) = Σ sinh((k+1)φ)/sinh φ · u^k
numbers: p = 5, φ = ½ log 5: poles 1/√5, √5 (Re s = 1, 0)
pitfalls: Local poles never lie on the critical line of a cusp form (TAA Lemma 160, correction 3).

concepts.name: Morse picture of the strata: lobes (extrema), wedge (saddle level), hyperbolic windows (index 1)
aliases: lobes vs wedges vs hyperbolic windows
concepts.plain: Near a non-degenerate critical point a function looks like a quadratic form: a minimum gives closed elliptical loops (lobes), a saddle gives hyperbolas, and the level through the saddle is a pair of crossing lines (the wedge).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Morse lemma: near a non-degenerate critical point f = f(p) ± x² ± y² in suitable coordinates. Index 0 or 2: level sets are closed ellipse-like loops (J. W. McGreevy’s lobes). Index 1: level sets are hyperbolas and the critical level is a crossing line pair (the pure wedge, the dual conic of which is a double point: dual_conic). det Hess = 0 is the degenerate parabolic case (a² = 4q, double line). This is the local version of conic_type_at_infinity, and the block test of blockwise_weil_diagnostic: an off-line pair gives an index-1 (hyperbolic) 2×2 block, a ‘hyperbolic window’ (DH: [84.36,84.77], [85.48,85.91], [114.04,114.29], TAA Lemma 153). [A] Identification with the animation frames.
concepts.uncertain: Chat-level concept; not a lemma result. Morse lemma not opened at source.
pitfalls: Standard Morse lemma; no source opened in a lemma. The reading of the animation frames is an Analogy (code lost, TAA Lemma 152, correction 11).

concepts.name: Zeros as frames: simple real zero = elliptic, double zero = parabolic (collision), conjugate pair/quartet = hyperbolic; real zeros leave the line only by collision or from infinity
concepts.plain: Think of each zero on the line as a frame that is still elliptic. Two zeros can leave the line only by first merging into a double zero, the parabolic moment, and then splitting into a mirror pair off the line. The only other route is for off-line zeros to come in from infinity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] For a continuous family F_t of real entire functions (e.g. de Bruijn–Newman H_t, Rodgers–Tao convention H_t(z) = ∫₀^∞ e^{tu²}Φ(u)cos(zu)du, H_0(z) = ξ(½ + iz/2)/8): (a) a simple real zero stays simple and real for nearby t (Hurwitz + conjugation symmetry); (b) non-real zeros come in pairs z, z̄ (quartets ±z, ±z̄ for even F_t = TAA Lemma 103 ghost quartet); (c) a real zero becomes non-real inside a bounded region only through a real zero of multiplicity ≥ 2 at the transition; otherwise non-real zeros arrive from infinity. [A] Spectral reading: separated F ≠ V on the circle / F = V merge / hyperbolic split (TAA Lemma 158 §H). [N] independent quadrature: zeros 4, 5 of H_t collide at t* = −3.954792524, x* = 66.1974676 (TAA Lemma 111 −3.954792522, diff 2.2e−9), ∂²H ≠ 0 (double); box |Re z − x*| ≤ 4, |Im z| ≤ 1.5: argument principle 2.000000 at t* + 0.05, t* − 0.05, t* − 0.3, real zeros 2, 0, 0; pair 66.4147 ± 0.7812i at t* − 0.3; fold law |Im| ∝ (t* − t)^{1/2} (Polymath §3; TAA Lemma 111 fit 0.51). [T, KGL] only opposite Krein signs exit (4×4 toy, ε = 0.2: window |ω₁ − ω₂| < 0.2, max Re λ 0.0995; same sign ≤ 2.2e−16); graphical Krein sign of H_t alternates (−,+,… on zeros 1–8), so every adjacent pair is a possible exit.
numbers: box count 2.000000 across collision; real count 2 → 0
pitfalls: Global zeros are not frame mergers: no Euler factor vanishes (TAA Lemma 160, correction 1, TAA Lemma 160, correction 4).
Zeros can also arrive from infinity; Hurwitz is local (TAA Lemma 160, correction 11).

rels.note: zero-level version of the F/V merge

concepts.name: Pole of ζ at s = 1 (residue / 3/π)
concepts.plain: ζ has a pole at s = 1; the Eisenstein series E(z,s) has its pole there with residue 3/π, the reciprocal of the area of the modular surface.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Res_{s=1} E(z,s) = 3/π = 1/vol(SL₂(ℤ)∖ℍ); E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) is the non-holomorphic correction (TAA Lemma 144/TAA Lemma 145 context).
pitfalls: The point 1 is not ∞.

concepts.name: Dual conic (adjugate): ellipse ↔ ellipse, hyperbola ↔ hyperbola, line pair ↔ double point
concepts.plain: The family of tangent lines of a conic is itself a conic; for a pair of crossing lines it collapses to the crossing point, counted twice.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The tangent lines of a nondegenerate conic xᵀMx = 0 (3×3) form the dual conic uᵀM⁻¹u = 0 (equivalently adj M). For the affine block xᵀAx = 1: dual yᵀA⁻¹y = 1 (same type). A line pair (rank 2 in P²; J. W. McGreevy's pure wedge) has rank-1 adjugate: the dual is the vertex counted twice (claim 4 correct, for the 3×3 projective matrix). Fixes the 'unique absolute definition' of each stratum up to scale.

concepts.name: Arakelov geometry
concepts.plain: Compactified arithmetic surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 74: Ô(1)² = ½ for FS metrics; pole-plane Gram [[½,1],[1,0]] signature (1,1); Hodge index vacuous in genus 0. TAA Lemma 139: Pic^(Spec ℤ̄) ≅ ℝ has rank 1 and no complex structure. TAA Lemma 65/TAA Lemma 145: Faltings–Hriljac = Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces (curve × Spec O_K), relative part = Néron–Tate, not ζ. TAA Lemma 138 R5: Néron–Tate PD (37a1 ĥ = 0.051114). TAA Lemma 152: Faltings 1984 (Ann. Math. 119, 387–424), Hriljac 1985 (Amer. J. Math. 107, 23–38), bibliographic data verified: Hodge index on arithmetic surfaces ⇒ Néron–Tate positive definite; not RH for any L-function (TAA Lemma 152, correction 12).
numbers: TAA Lemma 158: Moriwaki (opened) Thm B, d = 1 case = Faltings–Hriljac: deg(x·ĉ₁(H)^{d−1})-form ≤ 0 on classes with z(x)·H^{d−1} = 0, equality iff nx = f*(y); hypothesis d = dim f ≥ 1 excludes Spec ℤ itself (d = 0, CĤ¹ ≅ ℝ)
pitfalls: Faltings–Hriljac gives height positivity, not RH (TAA Lemma 152, correction 12).

concepts.name: √2 family
concepts.plain: Geodesic from 1 + √2; it is not singled out.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §1: traces t_k = 6, 34, 198, 1154, 6726 (Pell), lengths kℓ₀, ℓ₀ = 4 log(1+√2) = 3.5255; length-ordered series is periodic (period 2πi/ℓ₀ = 1.7822i) ⇒ cannot carry ζ zeros; conductor-ordered = h⁺R(8)ζ(s−1)/L(s,χ₈). TAA Lemma 146, correction 2: √2 is not the first norm −1 unit (φ is smaller).
pitfalls: √2 is not the first norm −1 unit; the golden ratio is smaller (TAA Lemma 146).

concepts.name: Toeplitz / Verblunsky coefficients
concepts.plain: Positivity of Toeplitz matrices ⇔ |α_n| < 1; each step a boost of rapidity artanh|α|.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 112 [C Simon]: Carathéodory–Toeplitz–Herglotz; T_{n+1} ≻ 0 ⇔ |α_j| < 1 ∀j < n; n₋(T_N) = #{E_n < 0}, sign flips at each |α_j| > 1. Levinson: PD ⇔ |κ_j| < 1, each step a boost of rapidity artanh κ (true |κ| < 1 for 60 orders; ghost κ₈ = −1.0009). TAA Lemma 117: U(1,1) boost of velocity |α|; |α| > 1 = Krein swap ∘ boost. TAA Lemma 37/TAA Lemma 118: Schur/Verblunsky layer stripping = restatement (circular).

concepts.name: Cusp ≠ archimedean place
concepts.plain: The cusp of the modular curve and the archimedean place of ℚ are different objects, though both get written ∞.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The cusp is a point of the modular curve; the archimedean place is a valuation of ℚ. Neither is the frame bundle, and ∞-toposes are unrelated to the infinite place.
pitfalls: Do not identify cusp, place ∞, frame bundle, ∞-topos.

concepts.name: F₁ base
concepts.plain: The hoped-for "field with one element" under Spec ℤ. Over F₁ the single Frobenius trace becomes a sum over all zeros, and Connes–Consani take the sphere spectrum 𝕊 as F₁.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 65: a_p is the right model, but over F₁ the single trace becomes Σ_ρ u^ρ (one eigenvalue per zero, infinite genus, N(1) = −∞); for curves the CC dictionary is literal (u = qⁿ, α_i = q^{ρ_i}). CC10 N(u) positive on (1,∞) is prime-side and shared by Beurling systems ⇒ cannot force RH alone. TAA Lemma 147, correction 4: "On the metaphysics of F₁" proves no new RR; it restates CC23 and discusses 𝕊 as F₁.
pitfalls: CC N(u) is only formal (TAA Lemma 65 C1).
TAA Lemma 158: Borger's square is the Witt space W*(Spec ℤ), not Spec ℤ (the collapse is Durov's).

concepts.name: Gluing connections are flat; a signed curvature must live in the metric
concepts.plain: A Galois representation is an étale local system on Spec Z minus finitely many primes, i.e. a flat connection whose holonomy at p is Frobenius. The connection ω = W⁻¹dW of the window family W(t) = A + Σ t_p T_p is also flat. In the Hessian geometry of −log det the flat and Levi-Civita connections differ by a symmetric tensor (non-metricity), not by torsion. So curvature with a sign has to come from a metric (Petersson, Weil), whose existence over Spec Z is the open part.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Gluing connections are flat; a signed curvature must live in the metric.

concepts.name: Local-to-global failure
concepts.plain: Local positivity at each prime does not imply global.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 25 Rem 6.2: naive local positivity fails (K < 0 for |r| < 6.28984); CC21 Thm 1 local archimedean positivity only for supp ⊂ [2^{−½}, 2^{½}] with vanishing. TAA Lemma 64/TAA Lemma 65: local Hasse (Q_p > 0 at every p, proved) vs global RH for L(E,s) (open) — the collective split. TAA Lemma 66: local positivity via Deligne weights is ghost-blind residual data.

concepts.name: No real-coefficient Weil cohomology for arithmetic curves
concepts.plain: A Serre-type argument excludes a Weil-type cohomology with real coefficients for Spec of a number ring; a version valued in a Z/2-graded category (quaternionic odd part) remains possible. A real symmetric metric on the first cohomology must therefore carry an extra quaternionic structure.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: No real-coefficient Weil cohomology for arithmetic curves. Sources: arXiv:2204.02714.

concepts.name: Null-line quotient (Gupta-Bleuler form)
concepts.plain: In a non-degenerate space with exactly one negative square, the orthogonal complement of any neutral vector is non-negative and its quotient by that vector is positive definite; a dilation that fixes the neutral line descends to a unitary operator. On finite windows the scale-character representers are negative but tend to neutral, so the quotient is reached only in the limit. On each window the quotient is positive exactly when the arithmetic side has one negative square; there is no version with a margin uniform in the window length, since the margin is squeezed between the smallest eigenvalue of W and the second eigenvalue of Z, both tending to 0. The representer value q(K+-) is about 5 to 40 times lambda_min(W)/kappa^2 (Woodbury), so it tracks the smallest eigenvalue of W.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Null-line quotient (Gupta-Bleuler form)
concepts.formula: n_- = 1, Z(e) = 0  =>  Z >= 0 on e^perp,  e^perp / e positive definite

concepts.name: S-mirror ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄
concepts.plain: Reflecting across the critical line; a zero is fixed exactly when it is on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ρ fixed by ρ ↦ 1 − ρ̄ ⇔ β = ½.

concepts.name: Arithmetic Hodge index: definite after quotienting an isotropic line
concepts.plain: For adelic line bundles with zero degree against nef big classes, the self-intersection is non-positive; the pairing is semi-definite on the orthogonal of the pulled-back classes, those classes are maximal isotropic, and the quotient is definite.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Arithmetic Hodge index: definite after quotienting an isotropic line. Sources: arXiv:1304.3538; doi:10.1007/s00208-016-1414-1.

concepts.name: Closed geodesics on the modular surface
concepts.plain: Lengths 2 log ε_t from traces t; Selberg trace formula pairs them with resonances.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Length 2 log ε_t with h⁺ classes (TAA Lemma 143); trace-6 has 3 primitive oriented classes (TAA Lemma 141); counts t = 3..11: 1,2,2,3,3,4,2,6,3. √2 geodesic ℓ = 3.5254943481, sinh(ℓ/2) = 2√2; golden geodesic 1.9248 is shortest. S(t) = Σ h⁺ log ε⁺², 36 discriminants 0 mismatches (TAA Lemma 143). TAA Lemma 148: S(t) extended to t ≤ 1e5 via quadclassunit, validated = qfbclassno on 8000 traces (2.3e−16); hR = √d L(1,χ)/2 checked to 2.2e−16.

concepts.name: Density / volume reading
concepts.plain: The modular surface’s volume form and the half-density: area π/3 gives degree 1/12, and the half-density y^½ is the Heaviside ½ — structure, not sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 §7: c₁(ω, Pet) = dxdy/(4πy²); area π/3 ⇒ deg ω = 1/12 = −ζ(−1); χ_orb = −1/6; half-density y^½ unitary L²(dr) → L²(dy/y²) = Heaviside ½. TAA Lemma 145: the U-form is indefinite, not a volume (TAA Lemma 145 corrections); volume formula for h⁰ is heuristic.
pitfalls: Volume form ≠ Levi-Civita connection (TAA Lemma 141 list).

concepts.name: Multi-channel first-order factors are bounded by the SOS fit
concepts.plain: If every channel of Q lies in a fixed operator dictionary, Σ_k Q_kᵀQ_k = Σ X_ab B_aᵀB_b with X ⪰ 0, so no number of channels beats the sum-of-squares fit in that dictionary. For Weil's form on short-support Legendre bases with the dictionary {I, functions of the archimedean part, prime shifts}, two channels reach 5.8–7.1% residual, matching the SOS bound (5.8–6.8%); one archimedean plus one shift channel is far worse (27–60%).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Multi-channel first-order factors are bounded by the SOS fit
numbers: independent recheck: λ_min = 9.44716e−7 (support 1, N 24), 2.05904e−16 (support 2, N 24), 1.62356e−20 (support 2, N 32); archimedean-plus-pole positivity up to support 0.7432
pitfalls: λ_min at fixed support keeps falling with N; quote N with every value

concepts.name: Modularity as the observability link
concepts.plain: By the modularity theorem the Galois phases of an elliptic curve over Q are those of a weight-2 newform, giving continuation, functional equation and a unitary automorphic representation with the Petersson metric. Shuffled angles have no modular partner. It is not sufficient for RH: elliptic curves and Delta are modular and their RH is open.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Modularity as the observability link.

concepts.name: Principalization
concepts.plain: Making divisors principal; Abel–Jacobi = principalization (TAA Lemma 139).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 60: "principalization as hamiltonization"; clutching = principalization (analogy). TAA Lemma 71: curve version theorem — #Pic⁰(F_{pⁿ}) = |1 − πⁿ|²; on Spec ℤ only the ℝ>0 boost (blind to θ_p). TAA Lemma 73: class group = obstruction to integral spinor square roots of light rays. TAA Lemma 139: Abel–Jacobi = principalization.

concepts.name: Selberg resonances
concepts.plain: Poles of φ(s) relate to ζ zeros at s = ρ/2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ = Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s) has poles in Re s < ½ exactly at ρ/2, φ(½) = −1 (TAA Lemma 143). ΣΛ(P)N^{−s} = Z′/Z(s) − Z′/Z(s+1). TAA Lemma 143: ρ/2 seen in the length spectrum from class numbers (projection on the predicted ζ term 1.003). Selberg zeros ρ/2: infinitely many off the line (TAA Lemma 141). TAA Lemma 148: per-resonance decay rates read for 79 ρ/2 (γ < 200), all consistent with ¼ (calibration).

concepts.name: Spec ℤ is terminal
concepts.plain: Spec ℤ has no base to fiber over, unlike a curve over F_q.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Spec ℤ ×_ℤ Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ (TAA Lemma 65 THM), so the "square" must be built elsewhere (arithmetic site, Borger). TAA Lemma 137: Spec ℤ is terminal ⇒ Yoneda gives uniqueness only. TAA Lemma 140: π₁ét(Spec ℤ) = 1.

concepts.name: Spinor/Clifford route
concepts.plain: Encode J and F as a Clifford pair; ghosts give the indefinite Cl(1,1).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 101/TAA Lemma 110: ghosts give Cl(1,1); true case Cl(2,0).

concepts.name: Three indices that must not be conflated: Fredholm index, negative (Pontryagin) index, conserved charge
concepts.plain: Three different 'indices' must not be conflated: the Fredholm index dim ker − dim coker (a homotopy invariant of an operator); the negative (Pontryagin) index κ = n₋ of a Hermitian form (a congruence invariant by Sylvester's law, which is what the ghost count and the arithmetic Hodge index theorem are about); and a conserved charge (a Noether quantity of a flow). An 'index-zero conservation law' that moves between them is not a theorem. Recorded as a correction in v1.6.1.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Three indices that must not be conflated: Fredholm index, negative (Pontryagin) index, conserved charge.
concepts.formula: ind F = dim ker F − dim coker F;  κ(H) = n₋(H) (Sylvester);  Q = ∫ j⁰ (Noether)
pitfalls: An "index-zero conservation law" that moves between the three notions is not a theorem; the ghost count and the arithmetic Hodge index theorem concern κ = n₋, not a Fredholm index.

rels.note: the ghost count is a statement about κ = n₋
Pontryagin spaces carry the negative index κ

concepts.name: Weil Rosetta stone
concepts.plain: Weil’s analogy number fields / function fields / Riemann surfaces.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 140: Rosetta table (loop, H¹, 1 ⊕ 𝕃, counts, involution, sign); the Spec ℤ sign cell is missing (Weil positivity ⇔ RH). Column 2’s sign is the dim-2 algebraic shadow of Hodge–Riemann (surface + ample + RR ⇒ Hodge index). Weil’s 1940 letter quotes read at source (Krieger, Notices 52(3)).

concepts.name: Real-rooted exponential sums are restricted Lee–Yang polynomials
concepts.plain: Every real-rooted exponential polynomial is, up to a zero-free factor, a multivariate Lee–Yang polynomial restricted to a line; at most two thirds of the zeros of a real-rooted trigonometric polynomial can be zeta zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Real-rooted exponential sums are restricted Lee–Yang polynomials. Sources: arXiv:2610.26705.

concepts.name: A positive but non-coercive metric loses the zeros
concepts.plain: For the Bender–Brody–Muller Hamiltonian, the candidate metric is positive with trivial kernel but not coercive; its completion carries only the dilation generator with continuous spectrum and no zeta eigenstates.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: A positive but non-coercive metric loses the zeros. Sources: arXiv:2607.19067.

concepts.name: Two-component Lee–Yang can fail
concepts.plain: The Lee–Yang property holds for one-component Ising and two-component XY spins but fails for complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos; tail behaviour of the single-site law decides it.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Two-component Lee–Yang can fail. Sources: arXiv:1708.08820.

concepts.name: Window Weil form: simple even ground state, certified
concepts.plain: Certified bounds show the compact-window Weil form is positive on a window 2.3 times the classical range, with a simple even ground state, the hypothesis used by rank-one zeta spectral triples.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Window Weil form: simple even ground state, certified. Sources: arXiv:2608.24827; arXiv:2511.22755.

concepts.name: Cohesion (arena)
concepts.plain: Cohesion is the arena, not the surface.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 141 §3: cohesion is the arena, not the surface; the étale ∞-topos of Spec ℤ is not cohesive (pro-shape, Hoyois); new Thm: [ℕ^×, Set] is not cohesive (Γ has no right adjoint). D10 (relative cohesion). TAA Lemma 146 §5: the cohesion quadruple Π ⊣ Disc ⊣ Γ ⊣ coDisc is a line without sign; RLGC is a 2×2 grid with mirror/KK/sign — numerology only.
pitfalls: Heaviside ≠ cohesion one-to-one.

concepts.name: Kramers–Kronig relations
concepts.plain: Causal response: real (dispersive) and imaginary (absorptive) parts determine each other. Absorption’s sign is the passivity condition.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146: dispersion = phase (ghost-blind), absorption sign = passivity ⇔ Lagarias ⇔ RH. TAA Lemma 154: for ξ′/ξ on a line σ: Im = −H[Re] + Σ_{β>σ} −2(t−γ)/((σ−β)²+(t−γ)²) [T]; FFT check on DH/ζ models (zeros |γ−100| < 40, t ∈ [−1900, 2100]): residual ≤ 1e−4 when no zero is right of σ; DH ghost term recovered to ≤ 9.5e−5. KK alone is an identity either way (TAA Lemma 146, correction 3); the sign of Re carries RH.
pitfalls: Passivity implies causality, not conversely (TAA Lemma 146).

concepts.name: No-ghost theorem ↔ Gupta–Bleuler quotient of the window form (Analogy)
concepts.plain: In string theory 24 transverse oscillators each contribute ½ζ(−1) = −1/24 to the vacuum energy, giving intercept a = 1; null spurious states decouple and the physical quotient has no negative-norm states (no ghosts), with one tachyon at level 0. On the arithmetic side, Weil’s window form has one negative square (the pole), the pole’s null line is quotiented out (Gupta–Bleuler), and the quotient is positive exactly when RH holds. The dictionary is good at the level of "a null line quotiented out of an index-1 space". It breaks at what forces the critical point: in the string an algebra (Virasoro, central charge 24) forces it; on our side nothing does.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: No-ghost theorem ↔ Gupta–Bleuler quotient of the window form (Analogy). From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma). Goddard–Thorn 1972 and Brower 1972 are cited by name (not opened); the string-side statements are standard textbook content.
numbers: indefinite Fock space ↔ Weil form Z_ℓ with one negative square [Analogy, good]
null spurious states decoupled ↔ pole null line e, quotient e^⊥/e [Analogy, good]
no ghosts ⇔ positive physical quotient ↔ W ≥ 0 on the primitive part ⇔ RH [Analogy; circular as a criterion]
one tachyon ↔ one Perron/pole mode for ζ; none for Δ (no pole); the Eisenstein part E₁₂ (L = ζ(s)ζ(s−11)) has poles [Analogy]
intercept a = 1 from 24·(1/24) ↔ the pole of ζ at s = 1: a coincidence [Heuristic] — the pole comes from the divergence of Σn^(−s) (Haar measure), not from a zero-point sum
critical dimension fixed by the central charge ↔ no analogue found [Open]
pitfalls: The no-ghost theorem gives a ghost-free spectrum for a = 1 and D ≤ 26; it is not "unitary iff D = 26". D = 26 is the critical point where an extra family of null states decouples and light-cone Lorentz invariance closes.

concepts.name: Equivalence-principle gap across a collision: TAA Lemma 157 gap 1 − 2β is 0 before and at the merge and opens ∝ (t* − t)^{1/2} after; RH read as ζ on the EP side, at its edge (at infinity)
concepts.plain: TAA Lemma 157's gap between the two Verschiebungs is zero while a zero sits on the line and opens once a pair splits off. If you call that gap the difference between inertial and gravitational mass, RH says ζ obeys the equivalence principle, but only just.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: [T, TAA Lemma 157] ⟨(Θ^∨ − Θ†)v, v⟩ = 1 − 2β for an eigenvector with eigenvalue β + iγ. Along a dBN collision: 0 before (both real), 0 at the double zero, ±(1 − 2β) after, growing like (t* − t)^{1/2} by the fold law. [N] DH certified gaps 0.617034364913, 0.301660161219, 0.148712100902, 0.448515389254 (TAA Lemma 156/TAA Lemma 157). [A] 'inertial = gravitational' ↔ dual = adjoint. Flags: the EP is postulated in physics (renaming, not mechanism); the gap is computed from zeros (circular unless Θ† comes from an Euler-product metric, MP4 sharp).
pitfalls: Postulated in physics: reading RH as the EP is a restatement (TAA Lemma 160, correction 8).
No Lagrangian with these two masses exists.

concepts.name: Gribov ambiguity
concepts.plain: In QCD the gluon propagator violates positivity (it changes sign in Euclidean time) — the physics example of a "spectral weight" that is not positive.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §3: Gribov C(t) re-derived to 1e−16, first sign change t* = π/(2√2 M) = 1.1107 (in units of M). Interpretation as positivity violation is interpretive (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).
pitfalls: Gluon positivity violation as confinement evidence is interpretive (TAA Lemma 146 corrections).

concepts.name: Metaplectic / Kubota cocycle
concepts.plain: A 2-valued cocycle on SL₂ behind half-integer weight; structure without sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §4: Kubota cocycle is a phase (Ax3); Hilbert product formula 300/300, quadratic reciprocity; θ weight ½ is metaplectic (a fourth root, TAA Lemma 141 §7) — mod 2 data, ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 151: θ multiplier eighth roots = Weil index; local covers split over SL₂(ℤ_p), p odd [BIB]; obstruction at 2 and ∞ = half-twist ±1.

concepts.name: Half Tate twist ℚ(½)
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ℚ(1) cyclotomic, H² = ℚ(−1); ℚ(½) not canonical: ℓ-adic F(½) needs a chosen √p (Katz–Rojas-León, opened); g_p² = (−1/p)p gives canonical √(p*) ∈ ℚ(ζ_p); √p for p ≡ 3 mod 4 costs √−1 (disc ℚ(√p) = 4p: ramified at 2; p* < 0: sign at ∞). Over ℝ canonical: Connes's E(f)(g) = |g|^{½} Σ f(qg) and C(1) = (j,λ) ↦ |j|λ. Two product formulas: ∏|x|_v = 1 (size: norm map, scaling flow, √ = critical line) vs ∏(a,b)_v = 1 (phase, obstruction at 2). HEURISTIC nexus: Deninger's cohomology contains an honest ℚ(½), MP4 stated on H¹(½); all twist data ghost-blind.

concepts.name: Bost–Connes KMS states
concepts.plain: A quantum statistical system whose partition function is ζ(β); its positive KMS states and phase transition at β = 1 see ζ only at real β > 1, never the zeros.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: BC95 (Thm 5; CM08 3.32): Q-structure, Gal(Q^cycl/Q) symmetry, positive KMS states, ζ(β) real for β > 1; no trace equal to the Weil distribution found (TAA Lemma 30). TAA Lemma 38: strongest rigorous bridge; BC time is dual to rapidity, (β,t) = (Re s, −Im s); BC ordered phase ⇔ ω > ½. TAA Lemma 39: BC = tensor product over primes twisted by Galois. TAA Lemma 54/TAA Lemma 118: KMS/passivity uses ζ at real β > 1 ⇒ ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 162: the precise form of 'local boosts become global rotations' is KMS periodicity in imaginary time (Bisognano–Wichmann/Unruh); p^{−it} is the Bost–Connes time evolution; DH has no primon gas. TAA Lemma 164: B2 negative: KMS/Bochner positivity = non-negative multiplicities; Epstein Z_Q passes and has off-line zeros; BC's arithmetic = multiplicativity (Hecke algebra, Galois), i.e. the Euler product.
numbers: TAA Lemma 159: BC95 Thm 5 re-read (lit/lemma31/bc95.txt): 0 < β < 1 unique KMS (III₁); β > 1 simplex over embeddings of ℚ^cycl (I∞), normalization 1/ζ(β), T_c = 1; §1 KMS strip F(t + iβ) and log Tr e^{−βH} = sup(S − βφ(H))
TAA Lemma 159: φ_β(t) = ζ(β+it)/ζ(β) positive definite (Toeplitz min eig 1.3e−10 at β = 2); DH −7.78
pitfalls: BC95 Thm 5(a) states β < 1 (β ≤ 1 from CM08 3.32) (TAA Lemma 38 flag).

concepts.name: Functional equation ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s)
concepts.plain: ζ’s completed version is symmetric under s ↦ 1 − s. Ghosts satisfy it too, so it cannot prove RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ξ(s) = ξ(1 − s); DH satisfies FE to 5×10⁻¹⁵ yet Re ξ′/ξ = −66.8 off the line (TAA Lemma 146). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Symmetry is phase data, never sign.

concepts.name: Gauss-sum unitarity |g| = √p (RH for a CM curve as a unitarity identity)
concepts.plain: A quadratic Gauss sum has absolute value exactly √p: this is the statement that the finite Fourier transform is unitary. For the CM curve y² = x³ − x and p ≡ 1 mod 4, the Frobenius eigenvalue is a Gaussian integer π with ππ̄ = p, so RH for this curve is the same kind of unitarity identity.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |g|² = p (checked numerically for all odd p ≤ 691) = Plancherel for the finite Fourier transform, the same |x|^{½} twist as TAA Lemma 145. For p ≡ 1 mod 4, π ∈ ℤ[i], ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π, so |α| = √p is automatic. Over ℚ the analogue |ε| = 1 of a root number holds for Davenport–Heilbronn too: necessary, not sufficient. Open: a ζ-analogue in which the eigenvalue itself is a Gauss sum.
concepts.formula: |g|² = p, ππ̄ = p, a_p = 2 Re π
pitfalls: Unitarity identities of this kind are Ax3 (phase); over ℚ they are satisfied by DH too and cannot replace the sign.

rels.note: CM case: |π|² = p as a norm identity
Gauss sum = Weil index phase of the reflection (TAA Lemma 151)

concepts.name: E₂ anomaly (E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy))
concepts.plain: E₂ fails to be modular; fixing it costs a non-holomorphic term 3/(πy) tied to the pole. One reading treats the failure as a 2-class.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: E₂(−1/z) = z²E₂(z) + 12z/(2πi)… corrected by E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy), modular of weight 2. Ghost-blind (phase/automorphy data).
concepts.uncertain: Exact transformation constant quoted from standard theory; the 2-class reading is conjectural.

concepts.name: Half turn = sign flip (S² = −I, root number, Hardy Z sign changes)
concepts.plain: Turning by 180° is a sign: it flips modular forms of odd weight, gives the root number, and is the sign change of Hardy’s Z at each zero on the line.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: S² = −I in SL₂(ℤ) acts by (−1)^k on weight k (odd weights vanish; weight ½ needs the metaplectic cover). s ↦ 1 − s is the 180° rotation about ½; its sign is the root number (+1 for ζ, −1 for 37a1, forcing L(E,1) = 0). Hardy Z(t) = e^{iϑ(t)} ζ(½ + it) is real; it changes sign at each on-line zero of odd order. An off-line pair adds 2 to N(T) and no sign change. TAA Lemma 152 NUM (t ∈ [10,120], step 0.01): ζ 38 sign changes / 38 zeros; DH 62 / 66, the two deficits of 2 exactly in [80,90] and [110,120] (off-line pairs 85.699, 114.163). ℝP¹ = directions mod 180°; tautological bundle = Möbius band (the sign).
numbers: DH: 62 sign changes vs N = 66; 5 vs 7 on [80,90] and [110,120]
pitfalls: Ghost-blind at on-line zeros (DH flips like ζ); off-line zeros appear only as missing flips against a global count N(T) (argument principle, Turing-type): detection, not positivity (TAA Lemma 152, correction 8).
TAA Lemma 158: every quadratic form has Q(−x) = Q(x): the half turn persists through the F/V merge; ghost-blind. The signal is the sign pattern (definite → indefinite).

rels.note: s ↦ 1 − s half turn; root number
the wedge is the sign layer, not the missing surface (TAA Lemma 152, correction 8)

concepts.name: Hecke on S³ (Lubotzky–Phillips–Sarnak): for p ≡ 1 mod 4 the p+1 norm-p quaternions act on S³/±1 and on PSL/PGL(2,F_q) Cayley graphs; constant function eigenvalue p+1 (= ζ frame √p + 1/√p after normalizing), all other eigenvalues |λ| ≤ 2√p (Ramanujan via Deligne/Eichler) = elliptic frames; unique factorization ⇒ (p+1)-regular tree
concepts.plain: Multiplying by the p+1 quaternions of norm p is an averaging operator on the 3-sphere. The constant function is its one 'big' eigenvector, which is the ζ-type piece. Every other eigenvalue is at most 2√p, which is the Ramanujan bound and the compact, rotation-type piece.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N] X^{5,13} (2184, PGL bipartite) max nontrivial |λ| 4.2497 ≤ 4.4721; X^{13,17} (2448) 7.0902 ≤ 7.2111; X^{17,13} (1092) 7.8509 ≤ 8.2462; X^{5,17} (4896) 4.3089 ≤ 4.4721. Hecke T_p on SO(3) harmonics ℓ ≤ 15: max |λ| 4.2841 (p = 5), 7.0075 (p = 13). Primitive norm-p^k counts (p+1)p^{k−1} (k ≤ 3). [C] LPS Combinatorica 8 (1988) 261–277; CPAM 39 (1986) S149–S186 (bibliographic + reference list). [T] trivial rep ↔ Eisenstein/ζ (hyperbolic, poles side); cusp part ↔ compact, Ramanujan. DH has no Hecke eigen-system here (c(2)c(3) = −κ² ≠ c(6) = 1).
pitfalls: The 2√p bound uses Deligne (Weil conjectures) — it is input, not output.
The trivial eigenvalue p+1 is ζ's frame; ζ's zeros are not eigenvalues here.

concepts.name: Moser/Souriau: bound Kepler orbits at fixed E < 0 form S²×S² with coordinates j± = (L ± A′)/2, |j₊| = |j₋| = 1/(2√(−2E)); H²(S²×S²) intersection form [[0,1],[1,0]] (signature (1,1): diagonal +2, anti-diagonal −2 — Hodge-index shape); perturbations of a compact orbit average to slow precession of A at fixed |A|, unbound orbits only deflect
concepts.plain: Each bound Kepler orbit of a given energy is labelled by two points, one on each of two spheres, so the space of orbits is a product of two spheres. Its intersection pattern has one positive and one negative direction, the same shape Weil used. A small push to a closed orbit only makes it precess slowly; an open orbit is just deflected once.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] (1e−15, 200 random bound states) L·A′ = 0 ⇒ |j₊| = |j₋|; [C] Moser CPAM 23 (1970) 609–636 (regularization: Kepler flow at E < 0 ↔ geodesic flow on S³; oriented great circles of S³ = S²×S²). Exact Kepler: A conserved at every energy (no precession, no snapping back, TAA Lemma 162 correction to); E = 0 changes only the rescaling A′ = A/√(∓2E): so(4) vs so(3,1). [A] product surface with one positive and one negative direction, cf. Weil's C×C; Euler product ↔ hidden symmetry, DH κ-mix ↔ symmetry-breaking perturbation: precession (zeros move on the line) vs escape (Krein collision). [T] FE rigidity: in span{Λ(χ), Λ(χ̄)} the FE holds only for c = κ (one complex line), so an A4 test family must leave the span. Hydrogen level n = (j,j), j = (n−1)/2, Casimir (n²−1)/4: every n, no prime distinction.
pitfalls: In exact Kepler A does not precess at any energy.
S²×S² ↔ Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ is Analogy.

rels.note: orbit space of the SO(4) picture

concepts.name: Nash–Kuiper flexibility / Onsager threshold
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: No 'Nash–Kuiper transform': Nash 1954 / Kuiper 1955 C¹ isometric embeddings (flat torus in ℝ³, crumpled sphere); rigidity of convex surfaces for C^{1,α}, α > 2/3 (Borisov; Cohn-Vossen, Herglotz, Pogorelov for C²); h-principle α < 1/(1+n+n²) (CDS), 1/5 for 2D disks (DIS); threshold open in [1/5, 2/3] (½ suggested). Onsager 1/3 settled (CET 1994; Isett; BDLSV 2019). Cao–Hirsch–Inauen 1/3⁻ is Monge–Ampère, not isometric. ANALOGY: DH = the Nash–Kuiper surface (FE + phases, no Frobenius/H¹/cup ⇒ zeros unpinned).

concepts.name: Apsides = zeros of the dual-minus-adjoint gap form: for v′ = Xv, X ∈ sl₂(ℝ), r·v = ½⟨(Xᵀ − X^∨)v, v⟩; apsides are the null lines of the squeeze part; circle ⇔ gap ≡ 0 ⇔ dual = Euclidean adjoint (τ = i)
concepts.plain: In a two-dimensional orbit the radial speed is exactly TAA Lemma 157's dual-minus-adjoint gap. It vanishes at the apsides, where position and velocity are perpendicular, and it vanishes everywhere only for a circle, which is the case where the dual and the adjoint agree.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] ω-dual X^∨ = −X (Hamiltonian), Euclidean adjoint Xᵀ; r·v = vᵀXv = ½⟨(Xᵀ − X^∨)v, v⟩ = vᵀ Sym(X) v (TAA Lemma 157 gap form, reference metric). Apsides (r ⊥ v) = null directions of Sym(X) (the 𝔭/squeeze part of the polar decomposition). For the preserved metric g_τ (S_t) X is skew, so the S-adjoint of X equals X^∨: the gap is identically 0 — the apsidal gap measures reference (i) vs preserved (τ) complex structure. Invariant form: e_K = tanh d_H(i, τ), e_H² = 1 − e^{−2d_H(i,τ)} (any SL₂-conjugate; 200 random, 6e−8). [N] 200 random X: 1e−12; orbit t = 1: 4 zeros of r·v per period at the 45°/135° axes. Ghost-blind (archimedean, one frame).
pitfalls: The gap uses the Euclidean (reference) adjoint; for the preserved metric g_τ it is identically zero.
Eccentricity is gauge-dependent: a squeeze conjugation changes e but not F, V (TAA Lemma 161, correction 4).

concepts.name: Cup product / Poincaré duality pairing
concepts.plain: The pairing of cohomology classes; it gives the duality partner of a zero, ghosts included.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Duality partner via cup product (TAA Lemma 93); positivity needs conjugate + Hodge structure (HR).

concepts.name: Hecke operators
concepts.plain: Averaging operators on modular forms; self-adjointness gives real eigenvalues but not the Ramanujan bound.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Hecke self-adjoint ⇒ a_p ∈ ℝ, not |a_p| ≤ 2√p (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind (TAA Lemma 146). TAA Lemma 160: a_{p^k} = p^{k/2}U_k(t_p/2) — each Hecke eigenvalue is one frame; multiplicativity = product of frames; per-frame ellipticity (Ramanujan) is not known to imply GRH (Open). TAA Lemma 162: LPS Hecke on S³/±1 and PSL/PGL(2,F_q) graphs: trivial p+1 vs |λ| ≤ 2√p (4 graphs, ≤ 4896 vertices; S² harmonics ℓ ≤ 15).
pitfalls: a_p are not BSD generators.

concepts.name: Compact vs non-compact real forms of so(4,ℂ) = sl₂ℂ ⊕ sl₂ℂ: so(4) = su(2)⊕su(2) (Killing (0,6), S³), so(3,1) = sl(2,ℂ)_ℝ ((3,3), H³/Lorentz), so(2,2) = sl(2,ℝ)⊕sl(2,ℝ) ((4,2)); SO(2,2)₀ = (SL₂ℝ×SL₂ℝ)/±1 on AdS₃ = SL₂ℝ by x ↦ g x h⁻¹ is the F/V animation's own G×G, the non-compact twin of SO(4) on S³; rotation = elliptic, boost = hyperbolic (ζ: φ = ½ log p), null rotation = parabolic
concepts.plain: The same complex symmetry has three real versions: all rotations (compact, the 3-sphere), the Lorentz group (rotations plus boosts), and two copies of SL(2,ℝ) acting on anti-de Sitter space, which is the group the F/V animation already uses. Only the all-rotation version has bounded orbits and finite unitary pictures. ζ's prime frames are boosts.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Killing signatures computed: so(4) (0,6), so(3,1) (3,3), so(2,2) (4,2). SL₂ℝ×SL₂ℝ preserves det (signature (2,2)) on M₂(ℝ); diagonal = conjugation preserves tr = (F+V)/√q (2e−12). Lorentz: [K_i,K_j] = −ε J_k (convention), N± = (J ± iK)/2 commute only after complexification; K → iK gives so(4) (Killing (0,6)) — Weyl's unitary trick. Compact ⇔ bounded orbits, unit-circle eigenvalues, every finite-dim/unitary rep unitarizable; SO(3,1): non-trivial irreducible unitary reps infinite-dimensional. e^{iθJ} = cos θ + iJ sin θ needs J² = 1 (fails for spin-1 J_z: 0.235). Pauli: L² + A′² = −1/(2E) (E < 0, A′ = A/√(−2E)), A′² − L² = 1/(2E) (E > 0); L·A = 0; E_n = −1/2n² (1e−13). [A] definite energy = sign of the Casimir = compact real form (Theorem for Kepler; Analogy for ζ). [O] which real form is ζ's G×G. TAA Lemma 163: objective scoring K1–K7: SO(2,2) on AdS₃ unique 7/7 for the frame side ( adopted, scoped); SU(1,1) = SL₂ℝ, SL₂ℂ = so(3,1); sp(4,ℝ) not a form of so(4,ℂ).
pitfalls: N± split is complex; real boosts mix the two factors.
Sign of [K,K] is convention; the relative flip vs [J,J] is what matters.
"Purely imaginary generators" is the Hermitian physics convention.
