concepts.name: Archimedean place and Γ_ℝ factor
concepts.plain: The "prime at infinity": its Gamma factor contributes a term to the Weil form that can be positive or negative depending on the window.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Γ_ℝ contributes the arch functional to W; arch-only positivity holds on thresholds a* (TAA Lemma 127), ghost-blind.
pitfalls: ∞ is not the frame bundle.

concepts.name: Cusp forms & Petersson positivity
concepts.plain: Cusp forms have positive Petersson norm — a real positivity, but it does not see ζ’s zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ⟨f,f⟩ = ∫|f|²y^k dμ > 0; HR = 2 × Petersson (TAA Lemma 134). Ghost-blind for ζ (TAA Lemma 146).
pitfalls: Positive but about cusp forms, not ζ’s spectral weights.

concepts.name: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (Connes–Consani RR)
concepts.plain: The χ in the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch is an Euler characteristic: sections minus obstructions of a divisor D. It is a number attached to D, not a character of a Galois group.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: CC23 over 𝕊: χ(D) = dim H⁰(D) − dim H¹(D) = ⌈deg₂D⌉′ + 1 (TAA Lemma 147). TAA Lemma 145 parity: a linear χ is odd in D and never contains D²; the Hodge-index step needs a quadratic χ (D²/2 term). TAA Lemma 147: χ(D) + χ(−D) = 2 (deg₂D ∉ ℤ). TAA Lemma 160: χ-type vs h-type counts (invariant_vs_refined_count): χ conserved, h^i semicontinuous; for zeros, total count conserved, on-line count changes only at collisions.
pitfalls: Notation clash: this χ is an Euler characteristic, not the character χ (or ω) of the 691 class-group eigenspace.

concepts.name: Mazur–Wiles main conjecture ("Euler characteristic = L-value")
concepts.plain: The size of each Teichmüller piece of the class group (and of the Iwasawa module up the cyclotomic tower) equals the p-part of an L-value; slogan: an algebraic Euler characteristic equals an analytic L-value.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Mazur–Wiles 1984: characteristic ideal of the χ-part of the Iwasawa module = ideal of the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function. Finite-level consequence: #A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) = p-part of L(0, ωᵏ⁻¹) (Ribet, Berkeley slides). TAA Lemma 66: main conjecture = Hilbert–Pólya-type with free p-adic unitarity (γ eigenvalues are 1-units); μ = 0 is not a positivity; no positivity found on the Iwasawa side (OPEN).
pitfalls: Iwasawa theory measures sizes (orders, characteristic ideals), never the sign of D²; it cannot by itself give Weil positivity.
"Euler characteristic = L-value" is a slogan (Heuristic wording), the theorem is the equality of ideals.

concepts.name: Connes–Consani 2021: Weil positivity at the archimedean place (support [2^{−1/2}, 2^{1/2}])
concepts.plain: Connes and Consani explain why Weil’s form is positive for test functions too narrow to see the prime 2: it dominates a trace on Sonin space.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Selecta Math. (N.S.) 27 (2021) no. 4, art. 77 (arXiv 2006.13771, opened). Weil's inequality: f smooth positive definite, supp f ⊂ (1/2, 2), f̂(±i/2) = 0 ⇒ W∞(f) ≥ 0 (proved by Yoshida 1992 by explicit computation); ⇔ QW(g) = W∞(g∗g*) ≥ 0 for supp g ⊂ [2^{−1/2}, 2^{1/2}], ĝ(i/2) = 0. Support (1/2,2) chosen so that no rational prime enters. Thm 1: if also ĝ(0) = 0, W∞(g∗g*) ≥ Tr(ϑ(g) S ϑ(g)*), S = projection on Sonin space; Thm 6.11: without ĝ(0) = 0, ≥ Tr(...) − c|ĝ(0)|², 13 < c < 17. Their abstract method alone reaches I = [u⁻¹,u], u = 1.10246 (Cor 8) / 1.15077 (Rem 9); [1/2,2] needs Sonin/prolate and numerics (§6). In log scale: f supported in |u| < log 2 = the first prime atom; TAA Lemma 25's OS-RP fails exactly when the atom log 2 enters. Ghost-blind (archimedean only).

concepts.name: What each 𝔽₁ approach builds in place of Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ
concepts.plain: Each 𝔽₁ theory either collapses the square back to Spec ℤ (Durov), replaces it by something huge (Borger's Witt space, Connes–Consani's tropical square), or skips it (Deninger). None yet carries a proved sign.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: [C, opened] Manin/Soulé: ask for Spec ℤ ×_{Spec 𝔽₁} Spec ℤ, motivated by C × C in Weil's proof (Soulé 2004 §1.2). Durov: forces Spec ℤ ×_{𝔽₁} Spec ℤ ≅ Spec ℤ, 'unsuitable to pursue Deninger's program' (López Peña–Lorscheid). Borger (Λ-rings): 𝔽₁-structure on flat X = commuting Frobenius lifts ψ_p; 'Spec Z ×_{Spec F1} Spec Z must be defined to be the Witt space W*(Spec Z)'; 'says nothing about the archimedean place'. Haran (abstract only): F-rings with an arithmetical surface Spec O_K × Spec O_K. Connes–Consani: square of the arithmetic site = topos N̂^{×2} with ℤ_min ⊗_B ℤ_min (reduced: Newton polygons), points over ℝ_max⁺ = product of points, Frobenius correspondences Ψ(λ) as congruences (CC16); H¹/RR on the square open (CC19); ℤ ⊗_𝕊 ℤ non-trivial over 𝕊-algebras (Connes essay). Deninger: no square; H¹ with flow. [T,N] Witt link: big Witt W_12(ℤ): F_nV_n = n (ghost), V_nF_n = V_n(1)·, projection formula V_n(x·F_n y) = V_n(x)·y, F₂F₃ = F₆, integrality — the pairing side (sign-free) of TAA Lemma 157's two Verschiebungs (Analogy).
numbers: Witt checks: F_nV_n = n, projection formula, F₂F₃ = F₆, integrality (N = 12)
pitfalls: Witt 'ghost components' are unrelated to TAA ghosts (off-line zeros).
Haran: abstract only, not opened.
Earlier TAA record (lit/lemma30/verified_refs.md) called 'ℤ⊗_{𝔽₁}ℤ = ℤ' for Borger a deduction; Borger's own definition gives W*(Spec ℤ) (TAA Lemma 158, correction 8).

concepts.name: Herbrand–Ribet: ω¹⁻ᵏ eigenspace of Cl(ℚ(μ_p)) and p | B_k
concepts.plain: The p-part of the class group of ℚ(μ_p) splits into pieces labelled by powers of the Teichmüller character ω. The piece ω¹⁻ᵏ is nonzero exactly when p divides the Bernoulli number B_k; for p = 691, k = 12 this is the ω⁻¹¹ piece.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: For odd p and even k, 2 ≤ k ≤ p−3: A(ω¹⁻ᵏ) ≠ 0 ⇔ p | B_k (Herbrand 1932 ⇒, Ribet 1976 ⇐). p = 691, k = 12: B₁₂ = −691/2730, class in ω⁻¹¹ = ωᵖ⁻¹² (same character, since ω has order p − 1); odd character ⇒ minus part. TAA Lemma 66: 691 has two irregular indices (12, 200), so Cl/691 is 2-dim (ω⁻¹¹, ω⁻¹⁹⁹); ρ_{Δ,691} ss = 1 ⊕ ω¹¹, the non-split extension gives the ω⁻¹¹ class via CFT (Greenberg–Monsky lattices).
pitfalls: Notation: det ρ_Δ = χ_cyc¹¹ (cyclotomic character), whose reduction mod 691 is ω¹¹; the class itself sits in ω⁻¹¹ (TAA Lemma 66).
Ribet 1976 used weight-2 forms on Γ₁(p), not Δ.
Some authors write ωᵖ⁻¹²; it is the same eigenspace.

rels.note: size statement implied by the main conjecture
sizes, not signs: ghost-blind residual data (TAA Lemma 66)

concepts.name: The n! bridge: n! carries every place (Γ/Stirling at ∞; v_p(n!), Morita's Γ_p and Gauss sums at p), tied by the product formula; each place is ghost-blind, so what is missing is a positivity coupling all places at once
concepts.plain: The factorial already contains the archimedean data (the Gamma function) and the p-adic data (how often each prime divides it). Each piece alone cannot tell ζ from a fake; what is missing is something that ties all of them together with a sign.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [Theorem] Chebyshev: log n! = Σ_{d≤n} Λ(d)⌊n/d⌋ (log = Λ ∗ 1; exact for n = 10, 100, 1000). Legendre: v_p(n!) = (n − s_p(n))/(p − 1) (100!, p = 2, 3, 5, 7). Stirling/Γ: n! = Γ(n+1), Γ the archimedean factor (error 2.7e−12 at n = 1000). Product formula |n!|_∞ Π_p |n!|_p = 1 (exact for n = 20). F₁ limit |GL_n(F_q)|/(q−1)^n → n! (2, 6, 24); the F₁ reading is a Heuristic (Tits/Soulé, not opened). [Cited] Morita 1975 p-adic Γ_p (values in ℤ_p^×); Gross–Koblitz 1979: Gauss sums = π-power × products of Γ_p values. Link to the SL(2,F_p) half representations: character values (±1 ± √(εp))/2 with √(εp) the quadratic Gauss sum, g_p² = εp; consistency mod p ((p−1)/2)!² ≡ (−1)^{(p+1)/2} for p < 1000. Ghost check: DH shares Γ; its c ∗ a = a·log needs composite c (6, 12, 14, …), so the bridge separates DH only through the support of Λ (the Euler product). Verdict: no new non-archimedean element is needed; what is missing is a positivity coupling all places at once (R8′). The product formula is the only known all-places coupling and is an identity with no sign; provisional definition: a signed product formula on the square (Open).

rels.note: quadratic Gauss sum = Γ_p(½) case of Gross–Koblitz
separates DH only through the support of Λ

concepts.name: Ramanujan congruence τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691 (Δ ≡ E₁₂)
concepts.plain: The cusp form Δ agrees with the Eisenstein series E₁₂ modulo 691, because 691 divides the numerator of ζ(−11). It is the meeting point of the Eisenstein (reference) and cusp-form (primitive) parts of the Hecke algebra.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) mod 691; ζ(−11) = −B₁₂/12 = 691/32760 (constant term of E₁₂ ∝ ζ(−11)/2 = 691/65520, TAA Lemma 70). TAA Lemma 66: τ(p) ≡ 1 + p¹¹ mod 691 for all 9592 p < 10⁵; Hecke congruence moduli N_k = |num(B_k/2k)| = 691, 3617, 43867, … (k = 12, 16, 18, …); bridge = closed point where Eisenstein and cuspidal components of Spec 𝕋 meet. TAA Lemma 70 (Mazur77 at source): Eisenstein ideal 𝕋/𝔍 ≅ ℤ/n, modulus = numerator of an Euler-depleted ζ(1−k); cusp encodes it as a negative zeta value; positivity invisible (timelike f ≡ spacelike E).
pitfalls: The congruence is mod 691 data: it says nothing about the sign of the Weil form (TAA Lemma 66: bridge = where positivity is lost).
E₁₂ has all its zeros off Re s = 6 (unconditional, TAA Lemma 66) — an "all ghost" Euler product.

rels.note: weight-12 rung: E₁₂ reference vs Δ primitive
Eisenstein = reference, cusp form = primitive split

concepts.name: Self-dual / anti-self-dual split as push / shear
concepts.plain: In four Euclidean dimensions the Hodge star splits a field strength into self-dual and anti-self-dual parts. The energy is the sum of their squares and the topological density is the difference. On a Kähler surface the self-dual (1,1) part is the Kähler direction (push) and the anti-self-dual part is the primitive part (shear), so push minus shear is the Hodge-index form pointwise. Saturating the instanton (Bogomolny) bound means zero shear, which is stronger than Hodge index.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Self-dual / anti-self-dual split as push / shear Belavin–Polyakov–Schwarz–Tyupkin, Phys. Lett. B 59 (1975) 85–87.
concepts.formula: ⋆²=1 on Λ²(R⁴); F^± = (F±⋆F)/2; |F|² = |F⁺|²+|F⁻|²; F∧F = (|F⁺|²−|F⁻|²) vol; |F|² ≥ |⟨F,⋆F⟩| with equality iff F = ±⋆F; for F = aω+P (P primitive (1,1)): F∧F = (2a²−|P|²) vol
numbers: real (1,1)-forms on C² form R·ω ⊕ Λ⁻ (dim 4); ω self-dual, primitive forms anti-self-dual (error 2e−16)
Lorentzian signature: ⋆² = −1 on 2-forms (exact), so the split is complex there
pitfalls: the real split needs Euclidean signature
½(E²+B²) is T⁰⁰, not a Lorentz invariant; B²−E² and E·B are indefinite (502/498 signs in 1000 samples); what is positive is u ≥ |E×B| (dominant energy)
energy positivity alone carries no information: it holds for every field

concepts.name: Standing frame of the F/V frame geometry: SO(2,2)₀ = (SL₂ℝ×SL₂ℝ)/±1 on AdS₃ = SL₂ℝ (x ↦ g x h⁻¹), compact dual SO(4) on S³ — the unique candidate meeting seven criteria read off the animation (all frame types; trace-preserving conjugation; transitive sweep through t = ±2; real traces only; real form of so(4,ℂ); all Satake frames of ζ and cusp forms; minimal)
concepts.plain: Of seven candidate symmetry groups for the per-prime frame picture, only SO(2,2) acting on SL(2,R) does everything the animation shows; its compact twin is SO(4) on the 3-sphere. That settles the figures' standing frame, not the RH question.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Candidates evaluated: SO(4) fails K1/K6 (no boosts, ζ frames absent); SO(3,1) ≅ PSL₂ℂ fails K2/K3/K4/K7 (complex traces, loxodromics, no real G×G); SL₂ℝ alone and SU(1,1) (= SL₂ℝ by Cayley) fail K3 (conjugation orbits dim 2) and K5; GL₂ℝ² fails K5/K7; Sp(4,ℝ) ≅ Spin(3,2) not a form of so(4,ℂ), contains so(2,2) as a vector stabilizer. Minimality: the anti-diagonal is an irreducible module of the diagonal sl₂. Satake: ζ's frame (p+1)/√p = endpoint of the spherical unitary dual (trivial rep.); tempered ⇔ |t| ≤ 2 (SU(2) classes). DH: no frames (undefined). Scope: frame side only; ζ's zero-side real form is RH-equivalent.
pitfalls: Frame side only: it does not say which real form ζ's hidden symmetry on H¹ has (that is RH).
SU(1,1) and SL(2,ℂ) are not new candidates: Cayley transform; SL₂ℂ = so(3,1).

concepts.name: Tate count / Picard number (ghost-blind)
concepts.plain: Counting algebraic classes on C×C does not see whether eigenvalues are on the circle.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ρ(C×C) = 2 + Σ m(λ)m(q/λ) (Tate 1966, S–S §14.6); = 2g for squarefree, fakes too (TAA Lemma 93 Prop 2.3).

concepts.name: Consani: archimedean cohomology, N at infinity, Γ-factor as a characteristic polynomial
concepts.plain: At the infinite place there is a proved cohomology whose Frobenius has the Gamma factor as characteristic polynomial; it is purely local.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Consani, Compositio 111 (1998) 323–358 (abstract read): a double complex with a monodromy-type operator N at the archimedean fibre, viewed as 'maximally degenerate' (analogue of LMHS); proves Deninger's conjecture that the archimedean Γ-factor is the (regularized) characteristic polynomial of an archimedean Frobenius on the N-invariants of the hypercohomology. Local only: says nothing about zeros (ghost-blind: DH has the Γ-factor of an odd character mod 5).

concepts.name: PV ↔ TS: dT∧dS = dP∧dV (Maxwell as one area identity); work = heat = enclosed area; PdV, TdS two primitives of one exact 2-form
concepts.plain: The first law makes the pressure–volume picture and the temperature–entropy picture two maps of the same area form: every cycle encloses the same area in both, which is why work equals heat. Work is an area (a flux), not a cohomology class.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] dU = T dS − P dV ⇒ 0 = d(dU) = dT∧dS − dP∧dV, so ω := dT∧dS = dP∧dV on the (fixed-N, 2-dim) state surface: (P,V) and (T,S) are two Darboux charts of one area form, ∂(T,S)/∂(P,V) = 1, and the four Maxwell relations are this identity in the charts (P,S), (T,V), (P,T), (S,V) (Wikipedia 'Maxwell relations' §Jacobians, opened; Ritchie AJP 36 (1968) 760 not opened). Equal area holds for every region, not only cycles; orientation preserved (engine cycles clockwise in (V,P) and in (S,T)). [N] ideal and vdW (a = 1, b = 0.2) gases: Jacobian 1 ± 2e−9 at 200 random points; ellipse cycle W = ∮PdV = 1.272345 = Q = ∮TdS = π·0.9·0.45; Maxwell (∂T/∂P)_S = (∂V/∂S)_P = 0.8 (ideal), 0.9 (vdW). [T] Cochains vs cohomology: P dV and T dS are not closed; both are primitives of ω (d(PdV) = d(TdS) = ω) and differ by dU (first law). State space is contractible, so H¹ = 0: work over a cycle is the flux of ω through the enclosed region (Stokes), not a cohomology class. The honest cohomology in the arithmetic picture: d log ξ is closed on ℂ∖{zeros} (the Fisher zeros are the holes); periods 2πi·multiplicity [N: ζ box at 14.13 → 1.0; DH box around ρ₁ → 1.0; box around ρ₁ and 1−ρ̄₁ → 2.0]: counts, ghost-blind.
pitfalls: It is one 2-form in two charts, valid where (P,V) and (T,S) are both coordinates (fails on coexistence lines).
Work is not a cohomology class on a contractible state space; first law = [δQ − δW] = 0.

rels.note: ω on the state surface; g = Ruppeiner

concepts.name: Thermodynamic geometry: Ruppeiner/Weinhold metrics, contact structure (Mrugała), and the compatible J that a 2-dim state surface always has
concepts.plain: Thermodynamic stability gives a positive metric on the space of states, and the first law gives a contact structure. On a two-dimensional state space a compatible complex structure always exists, so the hard part of MP4, a J commuting with a flow, has no thermodynamic counterpart yet.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [C] Ruppeiner g_R = −Hess S (positive by stability), Weinhold g_W = Hess U, ds_R² = ds_W²/T; flat for non-interacting systems; Lorentzian signature for negative heat capacity (Reissner–Nordström) (Wikipedia, opened). Mrugała 2000 (opened): thermodynamic phase space = (2n+1)-dim contact manifold, Legendre submanifolds = equilibrium states; contact ↔ first law, metric ↔ second law; his G = dp dx + θ⊗θ has signature (n+1, n) (TAA Lemma 116, correction 1). [T] On a 2-dim oriented state surface with metric g and area form ω = f·vol_g (f > 0), J := rotation by 90° in g satisfies J² = −1, g(J·,J·) = g, ω(·, J·) = f g: the triple always exists, so it carries no content here; MP4's content is commutation with a flow (TAA Lemma 157/TAA Lemma 158), and equilibrium thermodynamics has no flow. [N] ideal gas at (U,V) = (3,2): g_R = diag(1/6, 1/4), ω = 1/3 dU∧dV, J² + 1 = 1e−16, Ruppeiner curvature 0; ω = √(2/3)·vol_W identically (sympy); vdW (1, 0.2): curvature 0.2244 (interaction), J² + 1 = 2e−16. TAA Lemma 116: Euler (multiplicative) field ⇒ flat; χ₄ field curved: curvature measures non-multiplicativity, not zeros. Stability = convexity ⇔ Legendre transform finite/involutive (TAA Lemma 153 window; Fenchel–Moreau); non-convex ⇒ convex hull (Maxwell construction, BIB).
pitfalls: In 2D the compatible J is free; do not count it as a missing piece (TAA Lemma 159, correction 13).
Gibbs, Hermann, Weinhold and Ruppeiner primary papers not opened.

rels.note: positivity free, commutation is the content

concepts.name: λ₂ is monotone under nested windows (Cauchy interlacing)
concepts.plain: On a fixed grid, the window spaces are nested: the test functions for a window of length ℓ are among those for any longer window. By Cauchy interlacing every eigenvalue of the arithmetic side Z_ℓ, in particular the second one λ₂, is non-increasing in ℓ. So "λ₂ never reaches 0 as the window passes each log p" is the same as "the infimum of λ₂ over all windows is ≥ 0": the decisive statement is a limit, not a sequence of events at the points log p. The theorem holds for every form, including Davenport–Heilbronn, so it locates where RH is decided rather than deciding it.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: λ₂ is monotone under nested windows (Cauchy interlacing). From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).
concepts.formula: V_ℓ ⊂ V_ℓ′ (ℓ < ℓ′) ⇒ λ_k(Z_ℓ′) ≤ λ_k(Z_ℓ) for every k; RH ⇔ inf_ℓ λ₂(Z_ℓ) ≥ 0 (by the ghost count; circular as a route)
numbers: ζ, box grid h = 0.02: the largest step-to-step increase of λ₂ on ℓ ∈ [0.3, 6] is −3.6e−6 < 0
h = 0.005: the step in λ₂ across log 7, log 11, log 13 and log 16 is at most 1.6 times the median step (no jump at log p)
base case: λ₂ > 0 for ℓ ∈ (0.2295, log 2] (TAA Lemma 182)
pitfalls: Monotonicity needs nested sections (a fixed grid); on families with a fixed number of boxes the sections are not nested.

concepts.name: Primary sign rule for a_p of y² = x³ − x
concepts.plain: For p ≡ 1 mod 4 write p = a² + b² with b even; the sign of a in a_p = 2a is fixed by a 2-adic normalisation (a + b ≡ 1 mod 4). The individual sign is phase data; RH is about the size |a_p| ≤ 2√p, not the sign.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: p = a² + b², b even, a_p = 2a with a + b ≡ 1 mod 4 (π primary mod (1 + i)³); checked for all 14 primes p ≡ 1 mod 4 below 120 (p = 5, 13, 17: a_p = −2, 6, 2). The individual sign is a 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); RH = |a_p| ≤ 2√p is a size statement. The distribution of the signs (Sato–Tate for CM curves) is a separate question; no citation given here. TAA Lemma 150 Prop 3.3: checked on all 147 primes ≡ 1 mod 4 below 2000. Individual sign = 2-adic phase (ghost-blind); the averaged sign is the Sarnak bias 1 − 2r (TAA Lemma 150 §2.1). CM angles: χ² = 0.34 on 10 bins (n = 39,175, p < 1e6), 50.07% positive; Hecke/Deuring equidistribution [BIB, not opened].
concepts.formula: a_p = 2a, p = a² + b², a + b ≡ 1 mod 4
concepts.uncertain: Sato–Tate/Hecke–Deuring citation for CM sign distribution not verified; none given.
pitfalls: The minus sign in a₅ = −2 is not the positivity sign of RH: it is a phase (choice of primary generator), and RH bounds the size.

rels.note: the sign of a_p is not the Castelnuovo sign

concepts.name: Archimedean thresholds a*
concepts.plain: Largest window size where the archimedean part alone is positive.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 127: a*_S2 < 0.5976773 (supersedes TAA Lemma 121’s 0.602); TAA Lemma 98 states a ≤ 1 in another normalization. Ghost-blind.
concepts.uncertain: Normalization between TAA Lemma 98 and TAA Lemma 127 not reconciled here.
pitfalls: Source conflict: TAA Lemma 98 "a ≤ 1" vs TAA Lemma 127 a* < 0.5976773 (different setups/normalizations to check).

concepts.name: Maass–Selberg relations
concepts.plain: Norm of truncated Eisenstein series expressed via φ and φ′; positivity there is automatic.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §8.1: Maass–Selberg ‖Λ^T E‖² minimum 0.611 (ζ) vs 1.383 (DH) over 540 points ⇒ ghost-blind; it only constrains ζ(w) ≠ 0 for Re w > 1 (already known). TAA Lemma 153 (G): on s = ½+it, ‖Λ^T E‖² = 2 log T − (φ′/φ)(½+it) + (φ̄T^{2it} − φT^{−2it})/(2it) (form as in TAA Lemma 69, checked there to ≤ 1.9e−15 by quadrature against Sarnak's (25)); a line in log T with slope 2 and intercept −φ′/φ(½+it) (J. W. McGreevy's y-intercepts). The intercept is not a positive density: −φ′/φ(½+it) = −1.907 at t = 0.5, −0.135 at t = 2, +0.005 at t = 3 (TAA Lemma 153, correction 23). Positivity reaches only the edge Re s = 1 (TAA Lemma 69).

concepts.name: Legendre-symbol linking matrix of primes ≡ 1 mod 4: spectrally random, indefinite, uncorrelated with Weil positivity
concepts.plain: In arithmetic topology primes behave like knots and the Legendre symbol like a linking number. The symmetric matrix of Legendre symbols among primes ≡ 1 mod 4 looks like a random sign matrix: about half its eigenvalues are negative, and its signs are uncorrelated with the Weil Gram coupling matrix. Quadratic linking does not see positivity.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Legendre-symbol linking matrix of primes ≡ 1 mod 4: spectrally random, indefinite, uncorrelated with Weil positivity Morishita, Knots and Primes (Springer 2012); Deninger, arXiv:0709.2801 (3-dimensional foliated dynamical systems, closed orbits as knots).
numbers: sign agreement with the Weil Gram matrix 0.495, correlation −0.008 (z = −1.6)

concepts.name: Slack ledger: record close pairs follow z ~ C/d (exponent 1.0±0.15, C ~ π²/(2 log p log q), no sharp constant); same-branch record jumps are exactly continued-fraction convergent denominators of log q/log p; slack left in [0,Z] is d_min(Z)²/8 ≈ C²/8Z²
concepts.plain: How fast the local slack is used up is governed by how well log q/log p is approximated by fractions.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Slack ledger: record close pairs follow z ~ C/d (exponent 1.0±0.15, C ~ π²/(2 log p log q), no sharp constant); same-branch record jumps are exactly continued-fraction convergent denominators of log q/log p; slack left in [0,Z] is d_min(Z)²/8 ≈ C²/8Z²
pitfalls: Z·d_min stays in [0.11, 5.4]; partial quotients drive the excursions.

concepts.name: Monotone quantities along the de Bruijn–Newman flow: kernel-side entropies are smooth through t = 0; zero-side energy relaxes
concepts.plain: Along the heat flow, the entropy, Fisher information and a one-dimensional Perelman-type functional of the tilted kernel e^{tu²}Φ change smoothly and monotonically, with nothing special at t = 0, so they cannot see the de Bruijn–Newman constant. The zeros' pair energy decreases and their spacing becomes more regular (the Rodgers–Tao gradient-flow picture), but any such zero-side quantity is circular as a route to RH.
concepts.label: Numerical
concepts.core: Monotone quantities along the de Bruijn–Newman flow: kernel-side entropies are smooth through t = 0; zero-side energy relaxes Perelman, arXiv:math/0211159; Rodgers–Tao, arXiv:1801.05914.
concepts.formula: W_min(p) = S − ½ log(2πe/I) ≥ 0; ∂_t x_k = 2Σ_{j≠k} 1/(x_k − x_j), ∂_t 𝓗 = −4E (formal, full system)

concepts.name: Conjecture-level target: a Hopf-type fibration of Spec ℤ (a global Kustaanheimo–Stiefel map) as a Deninger triple with a compact circle/Bohr-torus flow
concepts.plain: The KS map that turns Kepler into an oscillator is the Hopf fibration of S³. In the knots–primes dictionary, its arithmetic analogue would be a three-dimensional foliated system with a compact flow whose closed orbits are the primes; RH would say the net form is a sum of squares in that coordinate. A literal circle action is impossible because the periods log p are incommensurable; the compact object would be the Bohr torus. RH is not proved.
concepts.label: Conjecture

concepts.name: Branch selection by arithmetic
concepts.plain: A square root has a phase ambiguity; the sign-flip fibre is exactly that ambiguity. Positivity of the Weil form is a proxy for joint phase alignment across primes, not for any individual angle, each of which is locally allowed. The branch must be selected by the Galois representation (up to twists).
concepts.label: Heuristic
concepts.core: Branch selection by arithmetic.

concepts.name: Half-density normalization |x|^{½}
aliases: critical line = spectrum of unitary scaling
concepts.plain: Multiplying by |x|^{½} makes scaling unitary on L²; this is why the critical line is at ½.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 145 Thm twist: |x|^½ = (dx/d*x)^½ is unitary L²(dx) → L²(d*x); U_λ unitary with generator −(x∂_x + ½); Mellin is unitary only on Re s = ½ (Plancherel 0.35355339 both sides; at Re 0.4 a weighted norm 0.53173). Cusp gauge y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4). TAA Lemma 153 (E): (U_λ f)(x) = λ^{½}f(λx) on L²(ℝ₊,dx): U_λ x^{−s} = λ^{½−s} x^{−s} (NUM ≤ 2.2e−16), |λ^{½−s}| = 1 for all λ iff Re s = ½ (x^{−s} is a generalized eigenfunction, not in L²). Critical line = unitary spectrum of scaling; this is unitarity (Ax3), not positivity. TAA Lemma 159: β = ½ (the critical line) is inverse temperature ½, i.e. half-density weights n^{−½}, inside the Hagedorn-divergent region (Analogy for the identification).
pitfalls: There are two ½’s (TAA Lemma 145 corrections): the unitary twist and the critical line.

concepts.name: Theta inversion θ(1/t) = √t θ(t)
concepts.plain: Poisson summation gives the functional equation; phase data.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: θ(1/x) = √x θ(x) gives Riemann’s FE and the boundary terms f(0), f̂(0) of 1/(s(s−1)) (TAA Lemma 36 §6). TAA Lemma 138 R4: theta inversion for x² + 5y² to 3e−30; Weil representation unitary, (ST)³ = Gauss sum · I; unitarity ⇒ FE only, ghost-blind (Thm). TAA Lemma 145: θ FE error 6.3e−26; TAA Lemma 146: θ S-error ≤ 2.5e−16, Fresnel = half-density × Weil index. TAA Lemma 151 centrepiece: θ(1/t) = √t θ(t) and ϑ(−1/τ) = √(τ/i) ϑ(τ) to ≤1.5e−51; √(1/i) = (1 − i)/√2 primitive 8th root (√2 in the phase); t^{¼}θ(t) inversion-invariant; unitary inversion on L²(ℝ₊,dx) is x^{−1}f(1/x) (TAA Lemma 151, correction 6). TAA Lemma 153: √(1/i) = e^{−iπ/4} is the Maslov factor of a negative-definite Hessian (stationary phase).

concepts.name: The F/V sweep as an orbit sequence: invariant conics S_t = [[1,−t/2],[−t/2,1]] of g_t keep their apsidal axes at 45°/135° for all t; e_H² = 2t/(t+2); after Bohlin z², Kepler e_K = t/2 = (F+V)/2√q, F/√q = e_K + i b/a; circle → ellipse → parabola (t = 2, F = V, escape) → hyperbola; binding margin 1 − t/2 = 1 − e_K
concepts.plain: As t grows from 0 to 2 the invariant ellipse of the frame stretches along a fixed 45° line, like a planet given ever-larger kicks at periapsis. At t = 2, where F and V meet, the orbit becomes a parabola and escapes; beyond that it is a hyperbola. After squaring (Bohlin's map) the eccentricity is exactly t/2.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] gᵀS_tg = S_t; eigenvectors (1,1),(1,−1) ∀t > 0 (t = 0: S = I). Hooke eccentricity of S_t = 1 (t < 2) and S_t = −1 (t > 2, transverse axis on (1,1)): e_H² = 2c/(1+c), c = t/2 = cos θ | cosh φ; Wick form 1 − tan²(θ/2) → 1 + tanh²(φ/2); other family 1/e² + 1/e′² = 1. Table: t = 1.8165, 1.9.9871, 2.5 1.0541, 4 1.1547; e_H → √2. Bohlin (z ↦ z², Bull. Astr. 28 (1911) 113–119): focal conic with e_K = t/2 exactly (fit residual 1e−9), apsidal line 45° → 90°; F/√q = e_K + i b_K/a_K (elliptic), e^{±φ} = e_K ± b_K/a_K (hyperbolic); r_a/r_p = (1+e_K)/(1−e_K) = −((1+u)/(1−u))², u = F/√q (Cayley). Margin: S_t on (1,1)/√2 = 1 − t/2 = λ_min(S_t) = 1 − e_K = −2E r_p/μ (Kepler binding at fixed periapsis). Periapsis kick from a circle, v = k v_c: e = k² − 1, apsidal line and r_p fixed, escape k = √2 (⇔ t = 2). [N] 38 checks PASS. [A] 45° tilt = the fixed apsidal axis of the animation's normalized norm conic (q-normalized coordinates).
concepts.formula: e_H² = 2t/(t+2); e_K = t/2; F/√q = e_K + i·b/a; margin = 1 − t/2
pitfalls: The F/V real line is in the eigenvalue plane, the apsidal line in phase space (TAA Lemma 161, correction 5).
r_a/r_p ≠ F/V; e ≠ tanh φ (TAA Lemma 161, correction 6).
Definite energy is eroded by the kick, not produced by it (TAA Lemma 161, correction 9).

concepts.name: Eisenstein constant term & scattering φ(s)
concepts.plain: The Eisenstein series’ constant term has two pieces linked by φ(s); on Re s = ½ |φ| = 1 for any zeros — a phase statement.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: φ(s) = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s); |φ(½+it)| = 1 unconditionally (unitarity of scattering). Ghost-blind.
pitfalls: |φ| = 1 is only Ax3.

concepts.name: Gauss half: quadratic character, (p ± 1)/2 and the (p + 1)/4 square-root formula
concepts.plain: Every odd prime p splits the nonzero residues into (p − 1)/2 squares and (p − 1)/2 non-squares; the quadratic character (x/p) records which. For an elliptic curve y² = f(x), a_p is minus the sum of these characters, and its value mod p is a Gauss-half power.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: a_p = −Σ_x (f(x)/p) for y² = f(x); Hasse: a_p ≡ coefficient of x^{p−1} in f^{(p−1)/2} mod p. For p ≡ 3 mod 4, (p + 1)/4 is an integer and √a = a^{(p+1)/4} mod p (691 → 173). y² = x³ − x: a_p = −2, 6, 2 for p = 5, 13, 17; a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, so N₆₉₁ = 692. The Gauss halves see only the coherent H¹(E, 𝒪), i.e. a_p mod p; the bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p needs positivity (Castelnuovo/Hodge index). TAA Lemma 150 Prop 3.1 (THM+NUM): verified for p = 3,5,7,11,13,17,29,37,41,691; 70,563 square roots a^{(p+1)/4} and a_p = 0 for p ≡ 3 mod 4, p < 2000. The half records a_p mod p (Hasse invariant = Frobenius on coherent H¹); the bound needs positivity (TAA Lemma 150 Thm 2.2).
pitfalls: a_p mod p is phase-type information; it does not give the size bound |a_p| ≤ 2√p.
The ½ of (p ± 1)/2 is a counting half; relating it to the half-density ½ is an analogy.

rels.note: the ½ in (p ± 1)/2 vs the unitary |x|^{½} twist; analogy
mod-p data cannot give the size bound; that needs Castelnuovo–Severi
the square root sits here; the inequality does not (TAA Lemma 150)

concepts.name: Hilbert reciprocity at 2: the odd halves become sign bits
concepts.plain: At odd primes the halves (p − 1)/2 count squares; at 2 the corresponding quantities ε(u) = (u − 1)/2 and ω(u) = (u² − 1)/8 are sign bits. Hilbert reciprocity says the sign at 2 is fixed by the odd places and ∞. This is phase information, not positivity.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: (−1/p) = (−1)^{ε(p)}, (2/p) = (−1)^{ω(p)}. 2-adic Hilbert symbol: for a = 2^α u, b = 2^β v with u, v odd units, (a,b)₂ = (−1)^{ε(u)ε(v) + αω(v) + βω(u)} (Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III, Thm 1). Product formula ∏ᵥ (a,b)ᵥ = 1 over all places including ∞ ⇒ the 2-adic sign is determined by the odd places and ∞; it is a restatement of quadratic reciprocity with both supplementary laws. ℚ₂^×/squares has order 8; ℤ₂^×/squares = {±1, ±5} has order 4: two sign bits, ε (sign of −1) and ω (the √2 / χ₈ bit). Checked: product formula holds for 3000 random pairs |a|, |b| ≤ 5000; ε, ω for u = 1, 3, 5, 7: (0,0), (1,1), (0,1), (1,0). Phase data (Ax3), ghost-blind: Davenport–Heilbronn shares the same reciprocity.
numbers: Serre III Thm 1 formula vs PARI hilbert: 3000/3000
concepts.uncertain: to verify: Serre, A Course in Arithmetic, Ch. III Thm 1 not opened here; formula re-checked numerically via the product formula only.
pitfalls: The sign at 2 is a reciprocity sign (phase), not the positivity sign of RH; reading it as the half-density counterpart is an analogy.
Equivalent to quadratic reciprocity, not to RH.
Phase data: DH obeys the same reciprocity (TAA Lemma 150, correction 2).

rels.note: odd halves (p ± 1)/2 ↔ sign bits ε, ω at 2
Hilbert symbol = the cocycle behind the metaplectic cover

concepts.name: The prime 2 as the wild place
concepts.plain: The only even prime is 2 (not √2). At 2 the Gauss halves break: (p − 1)/2 is not an integer, every model y² = f(x) has bad reduction, and the Hilbert symbol / metaplectic cocycle is wild. √2 enters through (2/p), which depends on p mod 8.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Supplementary law: (2/p) = +1 ⇔ p ≡ ±1 mod 8; √2 ∈ ℚ(ζ₈), so (2/p) is the character χ₈ (the √2 family). At p = 2, (p − 1)/2 is not an integer and every Weierstrass model y² = f(x) is bad at 2; the Hilbert symbol and the metaplectic (Kubota) cocycle are wild at 2. All of this is phase data, hence ghost-blind.
pitfalls: The even prime is 2, not √2; √2 appears only through the character (2/p) = χ₈(p).
√2 is not a prime (TAA Lemma 150, correction 1); √2 enters via χ₈ and, separately, via Goldfeld's √2 (prime squares).

rels.note: wild at 2: Hilbert symbol / Kubota cocycle

concepts.name: Scattering unitarity |φ| = 1
concepts.plain: The cusp scattering coefficient has modulus one on the critical line — true with or without RH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: |φ(½ + it)| = 1 follows from the functional equation; it is Ax3 (adjoint) only and ghost-blind.
pitfalls: Not Rosati: only the ππ† = q half.

concepts.name: De Bruijn–Newman flow at one prime = the F/V sweep at fixed determinant: a_eff(t) = a e^{−t log²p}
concepts.plain: Running the heat flow on a single Euler factor changes only its trace, which shrinks or grows exponentially, while the product of the two Frobenius roots stays p. So the flow slides the pair along the F/V sweep.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: De Bruijn–Newman flow at one prime = the F/V sweep at fixed determinant: a_eff(t) = a e^{−t log²p}
concepts.formula: P_p(½+iz) = e^{−iz log p}(2cos(z log p) − a/√p); H_t = 2e^{t log²p}cos(z log p) − a/√p
numbers: forward: z → π/(2 log p), F,V → ±i√p (k = 2 point)
inversion: flowed 1/P_p diverges for t > 0 (weight 2·10^275 at k = 70, t = 0.05)

concepts.name: Four squares as the quaternion lift of ζ: Σ r₄(n) n^{−s} = 8(1 − 4^{1−s}) ζ(s) ζ(s−1); r₄(p)/8 = p + 1 ⇒ normalized t = (p+1)/√p = 2cosh(½ log p) — ζ's hyperbolic (boost) frames are the trivial/Eisenstein part; cusp parts appear only for other definite quaternion lattices (B ramified at 11, ∞: θ_O = E + (8/5) f₁₁ₐ₁)
aliases: Eisenstein vs cusp in theta series
concepts.plain: Counting the ways to write n as four squares gives exactly ζ(s)ζ(s−1), so ζ's per-prime frames are the 'trivial' part of the quaternion picture. Genuine wave-like (cusp) pieces only show up for other quaternion lattices, for example one tied to the curve 11a1.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] Jacobi r₄(n) = 8Σ_{d|n,4∤d} d (n ≤ 3000 exact); Dirichlet identity coefficientwise (n ≤ 3000) and numerically at s = 4, 5, 6.5 (1e−11). θ⁴ ∈ M₂(Γ₀(4)), all Eisenstein. Hurwitz order: #norm n = 24σ(n), n odd. B = (−1,−11)_ℚ (ramified at 11, ∞), maximal order O = ℤ⟨1, i, (1+j)/2, i(1+j)/2⟩, norm form Q ⊕ Q with Q = x² + xy + 3y²; θ_O = 1 + (12/5)Σ(σ(n) − 11σ(n/11))qⁿ + (8/5) η(z)²η(11z)² (n ≤ 300, exact). [C] Eichler 1954 Arch. Math. 5 355–366 (Brandt/basis problem; bibliographic). [A] 'definite energy' (TAA Lemma 161) ↔ definite quaternion algebra (compact quotient).
pitfalls: Four squares has NO cusp part (dim S₂(Γ₀(4)) = 0).
ζ sits on the Eisenstein (non-compact, boost) side; the quaternion lift does not place ζ's zeros in a compact setting.

rels.note: ζ(s)ζ(s−1) frames at φ = ½ log p

concepts.name: Fundamental domain of SL₂(ℤ): elliptic (CM points), parabolic (cusp), hyperbolic (closed geodesics)
concepts.plain: The modular surface has two cone points, one cusp and many closed geodesics: the three kinds of motion seen on the quotient.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Elliptic points i (stabilizer ⟨S⟩) and ρ = e^{2πi/3} (⟨ST⟩) = CM points of discriminant −4, −3; one cusp (0 = S·∞ ~ i∞ for SL₂(ℤ); for Γ₀(N) the cusps 0 and ∞ are distinct, swapped by the Fricke involution); hyperbolic classes ↔ closed geodesics of length 2 log ε (Selberg's primes). Interior: Δ ≥ 0 (selberg_eigenvalue_mass_shell); cusp: unitary scattering φ (eisenstein_resonances_rho_half); CM points: Epstein/Hecke (epstein). The cusp ties them: its constant term carries ζ.

rels.note: cusp is a point, not the place ∞

concepts.name: Half representations of SL(2,F_p): p+4 irreps of dims 1, p, p+1 ((p−3)/2 of them), p−1 ((p−1)/2), and two each of dims (p+1)/2 and (p−1)/2 — the induced rep from the quadratic (Legendre) character splits in half, with unipotent character values (1 ± √(εp))/2 and (−1 ± √(εp))/2, ε = (−1/p) (quadratic Gauss sum); needs F_p a field — the precise place where (p ± 1)/2 separates primes from odd composites
concepts.plain: Over the field with p elements, SL(2) has exactly two pairs of 'half-size' representations, of dimensions (p+1)/2 and (p−1)/2, and their characters carry the square-root Gauss sum. This needs p to be prime. For hydrogen, (n ± 1)/2 appears for every n, so it does not single out primes.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [N] p = 3, 5, 7, 11, 13: Σ dim² = p(p²−1); the unipotent class sum on Ind_B^G(Legendre) has eigenvalues giving χ(u) = (1 ± √(εp))/2 with multiplicity (p+1)/2 each; second orthogonality Σ|χ(u)|² = 2p. [C] Fulton–Harris §5.2 (table via Braun–Nebe, from Dornhoff Thm 38.1: ξ₁,₂(c) = ½(1 ± √(εq)), η₁,₂(c) = ½(−1 ± √(εq))). For composite n, SL(2,ℤ/n) = Π SL(2,ℤ/p^k) (CRT): reps are tensor products, no new n-halves. [T] Hydrogen (j,j), j = (n−1)/2, Casimir ((n−1)/2)((n+1)/2) for every n; odd n ⇔ integer j (parity, cf. hilbert_reciprocity_at_2). L is not 'the prime', A′ not ±1 (vectors, |j₊| = |j₋|). [H] per-prime, phase data ⇒ ghost-blind (DH shares the local quadratic characters).
pitfalls: The (p+1)/2 reps are halves of a principal series, not cuspidal; the (p−1)/2 are halves of the discrete series.
Ghost-blind: local quadratic data.

concepts.name: Yoshida window positivity
concepts.plain: For test functions supported in a small enough window, Weil positivity holds unconditionally.
concepts.label: Cited
concepts.core: Yoshida: W ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ small window; TAA Lemma 10 window ≤ log 3. Below ghost onsets, so ghost-blind. TAA Lemma 153: CC21 credit Yoshida (ASPM 21, 1992, 281–325) with W∞(f) ≥ 0 for supp f ⊂ (1/2,2), f̂(±i/2) = 0, i.e. |log x| < log 2 (before the prime 2).
pitfalls: Unconditional windows never reach ghost onset.
Atlas window ≤ log 3 (TAA Lemma 10) vs CC21/Yoshida (1/2, 2) ↔ log 2: different statements/normalizations, not reconciled here.

concepts.name: Counts vs quadratic positivity
concepts.plain: Point counts being positive does not force RH; only quadratic forms can.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 109: 2935 count-positive ghosts (g = 2, q = 11).
numbers: TAA Lemma 166: exact census (|a| ≤ 6q, |b| ≤ 20q, d ≤ 40): 675 (q = 7), 2935 (q = 11, reproduces TAA Lemma 109), 4961 (q = 13); on-circle 205/401/513

concepts.name: Λ = 0 exactly for every finite product of ≥ 2 strictly Hasse degree-2 factors at distinct primes; (a) infinitely many non-real zeros for all t < 0 (Kronecker close pairs + local Rouché on F + sF″; Bohr + Hurwitz), (b) real-rooted for t ≥ 0 (Pólya 1927, Laguerre–Pólya class)
concepts.plain: Zeros from different primes come arbitrarily close because the logarithms of primes are rationally independent, which is unique factorisation. Running the flow backward makes every such pair collide, so the product sits exactly at threshold 0, whatever the a_p are. This is a statement on the local unitarity line, not GRH.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: Λ = 0 exactly for every finite product of ≥ 2 strictly Hasse degree-2 factors at distinct primes; (a) infinitely many non-real zeros for all t < 0 (Kronecker close pairs + local Rouché on F + sF″; Bohr + Hurwitz), (b) real-rooted for t ≥ 0 (Pólya 1927, Laguerre–Pólya class)

concepts.uncertain: No exact reference found; the method is close to Csordas–Smith–Varga and Dobner (possibly folklore). Hasse-level, not GRH.

concepts.name: Kustaanheimo–Stiefel quaternion lift: x = q i q̄ (Hopf map S³ → S², |x| = |q|²) with the bilinear U(1) constraint turns 3D Kepler at energy E into the 4D isotropic oscillator with ω² = −E/2; E < 0 real ω (rotation), E > 0 inverted oscillator (boost) — the Wick rotation; the commutant of the constraint in u(4) is u(2)⊕u(2) ⊃ su(2)⊕su(2) = so(4)
concepts.plain: Squaring a quaternion turns the Kepler problem in 3D into a perfectly round oscillator in 4D. Bound orbits become ordinary oscillations and unbound ones become an upside-down oscillator, which is the same switch as a Wick rotation.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: [T] KS (J. reine angew. Math. 218 (1965) 204–219): x = q i q̄, fibre q ↦ q e^{iα}; dx kills the fibre, and on the horizontal space (⟨q i, q′⟩ = 0) dx = 2|q| × isometry (5e−10). With ds = dt/r: q″ = −ω²q, ω² = −E/2, |q′|² + ω²|q|² = μ/2 (coupling-constant metamorphosis; ΔE 1e−10, Kepler ẍ = −μx/r³ to 4e−7). E > 0: inverted oscillator → hyperbola (2e−6). 2D case = Levi-Civita/Bohlin z ↦ z² (TAA Lemma 161): e_K = e_H²/(2 − e_H²). u(4) (16 generators) ∩ commutant of the constraint = 8-dim u(2)⊕u(2), derived algebra 6 = su(2)⊕su(2) ≅ so(4) (bound Kepler); the two u(1) = constraint and oscillator H. [A] J. W. McGreevy. Ghost-blind (archimedean).
pitfalls: The 4D oscillator symmetry is U(4); only the su(2)⊕su(2) commuting with the constraint descends to Kepler.
Spelling: Kustaanheimo–Stiefel.

rels.note: ω → iω is cos θ → cosh φ

concepts.name: Legendre ↔ Fourier: stationary phase, half-density amplitude, Maslov phase
concepts.plain: The Fourier transform of a wave is, to leading order, its Legendre transform in the phase, a half-density in the amplitude, and a quarter-turn sign for each concave direction.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: ∫e^{i(S(x)−px)}dx ≈ √(2π)|S″(x_p)|^{−½} e^{−iS*(p)} e^{iπ sgn S″/4}, S′(x_p) = p, S*(p) = p x_p − S(x_p) (critical-value Legendre transform); exact for quadratic S (Fresnel). Tangent of slope p meets the y-axis at S − xS′ = −S*(p): the intercepts give the phase; the half-density |dx|^{½} → |dp|^{½} gives the amplitude |S″|^{−½}; the Maslov factor records the Hessian signature and jumps at caustics (S″ = 0), where stationary phase fails (Airy; TAA Lemma 153 NUM). TAA Lemma 153 NUM: rel. err 0.012 (λ=20), 0.003 (λ=80), both signs. e^{−iπ/4} = √(1/i) is the factor in ϑ(−1/τ) = √(τ/i)ϑ(τ) (TAA Lemma 151; 9e−17). Riemann–Siegel θ(t) = (t/2)log(t/2π) − t/2 − π/8 + 1/(48t) + … (NUM); −π/8 as a Maslov-type phase is Heuristic.
pitfalls: Intercepts give the phase, not the half-density; the amplitude comes from the curvature S″ (TAA Lemma 153, correction 15).
Hörmander / Guillemin–Sternberg: bibliographic data only (unopened).

concepts.name: One cusp, three readings: orbifold, Tate curve, archimedean monodromy
concepts.plain: Closing the cone angle 2π/m of the triangle orbifolds S²(2,3,m) runs from the Platonic solids (m = 3,4,5, Euler characteristic 2/|G|) through the flat case m = 6 to the modular orbifold at m = ∞, whose cusp is a pseudosphere horn of area 2π with unipotent holonomy T = 1+N, N² = 0. Arithmetically the cusp of X(1) is the Tate-curve degeneration (multiplicative reduction, nonzero N). At good primes Frobenius is semisimple and elliptic of trace a_p/√p; the inert value a_p = 0 is the order-2 point i, and the Hasse edge is a scalar, not a unipotent element. At the archimedean place an operator N playing the role of the logarithm of monodromy exists for local factors (Consani). On the modular surface the Riemann zeros appear as scattering resonances at Re s = 1/4, outside self-adjoint control. A polarized (N, log-Frobenius) package on a global cohomology would give Weil positivity; this is conjectural and RH is not proved.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Split/inert duality for a CM curve (32a1)
concepts.plain: For y² = x³ − x one character, χ₄(p), decides both properties. Split primes have i ∈ Q_p, are ordinary, and have the angle of a Gaussian prime, equidistributed for the uniform measure (Hecke), not Sato–Tate. Inert primes have i ∉ Q_p, are supersingular (Deuring), and have a_p = 0 and angle exactly 90°; there Frobenius satisfies π² = −p and anticommutes with complex multiplication, so π/√p is a 90° rotation. The two classes are the fibres of the Galois character of Q(i), a duality rather than an isomorphism. The same holds for every CM curve, and RH for their L-functions is open.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Johnson–Lippmann operator: a spin-dependent Laplace–Runge–Lenz operator commuting with the Dirac–Coulomb Hamiltonian
concepts.plain: For the relativistic hydrogen atom there is a first-order operator, built from spin and the Coulomb direction, that commutes with the energy and anticommutes with Dirac's K. It plays the role of a supercharge: the hidden symmetry made one level more fundamental. Analogy only for RH.

concepts.name: Kaluza–Klein circles, the infinite torus, and adelic solenoids
concepts.plain: A Kaluza–Klein circle gives a complex structure on its charged modes only. The pseudosphere is a warped circle of radius e^{−u}, and only the neutral (constant-term) mode reaches the cusp, where the scattering coefficient Λ(2s−1)/Λ(2s) carries ζ. The per-prime phases p^{−it} fill the infinite torus ∏S¹, the dual of the multiplicative group of positive rationals. That torus differs from the solenoid 𝔸/ℚ, which is the dual of the additive rationals; the p-adic solenoid is the inverse limit of S¹ under z ↦ z^p. The product formula makes ℚ^× preserve Haar measure, so the compatible structure is an invariant measure, not an invariant metric. The expected dynamical system for Spec ℤ (three-dimensional, orbits of length log p) has not been constructed.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: The 1/24 identities (1/24 = −ζ(−1)/2, η²⁴ = Δ, Θ_Leech) and the verdict: in Weil’s form the 1/24 acts only through the weight
concepts.plain: The 1/24 is real and global: 1/24 = −ζ(−1)/2, the exponent of q in η, and η²⁴ = Δ, of weight 12 = 24·½. It is ζ(2), an absolutely convergent Euler product, carried to s = −1 by the functional equation. But in the window model of Weil’s form the 1/24 enters only through the Γ-factor (the weight). Lowering the weight below 12 breaks positivity almost at once (a one-sided edge), but that edge is generic: 11a1, with weight 2 and no 1/24 in this sense, sits on the same kind of edge, even tighter. For ζ the 1/12 = B₂/2 enters only through Stirling’s 1/(12z) term, which is the same for every Γ-factor and identical for Davenport–Heilbronn, so it cannot tell a true zero from a planted ghost. Verdict: the 1/24 does not supply the positive metric on the primitive part.
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The 1/24 identities (1/24 = −ζ(−1)/2, η²⁴ = Δ, Θ_Leech) and the verdict: in Weil’s form the 1/24 acts only through the weight. From the TAA research notes of 29 Oct 2026 (window model of TAA Lemma 182; not yet in a lemma).

concepts.name: Weight ladder (modular weights)
concepts.plain: Modular forms come in weights; at each rung the Eisenstein series E_k is the reference. A “stratification” of modular structures is this ladder.

concepts.name: CM case: the Hasse triangle is Fermat's two-squares triangle
concepts.plain: For y² = x³ − x (CM by Z[i]) the Hasse triangle at p ≡ 1 mod 4 has integer legs 2a, 2b with a² + b² = p, and its angle is the argument of a Gaussian prime; at p ≡ 3 mod 4, a_p = 0 and α_p/√p = ±i. All Frobenius elements lie in one field Q(i), so a coherent family of local i's exists, yet RH for this L-function is open: local coherence is not the missing piece.

concepts.name: The critical-line wave: Hardy Z and the Riemann–Siegel phase
concepts.plain: On the critical line ζ(1/2+it) = Z(t)e^{−iθ(t)} with Z real, so the real and imaginary parts are one real wave seen through a rotating phase. Each simple zero is a sign change of Z, so the phase of ζ jumps by π. The mean of Re ζ on the line is 1; Gram's law is the separate statement (−1)^n Z(g_n) > 0 at Gram points, and it fails first at n = 126. Sign changes equal N(T) for all T iff RH holds and all zeros are simple. Under RH, (Z′/Z)′ = −Σ(t−γ)^{−2} − (log G)″, which forbids wrong-sign extrema wherever the sum dominates (checked for 5.7 ≤ t ≤ 400).
concepts.label: Theorem
concepts.core: The critical-line wave: Hardy Z and the Riemann–Siegel phase

concepts.name: Weil operator, star and the eighth turn
concepts.plain: On weight-one H^1, C = i^(p-q) is a complex structure, star = C composed with conjugation is antilinear with square -1 and commutes with C, so the quaternion triple is (i, star, i star), not (C, star, C star). The Deligne-torus element h(e^{i pi/4}) is a real square root of C (eighth turn) adding no new structure.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.core: [T] ∂_z log(√y|η(z)|²) = (πi/12)·E₂*(z), E₂* = E₂ − 3/(πy) (from (1/2πi) d log Δ = E₂, Zagier Prop. 7, and ∂_z ½ log y = −i/(4y)). Kronecker's first limit formula: E(z,s) = Σ′ y^s/|mz+n|^{2s} = π/(s−1) + 2π(γ − log 2 − log(√y|η|²)) + O(s−1). Constant term 2ζ(2s)[y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s}], φ = ξ(2s−1)/ξ(2s) (TAA Lemma 153 Birman–Krein). concepts.name: Beta integral, Maslov dequantization and entropy
concepts.plain: As hbar -> 0, hbar log B(a/hbar, b/hbar) tends to -(a+b) times the Shannon entropy of the split a:b, with an O(hbar log hbar) correction from Stirling. The integral collapses onto the saddle x* = a/(a+b) of a log x + b log(1-x), a max-plus problem, and the Beta(a/hbar, b/hbar) law satisfies a large-deviation principle with rate (a+b) KL(x*||x). With four points fixed, the Koba-Nielsen integral is the Beta function (Veneziano), and its high-energy fixed-angle limit is the same saddle. The Sato-Tate law is Beta(3/2,3/2), with constant pi/8 = Gamma(3/2)^2/Gamma(3). The CM split-prime law is Beta(1/2,1/2), with constant pi. This concerns the Gamma factors and the a_p distributions, not the zeros.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: The χ = −1 "effective pole" is half of ζ’s pole, entering through ζ_ℚ(i) = ζ·L(χ₄)
concepts.plain: Split the prime atoms by the character χ₄. The atoms with χ₄ = −1 equal one half of (odd-n ζ prime part − χ₄ prime part), an exact identity. They carry half of ψ(x)’s main term, i.e. half the pole, while the χ₄ part has no main term. On windows the cancellation is only approximate, because it comes from a main term (the prime number theorem in progressions), not from a symmetry.

concepts.name: The Galois deformation obstruction is a second-order curvature
concepts.plain: Deforming a flat connection by εu gives curvature ε·du + (ε²/2)[u∧u]; staying flat to second order needs the cup-bracket [u∪u] to vanish in H². For Galois representations this is the obstruction class in H²(G_Q,S, ad ρ) of Mazur's deformation theory, and for Kähler groups Goldman–Millson show the deformation space is the quadratic cone it cuts out. For modular representations the relevant obstructions vanish, so the Galois side stays flat: it cannot carry a curvature with a sign.
concepts.label: Theorem

concepts.name: Sector map w = e^{iπs/2}
concepts.plain: Mapping the critical strip to a 90° sector puts the critical line on the 45° ray; the functional equation becomes w ↦ i/w.

Poisson summation for the Gaussian gives the theta inversion, and its Mellin transform gives xi(s) = xi(1-s). This explains the symmetry s <-> 1-s, not the critical line. The archimedean term alone is positive only for support below 0.2143; with the pole (or on the pole-free space) the threshold is 0.7432.

concepts.name: Ruled quadric through a saddle: null lines, signature (1,1)

Its lines are null (zero proper time); proper time lives on the two-sheet hyperboloid. The mutual moment of two lines is symmetric, of constant sign within a ruling and zero across rulings, so no assignment of primes to lines reproduces Legendre symbols, which are antisymmetric on primes ≡ 3 mod 4.

concepts.name: Purity as distortionless transmission: weight strata = attenuation classes
concepts.plain: On a perfect cable every frequency fades at the same rate; RH-type purity says every Frobenius eigenvalue has the same size, and rescaling by √q makes the fading disappear altogether.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Lossless = unitary (|φ| = 1 on the line; after the half-density gauge no attenuation) [T]. Distortionless = every mode shares one attenuation rate [T for the line]. Frobenius eigenvalues |α| = q^{w/2}: α^n decays/grows at rate (w/2) log q, so the weight strata (rings |z| = q^{−σ}) are attenuation classes; purity (one ring) = distortionless [Restatement for Frobenius]; dividing by q^{1/2} (half Tate twist, the e^{−αx} factor) turns distortionless into lossless [T]. For ζ (no Frobenius) this is an Analogy. DH off-line zeros = modes with another attenuation = distortion [R, TAA Lemma 144 overdamped ghost]. Hyperbolic side: characteristics x ± ct are the null lines of dx² − c²dt²; Wick rotation t → iτ makes it dx² + c²dτ² (OS link) — a different sign flip from C → −C in the LC energy (TAA Lemma 153, correction 30). Elliptical conic sections, not elliptic curves. TAA Lemma 154: on the cusp purity = every zero has HWHM pair (¼, ¼), i.e. one lifetime [R]; DH ghost 1 measured (0.0957, 0.4042). On observer lines the FE pairs widths ±Γ (PT gain/loss shape, Analogy).

concepts.name: Hasse triangle and Newton's dT/dθ = L²
concepts.plain: Write a_p = 2√p cos θ_p. The triangle with legs a_p and √(4p − a_p²) and hypotenuse 2√p exists exactly when the Hasse bound holds. In Newton's geometric calculus (T = tan θ) the derivative is dT/dθ = L² = 4p/a_p². This restates the bound; it does not determine θ_p, which is Sato–Tate distributed for non-CM curves. The blow-up at a_p = 0 is a chart singularity of tan, but the locus a_p = 0 (α_p = i√p, supersingular) is arithmetic.
concepts.label: Restatement

concepts.name: One log-gas and its frozen limit
concepts.plain: Under the de Bruijn-Newman backward heat flow, the zeros of H_t move by dz_k/dt = 2 sum_{j != k} 1/(z_k - z_j), the gradient flow of a logarithmic (Coulomb) energy. An off-line pair collides onto the real axis in finite time. RH is equivalent to Lambda = 0, i.e. every charge already on the axis at t = 0. The Hopf-Cole transform turns the heat equation into Hamilton-Jacobi in the hbar -> 0 limit, with a min-plus (Hopf-Lax) solution. Koba-Nielsen weights are 2D Coulomb-gas Boltzmann weights, and the Stieltjes equilibrium of charges in a Gaussian field sits at Hermite zeros, which the beta-Hermite ensemble freezes onto as beta grows. GUE pair correlation of zeros (conjectural) is the beta = 2 log-gas. The picture explains symmetry and statistics; it gives no positivity.
concepts.label: Analogy

concepts.name: Laplace–Runge–Lenz vector: |A| = mk·e, so bound (definite, E < 0) ⇔ |A| < mk; hidden symmetry SO(4) (E < 0, compact, discrete spectrum) / E(3) (E = 0) / SO(1,3) (E > 0) = elliptic / parabolic / hyperbolic; tangential periapsis impulse stretches A (changes the margin), radial impulse rotates A (precession, spectrum-blind)
concepts.plain: The Runge–Lenz vector points from the Sun to the periapsis and its length is the eccentricity. Bound orbits have it shorter than its maximum, and that is when the hidden symmetry is the compact rotation group of a four-dimensional sphere. A push along the orbit lengthens it; a push along it only turns it, which is precession.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: [T] A = p × L − mk r̂ points focus → periapsis, |A|² = m²k² + 2mE|L|²; at periapsis gravity is anti-parallel to A, v ⊥ A. dA/dt = f × L + p × (r × f) for an extra force f (checked 6e−10). m = k = 1, r = (1,0), p = (0,1.2): A = (0.44,0), |A|² = 0.1936; Δp = 0.01 tangential: ΔA = (0.0241, 0) (stretch); radial: ΔA = (0, −0.012) (rotation; |A| changes at 2nd order). Linear model: rotation-conjugation of g_t = precession (trace, F, V, e unchanged); squeeze-conjugation changes e, not F, V; changing t = kick (changes the spectrum). [C] Pauli 1926 (Z. Phys. 36, 336–363), Fock 1935 (Z. Phys. 98, 145–154; momentum space → S³), Bargmann 1936 (Z. Phys. 99, 576–582); Bander–Itzykson 1966 (RMP 38, 330; 346): O(4) bound, O(1,3) scattering, E(3) at E = 0 (preprint). [A] definite ⇔ compact symmetry ⇔ unitary finite-dim reps ⇔ discrete spectrum ↔ TAA thesis 'RH is unitarity'; spherical/flat/hyperbolic matches the (2,3,n) split. [O] what compact group plays SO(4) for ζ (Katz–Sarnak 1999 symmetry types are statistical, not this). TAA Lemma 162: KS makes SO(4) manifest (commutant su(2)⊕su(2) of the U(1) constraint in u(4)); Pauli Casimir sign = real form; Moser orbit space S²×S²; in exact Kepler A never precesses (correction).
pitfalls: At periapsis the force is radial, not tangential (TAA Lemma 161, correction 11).
SO(4) ↔ RH is Analogy only.

concepts.name: SU(2)×SU(2) as a compact 'product surface': SO(4) = (SU(2)×SU(2))/±1 acts on S³ = SU(2) by x ↦ g x h⁻¹, stabilizer of 1 = diagonal (conjugation, preserves trace = F+V); Peter–Weyl L²(G) = ⊕ V_π ⊗ V_π* is the compact analogue of Künneth; dictionary to Weil's C×C (Δ ↔ diagonal, Γ_F ↔ translate, Lefschetz ↔ trace, Hodge index ↔ Haar positivity, automatic for compact G)
concepts.plain: The four-dimensional rotation group is two copies of SU(2), one acting from the left and one from the right, so the 3-sphere behaves like a 'product' with a diagonal. That mirrors the curve-times-curve surface Weil used, and on a compact group the positivity Weil needed comes for free. The catch is that ζ's own frames are boosts, not rotations.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: [T] (g,h) ↦ L_g R_{h⁻¹} ∈ SO(4), kernel ±(1,1), so(4) = su(2)_L ⊕ su(2)_R; diagonal conjugation preserves Re x = cos θ (latitude = Sato–Tate class). Peter–Weyl: characters U_n orthonormal for Sato–Tate (6e−15); matrix coefficients (MC 1.4e−3). Weil side: Gram of {pt×E, E×pt, Δ, Γ_F} on E×E (11a1) has one positive eigenvalue, det = a² − 4p (Hodge index ⇔ |a| ≤ 2√p ⇔ m² − a mn + p n² ≥ 0, the TAA Lemma 152 norm conic); fake a = 8 at p = 13 gives two positive eigenvalues. #E(F_p) = p + 1 − a_p (Lefschetz). [A] 'SU2 x SU2 … surface on SpecZ x SpecZ': compactness gives definiteness for free, but SU(2) is the group of an elliptic curve's frames; ζ's frames are boosts. [O] a compact G×G whose diagonal sees ζ's zeros. [C] Connes–Consani, The Arithmetic Site (C. R. 352 (2014) 971–975): Frobenius correspondences realized in the square of the arithmetic site.
pitfalls: Analogy only: no compact G×G is known whose diagonal sees ζ's zeros (Open).
Never name the missing cohomology: it is Deninger's conjectured cohomology (MP0–MP4).

concepts.name: Higgs mechanism: negative mass² at the symmetric point
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: V = −μ²|φ|² + λ|φ|⁴: mass² = −μ² < 0 at φ = 0 (tachyonic); vacuum |φ|² = μ²/2λ, ⟨φ⟩ = v/√2, v = μ/√λ ≈ 246 GeV; m_H² = 2μ² > 0; Yukawa m_f = y v/√2 (√2 a convention). Positivity by CHOICE of vacuum — RH cannot choose (zeros are given). Mass is not friction (no dissipation, Lorentz invariant; TAA Lemma 150, correction 14). Honest link to GRR/relative counts: main term + oscillation ↔ vev + fluctuation only.
pitfalls: The cusp two-Lorentzian “doublet” (TAA Lemma 153 Thm 7.7, TAA Lemma 154) is a parity doublet, not the Higgs complex doublet: no continuous group, no vev, no eaten modes (TAA Lemma 154, correction 13).

concepts.name: Anomalous dispersion
concepts.plain: Phase behavior near a line; ghost-blind.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 36: anomalous dispersion = analogy — gain lines are where absorption and phase disagree; THM 4.3 absorption–phase sum rule ∫₀ᵀ Re ξ′/ξ(σ₀+it)dt = π[N(T) − 2N(σ₀,T)] + …, deficit 2πN(σ₀,T) ≥ 0 (leads to zero density, not a proof). TAA Lemma 78: causality versus linewidth, Kramers–Kronig for the modular scattering matrix. TAA Lemma 146: dRe χ/dω at centre −6 (absorber) vs +6 (gain). TAA Lemma 154: precise form — per line Im F = −sgn(σ−β) H[Re F]; KK holds on σ iff no zero lies right of σ; a ghost flips the pairing locally (DH residual 9–20 at d = 0.25…0.05, = predicted term to 1e−4; ζ ≤ 1e−4). Re F = group delay d arg ξ/dt, Im F = −d log|ξ|/dt. Convention-free content: relative sign κ = −1/a³ (absorber < 0, gain > 0). J. W. McGreevy's strip prototype (TAA Lemma 36) = this object [R]; 'anomalous' in the optical sense [A].

concepts.name: The missing square Spec ℤ × Spec ℤ as the object (collapse ℤ⊗ℤ = ℤ; defect requirements R1–R5)
concepts.plain: Over ℤ the product of Spec ℤ with itself collapses onto its diagonal, so the surface Weil used does not exist. Treating that absence as the object needs a defect invariant with a sign, built from the primes, that fails for fake zeta functions.
concepts.label: Open
concepts.core: [T] ℤ⊗_ℤℤ = ℤ, so Spec ℤ ×_{Spec ℤ} Spec ℤ = Spec ℤ and the diagonal is an isomorphism: no off-diagonal room for a Frobenius graph, no NS(C×C), no Castelnuovo sign. Over 𝔽_q: C ×_{𝔽_q} C is a surface, Γ_F·Δ = #C(𝔽_q), Hodge index ⇒ |α| = √q (Weil). ℤ is initial among rings, so any deeper base must leave rings (Borger, opened). [T] Any invariant that depends only on the collapse is an invariant of ℤ alone, hence the same for ζ, L(s,χ) and DH: ghost-blind. [O] J. W. McGreevy's reading made mathematics: a defect invariant δ with (R1) built from Euler-product data (primes/multiplicativity), (R2) ghost-sensitive (fails or changes sign for DH), (R3) a sign whose validity ⇒ RH, (R4) reducing over 𝔽_q to the Castelnuovo defect def(D) = 2d₁d₂ − D² ≥ 0, (R5) not defined through the zeros. 'Topological barrier' = Analogy until δ exists. Deninger's conjectured cohomology (MP0–MP4) is the hole stated on H¹ (Restatement). TAA Lemma 162: SU(2)×SU(2) on S³ and Moser's S²×S² are compact product models with automatic definiteness, but they carry elliptic-curve (rotation) frames; ζ's frames are boosts (Analogy; Open).
pitfalls: The collapse is a property of ℤ only: it cannot by itself tell ζ from DH.
'Topological barrier' has no invariant yet: Analogy, not Theorem.

concepts.name: Lamb cutoff
concepts.plain: In a stratified fluid, waves below the Lamb cutoff frequency c/2H cannot propagate; on the modular surface the cusp’s −¼ is exactly this cutoff with scale height H = 1.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: TAA Lemma 146 §7: with dy/y² = e^{−r}dr, the cusp −¼ equals the Lamb cutoff c/2H with H = 1 (exact operator identity); TAA Lemma 141 §6: the cusp is a Webster horn A = e^{−r}, Liouville factor e^{r/2}, and +¼ cancels the horn cutoff. Same −¼ as y²∂²(y^½W) = y^½(W″ − W/4) (TAA Lemma 145).
pitfalls: Lamb’s original source not opened (TAA Lemma 146 refs); the identity is checked as an operator identity.

concepts.name: Two different χ’s: Euler characteristic vs class-group character
concepts.plain: The χ of the Connes–Consani Riemann–Roch on the square is an Euler characteristic of a divisor; the χ¹¹ / ω⁻¹¹ of the 691 story is a Galois character labelling an eigenspace. Different objects; any link is an analogy.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Euler characteristic χ(D) = dim H⁰ − dim H¹ (TAA Lemma 145/TAA Lemma 147, a number for each divisor) vs Teichmüller / cyclotomic character ω, χ_cyc (TAA Lemma 66, labels of eigenspaces of Cl(ℚ(μ₆₉₁)) and of ρ_Δ mod 691). Shared shape only: Mazur–Wiles equates an algebraic size with an L-value, as RR equates χ with degree + constant. Neither sees the sign of D² (Iwasawa: sizes; CC RR: linear χ).
concepts.uncertain: The analogy itself is interpretive; no TAA lemma relates the two.
pitfalls: Do not identify them: notation clash only.
Iwasawa measures sizes, never the sign of D².

concepts.name: Sha as a locally trivial, globally nontrivial defect
concepts.plain: Elements of the Tate–Shafarevich group are torsors trivial at every place but not globally; in the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula |Sha| sits next to the regulator, the Gram determinant of the Néron–Tate metric. Read as the arithmetic analogue of a holonomy defect on a locally flat space.

concepts.name: Ramanujan's 691 as a degeneration of the pole line
concepts.plain: tau(n) = sigma_11(n) mod 691 follows from Ramanujan's identity 691 + 65520 sum sigma_11(n) x^n = 441 Q^3 + 250 R^2, since 691 divides the numerator of B_12 and zeta(-11) = 691/32760. Over the complex numbers the Eisenstein (pole) line is orthogonal to the cusp forms; mod 691 its constant term, half of zeta(-11), vanishes and the Eisenstein line collides with the cuspidal line (Mazur's Eisenstein line meeting Spec T). So 691 is where the null-line quotient breaks down integrally, not an instance of it. An exploratory test found no irregular-prime signature in the real Weil-form model, as expected: primes enter only through smooth weights log p / p^(k/2). In the p-adic Stickelberger form on (Z/p)^x the pole is the unique eigenvalue of valuation -1, and the radical mod p sits exactly at the k with p | B_k (checked for 182 primes 5..1097, 66 irregular). At 691 the k = 12 radical line is the weight-12 Eisenstein constant term up to a unit; a second line sits at k = 200. What degenerates is a weight-k Eisenstein line in the p-adic family, not the pole of zeta; positivity has no p-adic analogue, only non-degeneracy.
concepts.label: Analogy
concepts.core: Ramanujan's 691 as a degeneration of the pole line

concepts.name: Candidate formulations of Castelnuovo-Severi over the integers
concepts.plain: Ranked candidates: Hodge index on the span of translates (a restatement of RH), a fibre-null completion of the pole channel, a quadratic Riemann-Roch on the square of the scaling site with the scaling correspondences as graphs, a positive involution on a first cohomology, and a q -> 1 finite-genus approximation. Obstructions: the product of Spec Z with itself collapses, fixed rank forces linear growth, counts do not induce the sign, and the functional equation is blind to off-line zeros.
